```sql
-- Dialect: SQL Server / T-SQL
-- Purpose: Create the normalized ERP source tables.
-- Run in: SSMS query window connected to NorthstarRetail_ERP.
-- Idempotency: each table and index is created only when missing.

USE NorthstarRetail_ERP;
GO

IF OBJECT_ID(N'erp.product_categories', N'U') IS NULL
BEGIN
    CREATE TABLE erp.product_categories
    (
        category_id         INT NOT NULL CONSTRAINT PK_product_categories PRIMARY KEY,
        category_name       NVARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
        parent_category_id  INT NULL,
        created_at          DATETIME2(3) NOT NULL,
        updated_at          DATETIME2(3) NOT NULL,
        CONSTRAINT FK_product_categories_parent FOREIGN KEY (parent_category_id)
            REFERENCES erp.product_categories(category_id)
    );
END;
GO

IF OBJECT_ID(N'erp.suppliers', N'U') IS NULL
BEGIN
    CREATE TABLE erp.suppliers
    (
        supplier_id         INT NOT NULL CONSTRAINT PK_suppliers PRIMARY KEY,
        supplier_code       VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,
        supplier_name       NVARCHAR(150) NOT NULL,
        country_code        CHAR(2) NOT NULL,
        lead_time_days      INT NOT NULL,
        active_flag         BIT NOT NULL,
        created_at          DATETIME2(3) NOT NULL,
        updated_at          DATETIME2(3) NOT NULL,
        CONSTRAINT UQ_suppliers_supplier_code UNIQUE (supplier_code),
        CONSTRAINT CK_suppliers_lead_time CHECK (lead_time_days >= 0)
    );
END;
GO

IF OBJECT_ID(N'erp.products', N'U') IS NULL
BEGIN
    CREATE TABLE erp.products
    (
        product_id          INT NOT NULL CONSTRAINT PK_products PRIMARY KEY,
        sku                 VARCHAR(30) NOT NULL,
        product_name        NVARCHAR(200) NOT NULL,
        category_id         INT NOT NULL,
        supplier_id         INT NOT NULL,
        brand               NVARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
        unit_cost           DECIMAL(12,2) NOT NULL,
        list_price          DECIMAL(12,2) NOT NULL,
        currency_code       CHAR(3) NOT NULL,
        active_flag         BIT NOT NULL,
        created_at          DATETIME2(3) NOT NULL,
        updated_at          DATETIME2(3) NOT NULL,
        CONSTRAINT UQ_products_sku UNIQUE (sku),
        CONSTRAINT FK_products_category FOREIGN KEY (category_id) REFERENCES erp.product_categories(category_id),
        CONSTRAINT FK_products_supplier FOREIGN KEY (supplier_id) REFERENCES erp.suppliers(supplier_id),
        CONSTRAINT CK_products_amounts CHECK (unit_cost >= 0 AND list_price >= 0)
    );
END;
GO

IF OBJECT_ID(N'erp.stores', N'U') IS NULL
BEGIN
    CREATE TABLE erp.stores
    (
        store_id            INT NOT NULL CONSTRAINT PK_stores PRIMARY KEY,
        store_code          VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,
        store_name          NVARCHAR(150) NOT NULL,
        region              VARCHAR(30) NOT NULL,
        state_code          CHAR(2) NOT NULL,
        city                NVARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
        open_date           DATE NOT NULL,
        active_flag         BIT NOT NULL,
        created_at          DATETIME2(3) NOT NULL,
        updated_at          DATETIME2(3) NOT NULL,
        CONSTRAINT UQ_stores_store_code UNIQUE (store_code)
    );
END;
GO

IF OBJECT_ID(N'erp.employees', N'U') IS NULL
BEGIN
    CREATE TABLE erp.employees
    (
        employee_id         INT NOT NULL CONSTRAINT PK_employees PRIMARY KEY,
        employee_number     VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,
        store_id            INT NULL,
        manager_employee_id INT NULL,
        first_name          NVARCHAR(80) NOT NULL,
        last_name           NVARCHAR(80) NOT NULL,
        job_title           NVARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
        hire_date           DATE NOT NULL,
        active_flag         BIT NOT NULL,
        created_at          DATETIME2(3) NOT NULL,
        updated_at          DATETIME2(3) NOT NULL,
        CONSTRAINT UQ_employees_number UNIQUE (employee_number),
        CONSTRAINT FK_employees_store FOREIGN KEY (store_id) REFERENCES erp.stores(store_id),
        CONSTRAINT FK_employees_manager FOREIGN KEY (manager_employee_id) REFERENCES erp.employees(employee_id)
    );
END;
GO

IF OBJECT_ID(N'erp.customers', N'U') IS NULL
BEGIN
    CREATE TABLE erp.customers
    (
        customer_id         INT NOT NULL CONSTRAINT PK_customers PRIMARY KEY,
        customer_number     VARCHAR(25) NOT NULL,
        first_name          NVARCHAR(80) NOT NULL,
        last_name           NVARCHAR(80) NOT NULL,
        email               NVARCHAR(255) NULL,
        phone               VARCHAR(40) NULL,
        signup_date         DATE NOT NULL,
        loyalty_tier        VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,
        marketing_opt_in    BIT NOT NULL,
        created_at          DATETIME2(3) NOT NULL,
        updated_at          DATETIME2(3) NOT NULL
        -- Deliberately no unique constraint on customer_number in the learning source:
        -- controlled duplicate business keys must reach Silver and be handled there.
    );
END;
GO

IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM sys.indexes WHERE object_id = OBJECT_ID(N'erp.customers') AND name = N'IX_customers_customer_number')
    CREATE INDEX IX_customers_customer_number ON erp.customers(customer_number);
GO

IF OBJECT_ID(N'erp.addresses', N'U') IS NULL
BEGIN
    CREATE TABLE erp.addresses
    (
        address_id          INT NOT NULL CONSTRAINT PK_addresses PRIMARY KEY,
        customer_id         INT NOT NULL,
        address_type        VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,
        line1               NVARCHAR(200) NOT NULL,
        line2               NVARCHAR(200) NULL,
        city                NVARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
        state_code          VARCHAR(10) NOT NULL,
        postal_code         VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,
        country_code        VARCHAR(10) NOT NULL,
        is_default          BIT NOT NULL,
        created_at          DATETIME2(3) NOT NULL,
        updated_at          DATETIME2(3) NOT NULL,
        CONSTRAINT FK_addresses_customer FOREIGN KEY (customer_id) REFERENCES erp.customers(customer_id)
    );
END;
GO

IF OBJECT_ID(N'erp.orders', N'U') IS NULL
BEGIN
    CREATE TABLE erp.orders
    (
        order_id            BIGINT NOT NULL CONSTRAINT PK_orders PRIMARY KEY,
        order_number        VARCHAR(30) NOT NULL,
        customer_id         INT NOT NULL,
        store_id            INT NULL,
        employee_id         INT NULL,
        channel_code        VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,
        order_timestamp     DATETIME2(3) NOT NULL,
        order_status        VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,
        promotion_code      VARCHAR(30) NULL,
        currency_code       CHAR(3) NOT NULL,
        created_at          DATETIME2(3) NOT NULL,
        updated_at          DATETIME2(3) NOT NULL,
        CONSTRAINT UQ_orders_order_number UNIQUE (order_number),
        CONSTRAINT FK_orders_customer FOREIGN KEY (customer_id) REFERENCES erp.customers(customer_id),
        CONSTRAINT FK_orders_store FOREIGN KEY (store_id) REFERENCES erp.stores(store_id),
        CONSTRAINT FK_orders_employee FOREIGN KEY (employee_id) REFERENCES erp.employees(employee_id),
        CONSTRAINT CK_orders_channel CHECK (channel_code IN ('STORE', 'ONLINE'))
    );
END;
GO

IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM sys.indexes WHERE object_id = OBJECT_ID(N'erp.orders') AND name = N'IX_orders_updated_at')
    CREATE INDEX IX_orders_updated_at ON erp.orders(updated_at) INCLUDE (order_id, customer_id, order_timestamp);
GO

IF OBJECT_ID(N'erp.order_items', N'U') IS NULL
BEGIN
    CREATE TABLE erp.order_items
    (
        order_item_id       BIGINT NOT NULL CONSTRAINT PK_order_items PRIMARY KEY,
        order_id            BIGINT NOT NULL,
        line_number         INT NOT NULL,
        product_id          INT NOT NULL,
        quantity            INT NOT NULL,
        unit_price          DECIMAL(12,2) NOT NULL,
        unit_cost           DECIMAL(12,2) NOT NULL,
        discount_amount     DECIMAL(12,2) NOT NULL,
        tax_amount          DECIMAL(12,2) NOT NULL,
        created_at          DATETIME2(3) NOT NULL,
        updated_at          DATETIME2(3) NOT NULL,
        CONSTRAINT UQ_order_items_line UNIQUE (order_id, line_number),
        CONSTRAINT FK_order_items_order FOREIGN KEY (order_id) REFERENCES erp.orders(order_id),
        CONSTRAINT FK_order_items_product FOREIGN KEY (product_id) REFERENCES erp.products(product_id)
        -- No positive-quantity check: controlled impossible quantities are a Silver lesson.
    );
END;
GO

IF OBJECT_ID(N'erp.payments', N'U') IS NULL
BEGIN
    CREATE TABLE erp.payments
    (
        payment_id          BIGINT NOT NULL CONSTRAINT PK_payments PRIMARY KEY,
        order_id            BIGINT NOT NULL,
        payment_timestamp   DATETIME2(3) NOT NULL,
        payment_method      VARCHAR(30) NOT NULL,
        payment_status      VARCHAR(30) NOT NULL,
        amount              DECIMAL(14,2) NOT NULL,
        currency_code       VARCHAR(3) NOT NULL,
        transaction_reference VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL,
        created_at          DATETIME2(3) NOT NULL,
        updated_at          DATETIME2(3) NOT NULL,
        CONSTRAINT UQ_payments_transaction UNIQUE (transaction_reference),
        CONSTRAINT FK_payments_order FOREIGN KEY (order_id) REFERENCES erp.orders(order_id)
    );
END;
GO

IF OBJECT_ID(N'erp.shipments', N'U') IS NULL
BEGIN
    CREATE TABLE erp.shipments
    (
        shipment_id         BIGINT NOT NULL CONSTRAINT PK_shipments PRIMARY KEY,
        order_id            BIGINT NOT NULL,
        carrier             NVARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
        tracking_number     VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
        ship_date           DATE NOT NULL,
        promised_delivery_date DATE NOT NULL,
        actual_delivery_date DATE NULL,
        shipment_status     VARCHAR(30) NOT NULL,
        shipping_cost       DECIMAL(12,2) NOT NULL,
        created_at          DATETIME2(3) NOT NULL,
        updated_at          DATETIME2(3) NOT NULL,
        CONSTRAINT UQ_shipments_tracking UNIQUE (tracking_number),
        CONSTRAINT FK_shipments_order FOREIGN KEY (order_id) REFERENCES erp.orders(order_id)
    );
END;
GO

IF OBJECT_ID(N'erp.inventory_transactions', N'U') IS NULL
BEGIN
    CREATE TABLE erp.inventory_transactions
    (
        inventory_transaction_id BIGINT NOT NULL CONSTRAINT PK_inventory_transactions PRIMARY KEY,
        store_id            INT NOT NULL,
        product_id          INT NOT NULL,
        transaction_timestamp DATETIME2(3) NOT NULL,
        transaction_type    VARCHAR(30) NOT NULL,
        quantity_change     INT NOT NULL,
        reference_type      VARCHAR(30) NULL,
        reference_id        BIGINT NULL,
        created_at          DATETIME2(3) NOT NULL,
        CONSTRAINT FK_inventory_transactions_store FOREIGN KEY (store_id) REFERENCES erp.stores(store_id),
        CONSTRAINT FK_inventory_transactions_product FOREIGN KEY (product_id) REFERENCES erp.products(product_id)
    );
END;
GO

IF OBJECT_ID(N'erp.inventory_snapshots', N'U') IS NULL
BEGIN
    CREATE TABLE erp.inventory_snapshots
    (
        inventory_snapshot_id BIGINT NOT NULL CONSTRAINT PK_inventory_snapshots PRIMARY KEY,
        snapshot_date       DATE NOT NULL,
        store_id            INT NOT NULL,
        product_id          INT NOT NULL,
        quantity_on_hand    INT NOT NULL,
        quantity_reserved   INT NOT NULL,
        reorder_point       INT NOT NULL,
        created_at          DATETIME2(3) NOT NULL,
        CONSTRAINT UQ_inventory_snapshot_grain UNIQUE (snapshot_date, store_id, product_id),
        CONSTRAINT FK_inventory_snapshots_store FOREIGN KEY (store_id) REFERENCES erp.stores(store_id),
        CONSTRAINT FK_inventory_snapshots_product FOREIGN KEY (product_id) REFERENCES erp.products(product_id)
    );
END;
GO

SELECT s.name AS schema_name, t.name AS table_name
FROM sys.tables AS t
JOIN sys.schemas AS s ON s.schema_id = t.schema_id
WHERE s.name IN ('erp', 'audit')
ORDER BY s.name, t.name;
GO
```

**Expected outputs:** The file's declared objects, logs, tables, checks, or documentation when the user later runs or reads it.

```sql
-- Dialect: PostgreSQL SQL
-- Purpose: create the digital source schema and tables.
-- Run in: pgAdmin Query Tool connected to database northstar_digital.
-- Idempotency: CREATE IF NOT EXISTS avoids replacing existing objects.

CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS digital;
CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS audit;

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS audit.source_load_batch
(
    batch_id            varchar(80) PRIMARY KEY,
    process_name        varchar(100) NOT NULL,
    started_at_utc      timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    finished_at_utc     timestamptz NULL,
    status              varchar(20) NOT NULL,
    source_file_count   integer NULL,
    loaded_row_count    bigint NULL,
    error_message       text NULL
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS digital.web_users
(
    web_user_id         bigint PRIMARY KEY,
    customer_id         integer NULL,
    anonymous_cookie_id varchar(64) NOT NULL,
    email_hash          char(64) NULL,
    created_at          timestamptz NOT NULL,
    updated_at          timestamptz NOT NULL,
    CONSTRAINT uq_web_users_cookie UNIQUE (anonymous_cookie_id)
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS digital.campaigns
(
    campaign_id         integer PRIMARY KEY,
    campaign_code       varchar(30) NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    campaign_name       varchar(200) NOT NULL,
    channel             varchar(40) NOT NULL,
    start_date          date NOT NULL,
    end_date            date NOT NULL,
    budget_amount       numeric(14,2) NOT NULL,
    currency_code       varchar(3) NOT NULL,
    created_at          timestamptz NOT NULL,
    updated_at          timestamptz NOT NULL,
    CONSTRAINT ck_campaign_dates CHECK (end_date >= start_date)
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS digital.web_sessions
(
    session_id          bigint PRIMARY KEY,
    web_user_id         bigint NULL REFERENCES digital.web_users(web_user_id),
    session_start_utc   timestamptz NOT NULL,
    session_end_utc     timestamptz NULL,
    source_channel      varchar(40) NOT NULL,
    campaign_id         integer NULL REFERENCES digital.campaigns(campaign_id),
    device_type         varchar(30) NOT NULL,
    country_code        varchar(10) NOT NULL,
    converted_order_id  bigint NULL,
    created_at          timestamptz NOT NULL,
    CONSTRAINT ck_session_end CHECK (session_end_utc IS NULL OR session_end_utc >= session_start_utc)
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS digital.web_events
(
    event_id            bigint PRIMARY KEY,
    session_id          bigint NOT NULL REFERENCES digital.web_sessions(session_id),
    event_timestamp     timestamptz NOT NULL,
    event_type          varchar(50) NOT NULL,
    page_url            text NULL,
    product_id          integer NULL,
    order_id            bigint NULL,
    event_properties    jsonb NULL,
    created_at          timestamptz NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS digital.campaign_touchpoints
(
    touchpoint_id       bigint PRIMARY KEY,
    web_user_id         bigint NULL REFERENCES digital.web_users(web_user_id),
    session_id          bigint NULL REFERENCES digital.web_sessions(session_id),
    campaign_id         integer NOT NULL REFERENCES digital.campaigns(campaign_id),
    touchpoint_timestamp timestamptz NOT NULL,
    touchpoint_type     varchar(40) NOT NULL,
    attribution_weight  numeric(8,6) NOT NULL,
    created_at          timestamptz NOT NULL,
    CONSTRAINT ck_touchpoint_weight CHECK (attribution_weight >= 0 AND attribution_weight <= 1)
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS digital.marketing_spend
(
    spend_id            bigint PRIMARY KEY,
    spend_date          date NOT NULL,
    campaign_id         integer NOT NULL REFERENCES digital.campaigns(campaign_id),
    channel             varchar(40) NOT NULL,
    spend_amount        numeric(14,2) NOT NULL,
    impressions         bigint NOT NULL,
    clicks              bigint NOT NULL,
    currency_code       varchar(3) NOT NULL,
    created_at          timestamptz NOT NULL,
    CONSTRAINT uq_marketing_spend_grain UNIQUE (spend_date, campaign_id, channel),
    CONSTRAINT ck_spend_nonnegative CHECK (spend_amount >= 0 AND impressions >= 0 AND clicks >= 0)
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS ix_web_sessions_start ON digital.web_sessions(session_start_utc);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS ix_web_events_session_time ON digital.web_events(session_id, event_timestamp);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS ix_marketing_spend_date ON digital.marketing_spend(spend_date);

SELECT table_schema, table_name
FROM information_schema.tables
WHERE table_schema IN ('digital', 'audit')
ORDER BY table_schema, table_name;
```

<a id="source-erp-productcategories"></a>
### Source object 1 — `erp.product_categories`

**Real-world object:** `product categories` in the SQL Server ERP domain.  
**Why it belongs in this source:** The object is generated and operated with the transaction or digital behavior assigned to SQL Server ERP; the placement creates a realistic heterogeneous integration boundary.  
**Declared grain:** one row per category identifier. Verify that every column and example row describes that same unit.  
**Primary key:** `category_id`  
**Foreign keys:** `parent_category_id` → `product_categories.category_id`  
**Index purpose:** Primary, unique, foreign-key, timestamp, and business-key indexes support integrity or extraction access patterns; do not add indexes without a query reason.

#### Column-by-column design

| Column | Data type | Null? | PK | FK | Business definition | Example | Why the type/constraint fits |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `category_id` | `INT` | No | Yes | — | Category identifier | `10` | a whole-number type for identifiers, counts, flags represented as numbers, or day values. Required because the business record is incomplete without it |
| `category_name` | `NVARCHAR(100)` | No | No | — | Business category name | `Home Office` | text with either a stated maximum length or engine-managed variable length. Required because the business record is incomplete without it |
| `parent_category_id` | `INT` | Yes | No | product_categories.category_id | Optional parent category | `NULL` | a whole-number type for identifiers, counts, flags represented as numbers, or day values. Nullable because the source can legitimately omit it |

### Source object 3 — `erp.products`

**Real-world object:** `products` in the SQL Server ERP domain.  
**Why it belongs in this source:** The object is generated and operated with the transaction or digital behavior assigned to SQL Server ERP; the placement creates a realistic heterogeneous integration boundary.  
**Declared grain:** one row per product identifier. Verify that every column and example row describes that same unit.  
**Primary key:** `product_id`  
**Foreign keys:** `category_id` → `product_categories.category_id`; `supplier_id` → `suppliers.supplier_id`  
**Index purpose:** Primary, unique, foreign-key, timestamp, and business-key indexes support integrity or extraction access patterns; do not add indexes without a query reason.

| `sku` | `VARCHAR(30)` | No | No | — | Stock keeping unit business key | `NRT-ELE-10001` | text with either a stated maximum length or engine-managed variable length. Required because the business record is incomplete without it |

#### DDL section — build and explain it before execution

**Language:** T-SQL  
**Exact file:** `sql/sqlserver/source/02_create_erp_tables.sql`  
**Execution location:** SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS), database `NorthstarRetail_ERP`.  
**Input:** The requirements and column design above.  
**Output:** One table plus its constraints and indexes when the statement is run in the correct database.

```sql
CREATE TABLE erp.products
    (
        product_id          INT NOT NULL CONSTRAINT PK_products PRIMARY KEY,
        sku                 VARCHAR(30) NOT NULL,
        product_name        NVARCHAR(200) NOT NULL,
        category_id         INT NOT NULL,
        supplier_id         INT NOT NULL,
        brand               NVARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
        unit_cost           DECIMAL(12,2) NOT NULL,
        list_price          DECIMAL(12,2) NOT NULL,
        currency_code       CHAR(3) NOT NULL,
        active_flag         BIT NOT NULL,
        created_at          DATETIME2(3) NOT NULL,
        updated_at          DATETIME2(3) NOT NULL,
        CONSTRAINT UQ_products_sku UNIQUE (sku),
        CONSTRAINT FK_products_category FOREIGN KEY (category_id) REFERENCES erp.product_categories(category_id),
        CONSTRAINT FK_products_supplier FOREIGN KEY (supplier_id) REFERENCES erp.suppliers(supplier_id),
        CONSTRAINT CK_products_amounts CHECK (unit_cost >= 0 AND list_price >= 0)
    );
```

#### DDL section — build and explain it before execution

**Language:** T-SQL  
**Exact file:** `sql/sqlserver/source/02_create_erp_tables.sql`  
**Execution location:** SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS), database `NorthstarRetail_ERP`.  
**Input:** The requirements and column design above.  
**Output:** One table plus its constraints and indexes when the statement is run in the correct database.

```sql
CREATE TABLE erp.stores
    (
        store_id            INT NOT NULL CONSTRAINT PK_stores PRIMARY KEY,
        store_code          VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,
        store_name          NVARCHAR(150) NOT NULL,
        region              VARCHAR(30) NOT NULL,
        state_code          CHAR(2) NOT NULL,
        city                NVARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
        open_date           DATE NOT NULL,
        active_flag         BIT NOT NULL,
        created_at          DATETIME2(3) NOT NULL,
        updated_at          DATETIME2(3) NOT NULL,
        CONSTRAINT UQ_stores_store_code UNIQUE (store_code)
    );
```

### Source object 5 — `erp.employees`

**Real-world object:** `employees` in the SQL Server ERP domain.  
**Why it belongs in this source:** The object is generated and operated with the transaction or digital behavior assigned to SQL Server ERP; the placement creates a realistic heterogeneous integration boundary.  
**Declared grain:** one row per employee identifier. Verify that every column and example row describes that same unit.  
**Primary key:** `employee_id`  
**Foreign keys:** `store_id` → `stores.store_id`; `manager_employee_id` → `employees.employee_id`  
**Index purpose:** Primary, unique, foreign-key, timestamp, and business-key indexes support integrity or extraction access patterns; do not add indexes without a query reason.

#### Column-by-column design

| Column | Data type | Null? | PK | FK | Business definition | Example | Why the type/constraint fits |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `employee_id` | `INT` | No | Yes | — | Employee identifier | `301` | a whole-number type for identifiers, counts, flags represented as numbers, or day values. Required because the business record is incomplete without it |
| `employee_number` | `VARCHAR(20)` | No | No | — | Employee business key | `EMP-00301` | text with either a stated maximum length or engine-managed variable length. Required because the business record is incomplete without it |

| `first_name` | `NVARCHAR(80)` | No | No | — | Synthetic first name | `Mina` | text with either a stated maximum length or engine-managed variable length. Required because the business record is incomplete without it |

| `hire_date` | `DATE` | No | No | — | Hire date | `2024-03-11` | a calendar date with no time-of-day component. Required because the business record is incomplete without it |

#### DDL section — build and explain it before execution

**Language:** T-SQL  
**Exact file:** `sql/sqlserver/source/02_create_erp_tables.sql`  
**Execution location:** SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS), database `NorthstarRetail_ERP`.  
**Input:** The requirements and column design above.  
**Output:** One table plus its constraints and indexes when the statement is run in the correct database.

```sql
CREATE TABLE erp.employees
    (
        employee_id         INT NOT NULL CONSTRAINT PK_employees PRIMARY KEY,
        employee_number     VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,
        store_id            INT NULL,
        manager_employee_id INT NULL,
        first_name          NVARCHAR(80) NOT NULL,
        last_name           NVARCHAR(80) NOT NULL,
        job_title           NVARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
        hire_date           DATE NOT NULL,
        active_flag         BIT NOT NULL,
        created_at          DATETIME2(3) NOT NULL,
        updated_at          DATETIME2(3) NOT NULL,
        CONSTRAINT UQ_employees_number UNIQUE (employee_number),
        CONSTRAINT FK_employees_store FOREIGN KEY (store_id) REFERENCES erp.stores(store_id),
        CONSTRAINT FK_employees_manager FOREIGN KEY (manager_employee_id) REFERENCES erp.employees(employee_id)
    );
```

### Source object 6 — `erp.customers`

**Real-world object:** `customers` in the SQL Server ERP domain.  
**Why it belongs in this source:** The object is generated and operated with the transaction or digital behavior assigned to SQL Server ERP; the placement creates a realistic heterogeneous integration boundary.  
**Declared grain:** one row per customer identifier. Verify that every column and example row describes that same unit.  
**Primary key:** `customer_id`  
**Foreign keys:** No foreign key; this object is a parent/reference table or independent event table.  
**Index purpose:** Primary, unique, foreign-key, timestamp, and business-key indexes support integrity or extraction access patterns; do not add indexes without a query reason.

#### DDL section — build and explain it before execution

**Language:** T-SQL  
**Exact file:** `sql/sqlserver/source/02_create_erp_tables.sql`  
**Execution location:** SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS), database `NorthstarRetail_ERP`.  
**Input:** The requirements and column design above.  
**Output:** One table plus its constraints and indexes when the statement is run in the correct database.

```sql
CREATE TABLE erp.customers
    (
        customer_id         INT NOT NULL CONSTRAINT PK_customers PRIMARY KEY,
        customer_number     VARCHAR(25) NOT NULL,
        first_name          NVARCHAR(80) NOT NULL,
        last_name           NVARCHAR(80) NOT NULL,
        email               NVARCHAR(255) NULL,
        phone               VARCHAR(40) NULL,
        signup_date         DATE NOT NULL,
        loyalty_tier        VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,
        marketing_opt_in    BIT NOT NULL,
        created_at          DATETIME2(3) NOT NULL,
        updated_at          DATETIME2(3) NOT NULL
        -- Deliberately no unique constraint on customer_number in the learning source:
        -- controlled duplicate business keys must reach Silver and be handled there.
    );
```

### Source object 7 — `erp.addresses`

**Real-world object:** `addresses` in the SQL Server ERP domain.  
**Why it belongs in this source:** The object is generated and operated with the transaction or digital behavior assigned to SQL Server ERP; the placement creates a realistic heterogeneous integration boundary.  
**Declared grain:** one row per address identifier. Verify that every column and example row describes that same unit.  
**Primary key:** `address_id`  
**Foreign keys:** `customer_id` → `customers.customer_id`  
**Index purpose:** Primary, unique, foreign-key, timestamp, and business-key indexes support integrity or extraction access patterns; do not add indexes without a query reason.

#### DDL section — build and explain it before execution

**Language:** T-SQL  
**Exact file:** `sql/sqlserver/source/02_create_erp_tables.sql`  
**Execution location:** SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS), database `NorthstarRetail_ERP`.  
**Input:** The requirements and column design above.  
**Output:** One table plus its constraints and indexes when the statement is run in the correct database.

```sql
CREATE TABLE erp.addresses
    (
        address_id          INT NOT NULL CONSTRAINT PK_addresses PRIMARY KEY,
        customer_id         INT NOT NULL,
        address_type        VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,
        line1               NVARCHAR(200) NOT NULL,
        line2               NVARCHAR(200) NULL,
        city                NVARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
        state_code          VARCHAR(10) NOT NULL,
        postal_code         VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,
        country_code        VARCHAR(10) NOT NULL,
        is_default          BIT NOT NULL,
        created_at          DATETIME2(3) NOT NULL,
        updated_at          DATETIME2(3) NOT NULL,
        CONSTRAINT FK_addresses_customer FOREIGN KEY (customer_id) REFERENCES erp.customers(customer_id)
    );
```

### Source object 8 — `erp.orders`

**Real-world object:** `orders` in the SQL Server ERP domain.  
**Why it belongs in this source:** The object is generated and operated with the transaction or digital behavior assigned to SQL Server ERP; the placement creates a realistic heterogeneous integration boundary.  
**Declared grain:** one row per order identifier. Verify that every column and example row describes that same unit.  
**Primary key:** `order_id`  
**Foreign keys:** `customer_id` → `customers.customer_id`; `store_id` → `stores.store_id`; `employee_id` → `employees.employee_id`  
**Index purpose:** Primary, unique, foreign-key, timestamp, and business-key indexes support integrity or extraction access patterns; do not add indexes without a query reason.

#### DDL section — build and explain it before execution

**Language:** T-SQL  
**Exact file:** `sql/sqlserver/source/02_create_erp_tables.sql`  
**Execution location:** SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS), database `NorthstarRetail_ERP`.  
**Input:** The requirements and column design above.  
**Output:** One table plus its constraints and indexes when the statement is run in the correct database.

```sql
CREATE TABLE erp.orders
    (
        order_id            BIGINT NOT NULL CONSTRAINT PK_orders PRIMARY KEY,
        order_number        VARCHAR(30) NOT NULL,
        customer_id         INT NOT NULL,
        store_id            INT NULL,
        employee_id         INT NULL,
        channel_code        VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,
        order_timestamp     DATETIME2(3) NOT NULL,
        order_status        VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,
        promotion_code      VARCHAR(30) NULL,
        currency_code       CHAR(3) NOT NULL,
        created_at          DATETIME2(3) NOT NULL,
        updated_at          DATETIME2(3) NOT NULL,
        CONSTRAINT UQ_orders_order_number UNIQUE (order_number),
        CONSTRAINT FK_orders_customer FOREIGN KEY (customer_id) REFERENCES erp.customers(customer_id),
        CONSTRAINT FK_orders_store FOREIGN KEY (store_id) REFERENCES erp.stores(store_id),
        CONSTRAINT FK_orders_employee FOREIGN KEY (employee_id) REFERENCES erp.employees(employee_id),
        CONSTRAINT CK_orders_channel CHECK (channel_code IN ('STORE', 'ONLINE'))
    );
```

### Source object 9 — `erp.order_items`

**Real-world object:** `order items` in the SQL Server ERP domain.  
**Why it belongs in this source:** The object is generated and operated with the transaction or digital behavior assigned to SQL Server ERP; the placement creates a realistic heterogeneous integration boundary.  
**Declared grain:** one row per sales-line identifier. Verify that every column and example row describes that same unit.  
**Primary key:** `order_item_id`  
**Foreign keys:** `order_id` → `orders.order_id`; `product_id` → `products.product_id`  
**Index purpose:** Primary, unique, foreign-key, timestamp, and business-key indexes support integrity or extraction access patterns; do not add indexes without a query reason.

#### DDL section — build and explain it before execution

**Language:** T-SQL  
**Exact file:** `sql/sqlserver/source/02_create_erp_tables.sql`  
**Execution location:** SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS), database `NorthstarRetail_ERP`.  
**Input:** The requirements and column design above.  
**Output:** One table plus its constraints and indexes when the statement is run in the correct database.

```sql
CREATE TABLE erp.order_items
    (
        order_item_id       BIGINT NOT NULL CONSTRAINT PK_order_items PRIMARY KEY,
        order_id            BIGINT NOT NULL,
        line_number         INT NOT NULL,
        product_id          INT NOT NULL,
        quantity            INT NOT NULL,
        unit_price          DECIMAL(12,2) NOT NULL,
        unit_cost           DECIMAL(12,2) NOT NULL,
        discount_amount     DECIMAL(12,2) NOT NULL,
        tax_amount          DECIMAL(12,2) NOT NULL,
        created_at          DATETIME2(3) NOT NULL,
        updated_at          DATETIME2(3) NOT NULL,
        CONSTRAINT UQ_order_items_line UNIQUE (order_id, line_number),
        CONSTRAINT FK_order_items_order FOREIGN KEY (order_id) REFERENCES erp.orders(order_id),
        CONSTRAINT FK_order_items_product FOREIGN KEY (product_id) REFERENCES erp.products(product_id)
        -- No positive-quantity check: controlled impossible quantities are a Silver lesson.
    );
```

### Source object 10 — `erp.payments`

**Real-world object:** `payments` in the SQL Server ERP domain.  
**Why it belongs in this source:** The object is generated and operated with the transaction or digital behavior assigned to SQL Server ERP; the placement creates a realistic heterogeneous integration boundary.  
**Declared grain:** one row per payment identifier. Verify that every column and example row describes that same unit.  
**Primary key:** `payment_id`  
**Foreign keys:** `order_id` → `orders.order_id`  
**Index purpose:** Primary, unique, foreign-key, timestamp, and business-key indexes support integrity or extraction access patterns; do not add indexes without a query reason.

#### DDL section — build and explain it before execution

**Language:** T-SQL  
**Exact file:** `sql/sqlserver/source/02_create_erp_tables.sql`  
**Execution location:** SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS), database `NorthstarRetail_ERP`.  
**Input:** The requirements and column design above.  
**Output:** One table plus its constraints and indexes when the statement is run in the correct database.

```sql
CREATE TABLE erp.payments
    (
        payment_id          BIGINT NOT NULL CONSTRAINT PK_payments PRIMARY KEY,
        order_id            BIGINT NOT NULL,
        payment_timestamp   DATETIME2(3) NOT NULL,
        payment_method      VARCHAR(30) NOT NULL,
        payment_status      VARCHAR(30) NOT NULL,
        amount              DECIMAL(14,2) NOT NULL,
        currency_code       VARCHAR(3) NOT NULL,
        transaction_reference VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL,
        created_at          DATETIME2(3) NOT NULL,
        updated_at          DATETIME2(3) NOT NULL,
        CONSTRAINT UQ_payments_transaction UNIQUE (transaction_reference),
        CONSTRAINT FK_payments_order FOREIGN KEY (order_id) REFERENCES erp.orders(order_id)
    );
```

### Source object 11 — `erp.shipments`

**Real-world object:** `shipments` in the SQL Server ERP domain.  
**Why it belongs in this source:** The object is generated and operated with the transaction or digital behavior assigned to SQL Server ERP; the placement creates a realistic heterogeneous integration boundary.  
**Declared grain:** one row per shipment identifier. Verify that every column and example row describes that same unit.  
**Primary key:** `shipment_id`  
**Foreign keys:** `order_id` → `orders.order_id`; `shipping_address_id` → `addresses.address_id`  
**Index purpose:** Primary, unique, foreign-key, timestamp, and business-key indexes support integrity or extraction access patterns; do not add indexes without a query reason.

| Column | Data type | Null? | PK | FK | Business definition | Example | Why the type/constraint fits |

#### DDL section — build and explain it before execution

**Language:** T-SQL  
**Exact file:** `sql/sqlserver/source/02_create_erp_tables.sql`  
**Execution location:** SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS), database `NorthstarRetail_ERP`.  
**Input:** The requirements and column design above.  
**Output:** One table plus its constraints and indexes when the statement is run in the correct database.

```sql
CREATE TABLE erp.shipments
    (
        shipment_id         BIGINT NOT NULL CONSTRAINT PK_shipments PRIMARY KEY,
        order_id            BIGINT NOT NULL,
        carrier             NVARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
        tracking_number     VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
        ship_date           DATE NOT NULL,
        promised_delivery_date DATE NOT NULL,
        actual_delivery_date DATE NULL,
        shipment_status     VARCHAR(30) NOT NULL,
        shipping_cost       DECIMAL(12,2) NOT NULL,
        created_at          DATETIME2(3) NOT NULL,
        updated_at          DATETIME2(3) NOT NULL,
        CONSTRAINT UQ_shipments_tracking UNIQUE (tracking_number),
        CONSTRAINT FK_shipments_order FOREIGN KEY (order_id) REFERENCES erp.orders(order_id)
    );
```

### Source object 12 — `erp.inventory_transactions`

**Real-world object:** `inventory transactions` in the SQL Server ERP domain.  
**Why it belongs in this source:** The object is generated and operated with the transaction or digital behavior assigned to SQL Server ERP; the placement creates a realistic heterogeneous integration boundary.  
**Declared grain:** one row per inventory movement identifier. Verify that every column and example row describes that same unit.  
**Primary key:** `inventory_transaction_id`  
**Foreign keys:** `store_id` → `stores.store_id`; `product_id` → `products.product_id`  
**Index purpose:** Primary, unique, foreign-key, timestamp, and business-key indexes support integrity or extraction access patterns; do not add indexes without a query reason.

#### Column-by-column design

| Column | Data type | Null? | PK | FK | Business definition | Example | Why the type/constraint fits |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `inventory_transaction_id` | `BIGINT` | No | Yes | — | Inventory movement identifier | `9400001` | a whole-number type used where identifiers or counts may exceed the normal integer range. Required because the business record is incomplete without it |
| `store_id` | `INT` | No | No | stores.store_id | Inventory location | `201` | a whole-number type for identifiers, counts, flags represented as numbers, or day values. Required because the business record is incomplete without it |

| `transaction_type` | `VARCHAR(30)` | No | No | — | RECEIPT, SALE, RETURN, ADJUSTMENT, or TRANSFER | `SALE` | text with either a stated maximum length or engine-managed variable length. Required because the business record is incomplete without it |

#### DDL section — build and explain it before execution

**Language:** T-SQL  
**Exact file:** `sql/sqlserver/source/02_create_erp_tables.sql`  
**Execution location:** SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS), database `NorthstarRetail_ERP`.  
**Input:** The requirements and column design above.  
**Output:** One table plus its constraints and indexes when the statement is run in the correct database.

```sql
CREATE TABLE erp.inventory_transactions
    (
        inventory_transaction_id BIGINT NOT NULL CONSTRAINT PK_inventory_transactions PRIMARY KEY,
        store_id            INT NOT NULL,
        product_id          INT NOT NULL,
        transaction_timestamp DATETIME2(3) NOT NULL,
        transaction_type    VARCHAR(30) NOT NULL,
        quantity_change     INT NOT NULL,
        reference_type      VARCHAR(30) NULL,
        reference_id        BIGINT NULL,
        created_at          DATETIME2(3) NOT NULL,
        CONSTRAINT FK_inventory_transactions_store FOREIGN KEY (store_id) REFERENCES erp.stores(store_id),
        CONSTRAINT FK_inventory_transactions_product FOREIGN KEY (product_id) REFERENCES erp.products(product_id)
    );
```

### Source object 13 — `erp.inventory_snapshots`

**Real-world object:** `inventory snapshots` in the SQL Server ERP domain.  
**Why it belongs in this source:** The object is generated and operated with the transaction or digital behavior assigned to SQL Server ERP; the placement creates a realistic heterogeneous integration boundary.  
**Declared grain:** one row per snapshot row identifier. Verify that every column and example row describes that same unit.  
**Primary key:** `inventory_snapshot_id`  
**Foreign keys:** `store_id` → `stores.store_id`; `product_id` → `products.product_id`  
**Index purpose:** Primary, unique, foreign-key, timestamp, and business-key indexes support integrity or extraction access patterns; do not add indexes without a query reason.

#### DDL section — build and explain it before execution

**Language:** T-SQL  
**Exact file:** `sql/sqlserver/source/02_create_erp_tables.sql`  
**Execution location:** SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS), database `NorthstarRetail_ERP`.  
**Input:** The requirements and column design above.  
**Output:** One table plus its constraints and indexes when the statement is run in the correct database.

```sql
CREATE TABLE erp.inventory_snapshots
    (
        inventory_snapshot_id BIGINT NOT NULL CONSTRAINT PK_inventory_snapshots PRIMARY KEY,
        snapshot_date       DATE NOT NULL,
        store_id            INT NOT NULL,
        product_id          INT NOT NULL,
        quantity_on_hand    INT NOT NULL,
        quantity_reserved   INT NOT NULL,
        reorder_point       INT NOT NULL,
        created_at          DATETIME2(3) NOT NULL,
        CONSTRAINT UQ_inventory_snapshot_grain UNIQUE (snapshot_date, store_id, product_id),
        CONSTRAINT FK_inventory_snapshots_store FOREIGN KEY (store_id) REFERENCES erp.stores(store_id),
        CONSTRAINT FK_inventory_snapshots_product FOREIGN KEY (product_id) REFERENCES erp.products(product_id)
    );
```

### Source object 14 — `digital.web_users`

**Real-world object:** `web users` in the PostgreSQL Digital domain.  
**Why it belongs in this source:** The object is generated and operated with the transaction or digital behavior assigned to PostgreSQL Digital; the placement creates a realistic heterogeneous integration boundary.  
**Declared grain:** one row per digital user identifier. Verify that every column and example row describes that same unit.  
**Primary key:** `web_user_id`  
**Foreign keys:** No foreign key; this object is a parent/reference table or independent event table.  
**Index purpose:** Primary, unique, foreign-key, timestamp, and business-key indexes support integrity or extraction access patterns; do not add indexes without a query reason.

#### DDL section — build and explain it before execution

**Language:** PostgreSQL SQL  
**Exact file:** `sql/postgres/source/01_create_digital_schema.sql`  
**Execution location:** pgAdmin 4 Query Tool, database `northstar_digital`.  
**Input:** The requirements and column design above.  
**Output:** One table plus its constraints and indexes when the statement is run in the correct database.

```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS digital.web_users
(
    web_user_id         bigint PRIMARY KEY,
    customer_id         integer NULL,
    anonymous_cookie_id varchar(64) NOT NULL,
    email_hash          char(64) NULL,
    created_at          timestamptz NOT NULL,
    updated_at          timestamptz NOT NULL,
    CONSTRAINT uq_web_users_cookie UNIQUE (anonymous_cookie_id)
);
```

```sql
);
```

#### DDL section — build and explain it before execution

**Language:** PostgreSQL SQL  
**Exact file:** `sql/postgres/source/01_create_digital_schema.sql`  
**Execution location:** pgAdmin 4 Query Tool, database `northstar_digital`.  
**Input:** The requirements and column design above.  
**Output:** One table plus its constraints and indexes when the statement is run in the correct database.

```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS digital.web_sessions
(
    session_id          bigint PRIMARY KEY,
    web_user_id         bigint NULL REFERENCES digital.web_users(web_user_id),
    session_start_utc   timestamptz NOT NULL,
    session_end_utc     timestamptz NULL,
    source_channel      varchar(40) NOT NULL,
    campaign_id         integer NULL REFERENCES digital.campaigns(campaign_id),
    device_type         varchar(30) NOT NULL,
    country_code        varchar(10) NOT NULL,
    converted_order_id  bigint NULL,
    created_at          timestamptz NOT NULL,
    CONSTRAINT ck_session_end CHECK (session_end_utc IS NULL OR session_end_utc >= session_start_utc)
);
```

**Why it belongs in this source:** The object is generated and operated with the transaction or digital behavior assigned to PostgreSQL Digital; the placement creates a realistic heterogeneous integration boundary.  
**Declared grain:** one row per event row identifier. Verify that every column and example row describes that same unit.

### Source object 18 — `digital.campaign_touchpoints`

**Real-world object:** `campaign touchpoints` in the PostgreSQL Digital domain.  
**Why it belongs in this source:** The object is generated and operated with the transaction or digital behavior assigned to PostgreSQL Digital; the placement creates a realistic heterogeneous integration boundary.  
**Declared grain:** one row per marketing touchpoint identifier. Verify that every column and example row describes that same unit.  
**Primary key:** `touchpoint_id`  
**Foreign keys:** `campaign_id` → `campaigns.campaign_id`; `web_user_id` → `web_users.web_user_id`; `session_id` → `web_sessions.session_id`  
**Index purpose:** Primary, unique, foreign-key, timestamp, and business-key indexes support integrity or extraction access patterns; do not add indexes without a query reason.

#### Column-by-column design

| Column | Data type | Null? | PK | FK | Business definition | Example | Why the type/constraint fits |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `touchpoint_id` | `BIGINT` | No | Yes | — | Marketing touchpoint identifier | `7300001` | a whole-number type used where identifiers or counts may exceed the normal integer range. Required because the business record is incomplete without it |
| `campaign_id` | `INTEGER` | No | No | campaigns.campaign_id | Campaign | `801` | the storage type selected for the business meaning and source-system behavior of this column. Required because the business record is incomplete without it |
| `web_user_id` | `BIGINT` | Yes | No | web_users.web_user_id | Known user | `700001` | a whole-number type used where identifiers or counts may exceed the normal integer range. Nullable because the source can legitimately omit it |
| `session_id` | `BIGINT` | Yes | No | web_sessions.session_id | Related session | `7100001` | a whole-number type used where identifiers or counts may exceed the normal integer range. Nullable because the source can legitimately omit it |
| `touchpoint_timestamp` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | No | No | — | Touchpoint time | `2026-01-04T13:58:00Z` | a date-and-time value used for event time, creation time, update time, or incremental watermarks. Required because the business record is incomplete without it |
| `touchpoint_type` | `VARCHAR(30)` | No | No | — | IMPRESSION, CLICK, EMAIL_OPEN, or EMAIL_CLICK | `CLICK` | text with either a stated maximum length or engine-managed variable length. Required because the business record is incomplete without it |
| `cost_amount` | `NUMERIC(12,4)` | No | No | — | Allocated cost | `0.8500` | an exact fixed-precision number suitable for currency or ratios where binary floating-point rounding is undesirable. Required because the business record is incomplete without it |
| `currency_code` | `CHAR(3)` | No | No | — | Cost currency | `USD` | text with either a stated maximum length or engine-managed variable length. Required because the business record is incomplete without it |
| `created_at` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | No | No | — | Source creation time | `2026-01-04T13:58:01Z` | a date-and-time value used for event time, creation time, update time, or incremental watermarks. Required because the business record is incomplete without it |

### Source object 19 — `digital.marketing_spend`

**Real-world object:** `marketing spend` in the PostgreSQL Digital domain.  
**Why it belongs in this source:** The object is generated and operated with the transaction or digital behavior assigned to PostgreSQL Digital; the placement creates a realistic heterogeneous integration boundary.  
**Declared grain:** one row per spend row identifier. Verify that every column and example row describes that same unit.  
**Primary key:** `marketing_spend_id`  
**Foreign keys:** `campaign_id` → `campaigns.campaign_id`

#### DDL section — build and explain it before execution

**Language:** PostgreSQL SQL  
**Exact file:** `sql/postgres/source/01_create_digital_schema.sql`  
**Execution location:** pgAdmin 4 Query Tool, database `northstar_digital`.  
**Input:** The requirements and column design above.  
**Output:** One table plus its constraints and indexes when the statement is run in the correct database.

```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS digital.marketing_spend
(
    spend_id            bigint PRIMARY KEY,
    spend_date          date NOT NULL,
    campaign_id         integer NOT NULL REFERENCES digital.campaigns(campaign_id),
    channel             varchar(40) NOT NULL,
    spend_amount        numeric(14,2) NOT NULL,
    impressions         bigint NOT NULL,
    clicks              bigint NOT NULL,
    currency_code       varchar(3) NOT NULL,
    created_at          timestamptz NOT NULL,
    CONSTRAINT uq_marketing_spend_grain UNIQUE (spend_date, campaign_id, channel),
    CONSTRAINT ck_spend_nonnegative CHECK (spend_amount >= 0 AND impressions >= 0 AND clicks >= 0)
);
```

## Lesson 4.5 — Verify, troubleshoot, commit, teach back, and stop safely

## What your screen should look like before starting

## Design decision — Source-system separation

**Question:**  
Where should ERP and digital data live?

**Options considered:**

- One SQL Server database.
- SQL Server ERP plus PostgreSQL digital.
- Only flat files.

**Beginner path selected:**  
Use SQL Server for ERP and PostgreSQL for digital activity.

**Why this path was selected:**  
Two engines create realistic integration work while remaining manageable locally.

**Tradeoff:**  
More installation, drivers, and dialect handling are required.

**What a company might do instead:**  
A company may use SaaS sources, managed cloud databases, event platforms, and CDC.

**How to explain this in an interview:**  
I separated operational domains across SQL Server and PostgreSQL to demonstrate heterogeneous-source ingestion and dialect-aware engineering.




## If you see Result A

The database/schema/table exists and metadata matches the declared columns, keys, and grain. Record the exact result, perform the named independent verification, and continue only when the gate is satisfied.

## If you see Result B

The object is absent, already exists with a different definition, or you are connected to the wrong database. Treat this as information, not permission to delete or overwrite. Follow the branch-specific diagnostic in the current action, preserve evidence, and continue only after the state is understood.

## If you see an error

Read the first meaningful error line, redact secrets, and verify the application, path, branch, server/database, catalog/schema, batch ID, parameters, version/tier, and object name. Run the smallest observational check first. Do not reset Git history, drop data, disable a rule, force-push, or replace the target merely to make the error disappear.

### Interpret `git status --short`

- `??` means untracked: Git sees a new path but it is not staged.
- ` M` means modified in the working tree but not staged.
- `M ` means the staged version differs from the last commit.
- `MM` means a staged version exists and the file has additional unstaged edits.
- `A ` means staged as a new file.
- `D` means deletion; stop and investigate unless deletion is deliberate.
- `R` means rename; inspect both old and new paths.
- A blank result means the working tree is clean. It does not prove database, Databricks, or Power BI work occurred.

### Verify on GitHub

1. CLICK: Open the repository page in a browser.

### Push-rejected recovery

If Git says the remote contains work you do not have, do not use `--force`. Run `git fetch origin`, inspect `git log --oneline --graph --decorate --all -20`, then rebase or merge only after understanding the divergence. Resolve conflicts one file at a time, run tests again, and push normally. A rejection protects remote work; it is not permission to overwrite it.

5. Troubleshooting: Your output differs from the example. What should you check before deleting, overwriting, resetting, force-pushing, or weakening a test?

7. Code reading: Why are input, accepted, rejected, and deduplicated counts recorded separately?
8. Ownership: Which status may you select only after personally performing and inspecting the verification?

---

## Mini quiz answer key and explanations

**1. B.** This phase is ordered after its prerequisites so its output has a trustworthy input. A is wrong because order is intentional; C is wrong because later phases depend on the handoff; D is wrong because screenshots follow verification.

**2. False.** Lack of an error proves only that the application accepted something; context and independent verification still matter.

**3. Grain.** Grain is the precise meaning of one row. A key identifies a row, but it does not by itself state the row’s business meaning.

**4. `Get-Location`.** It shows the shell’s current folder. `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` separately verifies the repository root when inside a clone.

**5.** Check application, folder/path, branch, server/database, catalog/schema, batch ID, parameters, source/target grain, filter context, version/tier differences, and the first meaningful error. Destructive changes are not a diagnostic step.

**6.** Track A has manual upload/download boundaries and batch latency. A production alternative is routable private connectivity with cloud object storage/managed warehouse, identities, and automated orchestration.

**7.** Separate counts make every row outcome explainable. A single final count can hide silent drops, duplicates, or records that moved to quarantine.

**8. `Verified by me` / `VERIFIED BY USER`.** `PLANNED`, `CREATED BY USER`, and `RUN BY USER` describe earlier states; only inspected evidence supports verification.

## Why this phase happens now

**Earlier work this phase depends on:** Complete source schemas and data-quality scenarios.  
**What would go wrong if it happened earlier:** You would create objects without a verified requirement, valid upstream input, protected repository state, or known execution environment.  
**Later work that depends on it:** Phase 6 loads the generated parent and child data into the two database engines.  
**Decision being made:** Choose and verify the simplest local-first method that teaches the professional concept without pretending that local services are publicly reachable.  
**Alternatives:** A company could use managed cloud databases, infrastructure as code, service principals, direct JDBC publication, deployment bundles, or streaming. Those options are discussed as tradeoffs, not substituted silently.  
**Beginner path selected:** Track A: local SQL Server and PostgreSQL, Python batch extracts, manual governed upload to Databricks, Delta Bronze/Silver/Gold, manual verified export, local SQL Server warehouse, and Power BI Import.  
**Reason for the order:** Requirements become source decisions; sources become generated data; source data becomes extraction batches; batches become Bronze; Bronze becomes Silver; Silver becomes Gold; Gold becomes warehouse and Power BI input.

## Three-level explanation of the phase

### Level 1 — Child-simple explanation

Imagine building a store from labeled boxes. This phase handles one box, checks that the label is correct, and makes sure the next box receives the right thing. You do not pour all boxes together and hope the result is understandable.

### Level 2 — Northstar Retail project explanation

Phase 5 creates the specific Northstar Retail files, database objects, transformations, tests, model objects, or evidence described in the lessons. Every output keeps a visible connection to its source and batch so you can trace an order, customer, product, campaign, return, shipment, or inventory record.

### Level 3 — Professional explanation

This phase establishes a controlled boundary in an end-to-end batch platform. It defines contracts, execution context, idempotency behavior, quality expectations, evidence, and handoff artifacts so the downstream layer can be reproduced and reviewed independently.

## Retained phase lesson, exercises, rules, and expected results

> **Track:** Track A required

## 1. What you are building

A reproducible Python generator that creates all ERP, digital, CSV, and nested JSON source data at configurable scales, keeps normal foreign keys coherent, injects controlled quality defects, writes a batch manifest/checksums, and validates its own output.

## 2. Why it matters

A portfolio project needs data rich enough to exercise engineering decisions without exposing real people or employer information. A fixed seed and quality fixture turn messy data from random surprise into a repeatable test case.

## 3. Words to know

| Term | Plain-language definition |
| --- | --- |
| Module | Python file/package imported or run with `python -m`. |
| Function | Named reusable block with inputs and output/side effect. |
| Loop | Repeats logic over records or tables. |
| Dictionary | Key/value mapping used for configuration and records. |
| DataFrame | Table-like in-memory data structure from pandas/Spark. |
| Random seed | Starting value that makes pseudo-random business content reproducible. |
| Configuration | Values separated from logic, here in YAML and CLI arguments. |
| Logging | Structured messages about progress and failures. |
| Exception | Error object raised when code cannot safely continue. |
| Referential integrity | Child references point to existing parent records for normal data. |
| Distribution | Pattern of values/likelihoods rather than uniform randomness. |
| Fixture | Known data/expectation used by tests. |
| Docstring/type hint | Description and expected Python types that improve readability/tools. |

## 4. What must already be completed

Phases 1–4 complete. `.venv` is active and dependencies installed. Source databases need not contain rows yet.

## 5. Applications to open

| Application | How to open it | Why it is open |
| --- | --- | --- |
| VS Code | Repository root; open `scripts/data_generation/generate_northstar_data.py`. | Read functions, imports, CLI, and TODO work. |
| Windows PowerShell | Repository root with `.venv` active. | Run generator/tests and inspect output. |
| File Explorer or VS Code Explorer | Open `datasets/sample/`. | Inspect generated files and metadata. |

## 6. Exact click-by-click steps

> **Beginner rhythm:** Read the whole step. Confirm the application and location. Perform only that step. Verify the visible result. Record an error before attempting a fix.

## 7. Exact commands, one code block at a time

## 8. Where each command runs

Never infer the execution location from the code language. The command headings above identify the application and folder/database/catalog. Before every PowerShell command, run `Get-Location`; before SQL, verify the selected database; before Spark, print the catalog/schema/batch widgets.

## TEACHING EXAMPLE

The following small example or reference pattern explains the concept before you attempt Northstar-specific work. Read it, then complete **MY TASK** without copying the answer.

### Line-by-line code explanation

| Line or action | Meaning | Why it belongs here |
| --- | --- | --- |
| python -c "import sys, pandas, faker, yaml; print(sys.executable); print(pandas.__version__)" | Confirms interpreter and core imports. | Avoid debugging generator logic with the wrong Python environment. |
| python -m scripts.data_generation.generate_northstar_data --scale quick --seed 20260815 --output-dir datasets\generated\practice_quick | Runs generator as a package module with explicit scale, seed, output. | Module execution preserves imports and separates practice output from included sample. |
| python -m scripts.validation.validate_generated_data --input-dir datasets\generated\practice_quick | Checks required non-empty files and normal source relationships. | Generation success message is not enough. |
| Get-Content datasets\generated\practice_quick\metadata\generation_summary.csv | Prints per-file row counts. | You must know what was generated before loading. |
| python -m pytest -q tests\unit\test_generator.py tests\data_quality\test_sample_quality_fixture.py | Runs deterministic generation and intentional-dirty-data tests. | Proves same seed and expected defects behave as designed. |

### Python concepts in this generator

- Imports bring in tested libraries instead of rewriting Faker/DataFrame/YAML behavior.
- Functions each generate one subject or perform one responsibility.
- Loops create repeated fictional entities and events.
- Dictionaries represent record fields and table collections.
- DataFrames provide column operations and CSV writing.
- `random.Random(seed)` and `Faker.seed(seed)` make business content repeatable.
- `argparse` gives `--scale`, `--seed`, `--output-dir`, and `--config`.
- Logging says what happened; exceptions stop unsafe output.
- `if __name__ == "__main__"` runs `main()` only when launched, not when imported by tests.

## MY TASK

Run quick mode twice with the same seed into two folders, prove selected business files are byte-identical, inspect every controlled issue type, and complete one small generator enhancement with dictionary/test updates.

**Acceptance criteria:** Two same-seed business files match, normal references validate, expected dirty rows are observed, and any enhancement updates code, data dictionary, config if needed, and deterministic tests.

## HINT 1 — CONCEPT

## HINT 3 — NEAR-COMPLETE PATTERN

## 16. Common errors and exact fixes

| Message/symptom | Likely cause | Exact diagnostic | Safe fix | Verify |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| No module named scripts | Script was launched by path from wrong folder/interpreter. | `Get-Location`; `python -c "import sys; print(sys.path[0])"`. | Run from repository root with `python -m scripts.data_generation...`. | Generator starts. |
| FileNotFound config | Current folder is not repository root. | `Get-Location`; `Test-Path config\data_generation.yml`. | Enter verified root or pass explicit config. | Config loads. |
| Output differs with same seed | Timestamp fields/batch ID compared or nondeterministic operation added. | Diff selected business CSVs and isolate columns. | Exclude run metadata from reproducibility assertion or seed/sort all business choices. | Business files match. |
| Generation is slow | Scale too large for debugging. | Read `--scale` and config. | Use quick; only run portfolio after correctness. | Quick completes and tests pass. |

For deeper tool-specific diagnosis, use [`the troubleshooting index near the end of this workbook`](#complete-troubleshooting-index).
