## Retained phase lesson, exercises, rules, and expected results

> **Track:** Track A required  
> **Ownership status at start:** Workbook instructions exist; your execution is not yet verified.  
> **Evidence rule:** Replace placeholders only after the verification steps pass.

## 1. What you are building

A local extraction process that reads both databases and file feeds, writes timestamped Parquet/file outputs, and creates a manifest with batch ID, mode, watermark, row counts, and checksums. You will design failure and watermark behavior before relying on incremental mode.

## 2. Why it matters

A batch is the unit of movement, retry, audit, and reconciliation. Without a stable batch ID and manifest, a cloud upload is just a collection of files whose origin and completeness cannot be proved.

## 3. Words to know

| Term | Plain-language definition |
| --- | --- |
| Extraction | Reading data out of a source without yet applying business transformation. |
| Full extraction | Read the complete selected source scope. |
| Incremental extraction | Read rows new/changed after a stored source position. |
| High-water mark | Latest source timestamp/position fully committed by a successful batch. |
| Tie-breaker | Second key used when many rows share a timestamp. |
| Manifest | Batch inventory with counts, checksums, paths, mode, and status. |
| Parquet | Columnar file format preserving types efficiently. |
| Checksum | SHA-256 file fingerprint. |
| Atomic handoff | Consumer sees a complete batch, not partially written files. |
| Idempotency | Safe repeat behavior for the same logical extraction window. |
| Batch status | RUNNING/SUCCESS/FAILED evidence. |
| Partial failure | Some files written before the process stops. |

## 4. What must already be completed

Both source databases are populated/reconciled; file feeds exist; `.env` works; `.venv` active; enough disk space is available.

## 5. Applications to open

| Application | How to open it | Why it is open |
| --- | --- | --- |
| VS Code | Open extractor, manifest examples, and runbook. | Understand logic before execution. |
| Windows PowerShell | Repository root with `.venv` active. | Run full/incremental extract and checks. |
| SSMS and pgAdmin | Source contexts. | Verify watermark/update columns and independent counts. |
| File Explorer | Open generated batch folder. | Confirm immutable folder shape before upload. |

## 6. Exact click-by-click steps

> **Beginner rhythm:** Read the whole step. Confirm the application and location. Perform only that step. Verify the visible result. Record an error before attempting a fix.

## 7. Exact commands, one code block at a time

## 8. Where each command runs

Never infer the execution location from the code language. The command headings above identify the application and folder/database/catalog. Before every PowerShell command, run `Get-Location`; before SQL, verify the selected database; before Spark, print the catalog/schema/batch widgets.

## TEACHING EXAMPLE

The following small example or reference pattern explains the concept before you attempt Northstar-specific work. Read it, then complete **MY TASK** without copying the answer.

### Line-by-line code explanation

| Line or action | Meaning | Why it belongs here |
| --- | --- | --- |
| python -m scripts.extraction.extract_local_sources --mode full --file-feed-dir datasets\sample\files --output-root datasets\raw | Reads local sources and writes one timestamped batch folder. | A full baseline is the safest first handoff. |
| Get-ChildItem datasets\raw -Directory \| Sort-Object LastWriteTime -Descending \| Select-Object -First 1 FullName, Name, LastWriteTime | Finds the newest batch folder without guessing its timestamp. | The exact folder name becomes workflow batch ID. |
| Get-Content datasets\raw\EXT-YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ\batch_manifest.json | Prints manifest. | You should inspect evidence before upload. |
| Get-FileHash datasets\raw\EXT-YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ\sqlserver\orders.parquet -Algorithm SHA256 | Computes SHA-256 independently. | Proves local bytes match manifest. |
| SELECT COUNT_BIG(*) AS orders, MAX(updated_at) AS max_updated_at FROM erp.orders; | Gets independent source count and candidate watermark. | Manifest must reconcile to source and watermarks need evidence. |
| SELECT COUNT(*) AS sessions, MAX(created_at) AS max_created_at FROM digital.web_sessions; | Gets digital count and event/source position evidence. | PostgreSQL tables may not share the same update column strategy. |

### Incremental decision rule

A generic `WHERE updated_at > watermark` is not valid for every table: some tables have only `created_at`, snapshots use a business date, events may be append-only, and file feeds use filenames/dates/checksums. A production-ready extractor stores a watermark per source object and may use `(updated_at, primary_key)` to avoid equal-timestamp gaps.

### Failure rule

Write to a unique batch folder, keep status FAILED on exception, do not publish/upload it as trusted, and do not advance the committed watermark. A later run can retry the same logical bounds with a new attempt ID or safely replace the failed folder under an explicit policy.

## MY TASK

Run/reconcile a full batch, independently verify one checksum, simulate one safe failure, and refactor/design per-table incremental metadata with a tie-breaker for at least orders and web events.

## STARTER SKELETON

```yaml
# config/incremental_sources.example.yml
sources:
  - source_system: SQLSERVER_ERP
    table: erp.orders
    watermark_column: updated_at
    tie_breaker_column: order_id
    last_success_value: TODO(USER)
    last_success_tie_breaker: TODO(USER)
  - source_system: POSTGRES_DIGITAL
    table: digital.web_events
    strategy: append_only
    watermark_column: event_timestamp
    tie_breaker_column: event_id
    last_success_value: TODO(USER)

# TODO(USER): state when values are committed and how deleted rows are handled.
```

**Acceptance criteria:** One full batch has exact source/file reconciliation and checksum proof; failed batch behavior is recorded; incremental design is per table with committed watermark/tie-breaker policy.

## HINT 1 — CONCEPT

 Watermark is a success checkpoint, not simply MAX(source) at process start.
## HINT 2 — PSEUDOCODE
 Use the primary key as a tie-breaker when timestamps can repeat.
## HINT 3 — NEAR-COMPLETE PATTERN
 Adapt the manifest structure already written; add attempt/status/watermark metadata before changing extraction filters.

## 13. Expected files or output

- `datasets/raw/EXT-.../` with sqlserver, postgres, files, manifest.
- Source-to-extract count matrix.
- Independent checksum match.
- FAILED practice manifest/evidence.
- Per-table incremental strategy document or config skeleton.

## 14. How to verify

- Every manifest file exists and hash matches.
- Full counts equal source counts.
- Failed attempt is not labeled SUCCESS.
- No watermark was advanced from failed attempt.
- Exact batch ID is ready for volume upload.

## 15. Automated tests

- Manifest schema/required fields test (add as user task).
- Checksum recomputation.
- Source count SQL reconciliation.
- Incremental boundary tests with equal timestamps and no-change rerun.

## 16. Common errors and exact fixes

| Message/symptom | Likely cause | Exact diagnostic | Safe fix | Verify |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| updated_at column not found | Generic incremental filter applied to a table without that column. | Inspect data dictionary/source schema. | Use per-table strategy and column mapping; full mode until implemented. | Each query uses valid source column. |
| Manifest FAILED | Source/file/permission/write error occurred. | Read error field and terminal exception. | Fix root cause; do not upload partial batch; rerun. | New complete SUCCESS batch reconciles. |
| Checksum differs | File changed, wrong path, or text transfer altered bytes. | Compare size/time/path; recompute local and uploaded copy later. | Use immutable binary upload and exact batch folder. | Hashes match. |
| Parquet package error | pyarrow missing/wrong environment. | `python -m pip show pyarrow`; interpreter path. | Install requirements in `.venv`. | Small Parquet write/read succeeds. |
| Disk space failure | Output/portfolio scale too large. | `Get-PSDrive -Name C` and batch size. | Use quick/small, clear only known failed/generated folders after backup. | Full batch completes. |

For deeper tool-specific diagnosis, use [`the troubleshooting index near the end of this workbook`](#complete-troubleshooting-index).

## 17. Explain it in your own words

1. Why is a manifest more than a file list?
2. When should a watermark advance?
3. Why might `(timestamp, key)` be safer than timestamp alone?
4. What happens to a partial failed batch?

Write your answers in [`the learning-journal fields in this phase`](the learning-journal fields in this phase). Do not copy the wording above.

## 18. Mini quiz

1. Which extraction mode should establish the first baseline?
2. What does a checksum prove and not prove?
3. Why does one generic updated_at filter fail across these sources?

Record your answers before opening the answer key.

## 19. Screenshot checkpoint

Capture the SUCCESS manifest, source count queries, and matching checksum. Also capture the safe FAILED attempt status without exposing credentials.

Save the image under `docs/images/` with a descriptive filename. Check that no credential, token, password, or unnecessary personal account detail is visible.

## 20. Git checkpoint and suggested commit message

Run `git status`, review the Source Control diff in VS Code, stage only the intended files, then commit:

```text
feat: extract manifest-driven local source batches
```

Push the feature branch only after tests pass.

## 21. Completion checklist

Use one status per item: `Not started`, `In progress`, `Verified by me`, or `Needs troubleshooting`.

- [ ] Full batch extracted — [STATUS]
- [ ] All files/counts reconciled — [STATUS]
- [ ] Checksum independently verified — [STATUS]
- [ ] Failure behavior tested — [STATUS]
- [ ] Watermark commit rule explained — [STATUS]
- [ ] Per-table incremental design completed — [STATUS]
- [ ] Batch ready for Databricks upload — [STATUS]

#### Folder-creation decision branches

##### If the folder is created

Run `Test-Path -LiteralPath ".\scripts" -PathType Container` and require `True`.

##### If PowerShell says the folder already exists

Do not delete or recreate it. Run `Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath ".\scripts" -Force`, inspect its existing files, and preserve them. Continue only when the existing folder is the intended path.

##### If the parent path does not exist

Return to the parent-folder tutorial. Create and verify one parent level at a time; do not create the entire future tree in one command.

#### Verify the folder

1. Run `Test-Path ".\scripts" -PathType Container`.
2. Require the output `True` before creating a child file.
3. Remember: Git does not track an empty folder by itself; the folder becomes visible in Git history when a tracked file is added.

### Optional reference answer for `scripts/extraction/extract_local_sources.py`

Attempt the file construction first. This reference is learning material, not evidence that you created or ran the file.

**Language:** Python  
**Exact file:** `scripts/extraction/extract_local_sources.py`  
**Purpose:** executable Python logic.  
**Inputs:** The requirements, configuration, source data, or upstream objects described in Phase 7.  
**Expected outputs:** The file's declared objects, logs, tables, checks, or documentation when the user later runs or reads it.

```python
"""Extract local SQL Server, PostgreSQL, and file feeds for Track A."""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import logging
import shutil
from datetime import UTC, datetime
from pathlib import Path

import pandas as pd
from sqlalchemy import text

from scripts.utilities.config import load_environment
from scripts.utilities.database import postgres_engine, sqlserver_engine
from scripts.utilities.logging_utils import configure_logging

LOGGER = logging.getLogger("northstar.extract")
SQLSERVER_TABLES = ["customers", "addresses", "products", "product_categories", "suppliers", "stores", "employees", "orders", "order_items", "payments", "shipments", "inventory_transactions", "inventory_snapshots"]
POSTGRES_TABLES = ["web_users", "web_sessions", "web_events", "campaigns", "campaign_touchpoints", "marketing_spend"]


def checksum(path: Path) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()


def extract_table(connection, query: str, output: Path) -> dict[str, object]:
    frame = pd.read_sql_query(text(query), connection)
    output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    frame.to_parquet(output, index=False)
    return {"file": output.as_posix(), "rows": len(frame), "sha256": checksum(output)}


def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--mode", choices=["full", "incremental"], default="full")
    parser.add_argument("--watermark", default="1900-01-01T00:00:00")
    parser.add_argument("--file-feed-dir", type=Path, default=Path("datasets/sample/files"))
    parser.add_argument("--output-root", type=Path, default=Path("datasets/raw"))
    args = parser.parse_args()
    configure_logging(); load_environment()
    now = datetime.now(UTC)
    batch_id = f"EXT-{now:%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ}"
    batch_root = args.output_root / batch_id
    manifest: dict[str, object] = {"batch_id": batch_id, "started_at_utc": now.isoformat(), "mode": args.mode, "watermark": args.watermark, "files": []}
    sqlserver_filter = "" if args.mode == "full" else " WHERE updated_at > :watermark"
    postgres_filter = "" if args.mode == "full" else " WHERE updated_at > :watermark"
    params = {"watermark": args.watermark}
    try:
        with sqlserver_engine().connect() as connection:
            for table in SQLSERVER_TABLES:
                query = f"SELECT * FROM erp.{table}{sqlserver_filter}"
                frame = pd.read_sql_query(text(query), connection, params=params)
                path = batch_root / "sqlserver" / f"{table}.parquet"
                path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True); frame.to_parquet(path, index=False)
                manifest["files"].append({"source_system": "sqlserver", "table": table, "file": path.as_posix(), "rows": len(frame), "sha256": checksum(path)})
        with postgres_engine().connect() as connection:
            for table in POSTGRES_TABLES:
                query = f"SELECT * FROM digital.{table}{postgres_filter}"
                frame = pd.read_sql_query(text(query), connection, params=params)
                path = batch_root / "postgres" / f"{table}.parquet"
                path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True); frame.to_parquet(path, index=False)
                manifest["files"].append({"source_system": "postgres", "table": table, "file": path.as_posix(), "rows": len(frame), "sha256": checksum(path)})
        for source in args.file_feed_dir.glob("*"):
            if source.is_file():
                target = batch_root / "files" / source.name
                target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True); shutil.copy2(source, target)
                row_count = sum(1 for _ in target.open("rb")) - (1 if target.suffix == ".csv" else 0)
                manifest["files"].append({"source_system": "files", "file": target.as_posix(), "rows": max(0, row_count), "sha256": checksum(target)})
        manifest["status"] = "SUCCESS"
    except Exception as exc:
        manifest["status"] = "FAILED"; manifest["error"] = str(exc)
        raise
    finally:
        batch_root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        (batch_root / "batch_manifest.json").write_text(json.dumps(manifest, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
        LOGGER.info("Wrote manifest %s", (batch_root / "batch_manifest.json").resolve())


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

```python
"""Small checksum functions used by extraction and reconciliation scripts."""
from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
from pathlib import Path


def sha256_file(path: str | Path) -> str:
    """Return the SHA-256 checksum of a file without loading it all into memory."""
    file_path = Path(path)
    digest = hashlib.sha256()
    with file_path.open("rb") as handle:
        for chunk in iter(lambda: handle.read(1024 * 1024), b""):
            digest.update(chunk)
    return digest.hexdigest()
```

### Optional reference answer for `scripts/utilities/database.py`

Attempt the file construction first. This reference is learning material, not evidence that you created or ran the file.

**Language:** Python  
**Exact file:** `scripts/utilities/database.py`  
**Purpose:** executable Python logic.  
**Inputs:** The requirements, configuration, source data, or upstream objects described in Phase 7.  
**Expected outputs:** The file's declared objects, logs, tables, checks, or documentation when the user later runs or reads it.

```python
"""Safe SQLAlchemy connection factories for local SQL Server and PostgreSQL."""
from __future__ import annotations

from urllib.parse import quote_plus

from sqlalchemy import Engine, create_engine

from scripts.utilities.config import required_env


def sqlserver_engine() -> Engine:
    """Create a SQL Server engine using values from .env, never hard-coded secrets."""
    server = required_env("SQLSERVER_HOST")
    database = required_env("SQLSERVER_SOURCE_DATABASE")
    driver = required_env("SQLSERVER_ODBC_DRIVER")
    trusted = required_env("SQLSERVER_TRUSTED_CONNECTION").lower() == "yes"
    trust_certificate = required_env("SQLSERVER_TRUST_SERVER_CERTIFICATE")

    if trusted:
        odbc = (
            f"DRIVER={{{driver}}};SERVER={server};DATABASE={database};"
            f"Trusted_Connection=yes;TrustServerCertificate={trust_certificate};"
        )
    else:
        username = required_env("SQLSERVER_USERNAME")
        password = required_env("SQLSERVER_PASSWORD")
        odbc = (
            f"DRIVER={{{driver}}};SERVER={server};DATABASE={database};"
            f"UID={username};PWD={password};TrustServerCertificate={trust_certificate};"
        )
    return create_engine(f"mssql+pyodbc:///?odbc_connect={quote_plus(odbc)}", future=True)


def sqlserver_warehouse_engine() -> Engine:
    """Create a SQL Server warehouse engine using the warehouse database name."""
    import os

    original = os.environ.get("SQLSERVER_SOURCE_DATABASE")
    os.environ["SQLSERVER_SOURCE_DATABASE"] = required_env("SQLSERVER_WAREHOUSE_DATABASE")
    try:
        return sqlserver_engine()
    finally:
        if original is None:
            os.environ.pop("SQLSERVER_SOURCE_DATABASE", None)
        else:
            os.environ["SQLSERVER_SOURCE_DATABASE"] = original


def postgres_engine() -> Engine:
    """Create a PostgreSQL engine using values from .env."""
    user = required_env("POSTGRES_USER")
    password = quote_plus(required_env("POSTGRES_PASSWORD"))
    host = required_env("POSTGRES_HOST")
    port = required_env("POSTGRES_PORT")
    database = required_env("POSTGRES_DATABASE")
    return create_engine(
        f"postgresql+psycopg://{user}:{password}@{host}:{port}/{database}", future=True
    )
```

## Lesson 7.5 — Verify, troubleshoot, commit, teach back, and stop safely

## What your screen should look like before starting

The Phase 7 outputs are visible, all runs are finished, open files are saved, and you can state the active branch and execution context. Any error you encountered has a recorded message and has not been hidden by deleting evidence.

## Design decision — CSV versus Parquet extracts

**Question:**  
Which local interchange format should the beginner path use?

**Options considered:**

- CSV/JSON plus manifest.
- Parquet.
- Direct JDBC from Databricks to localhost.

**Beginner path selected:**  
Use CSV and JSON with manifests and checksums for Track A.

**Why this path was selected:**  
The files are inspectable with basic tools and make schema/quoting issues visible.

**Tradeoff:**  
They are larger and less type-safe than Parquet.

**What a company might do instead:**  
Production pipelines often use Parquet/Delta in cloud object storage and CDC or direct networked ingestion.

**How to explain this in an interview:**  
I chose inspectable files for the local handoff, added checksums and manifests, and documented Parquet as a scale-oriented alternative.


## Design decision — Full versus incremental loading

**Question:**  
When should the extractor read every source row and when should it read only new or changed rows?

**Options considered:**

- Full extraction for every run.
- Incremental extraction from the first run.
- A full baseline followed by audited incremental batches.

**Beginner path selected:**  
Create and reconcile one full baseline, then use incremental extraction with a timestamp-plus-key boundary and advance the watermark only after success.

**Why this path was selected:**  
The baseline proves completeness and supplies a recovery point; incremental batches then teach efficiency, replay safety, and late/change handling.

**Tradeoff:**  
Two modes require more tests, metadata, and correction logic than a full-only learning pipeline.

**What a company might do instead:**  
A company may use CDC, transaction-log positions, event streams, snapshot isolation, backfill tooling, and automated restart/reconciliation controls.

**How to explain this in an interview:**  
I established a full baseline before introducing incremental watermarks so efficiency did not replace completeness or recoverability.


## If you see Result A

The full baseline reconciles and the incremental batch advances its watermark only after success. Record the exact result, perform the named independent verification, and continue only when the gate is satisfied.

## If you see Result B

No rows qualify, duplicate timestamps create an ambiguous boundary, or a failed batch has partial output. Treat this as information, not permission to delete or overwrite. Follow the branch-specific diagnostic in the current action, preserve evidence, and continue only after the state is understood.

## If you see an error

Read the first meaningful error line, redact secrets, and verify the application, path, branch, server/database, catalog/schema, batch ID, parameters, version/tier, and object name. Run the smallest observational check first. Do not reset Git history, drop data, disable a rule, force-push, or replace the target merely to make the error disappear.

### Interpret `git status --short`

- `??` means untracked: Git sees a new path but it is not staged.
- ` M` means modified in the working tree but not staged.
- `M ` means the staged version differs from the last commit.
- `MM` means a staged version exists and the file has additional unstaged edits.
- `A ` means staged as a new file.
- `D` means deletion; stop and investigate unless deletion is deliberate.
- `R` means rename; inspect both old and new paths.
- A blank result means the working tree is clean. It does not prove database, Databricks, or Power BI work occurred.

### Verify on GitHub

1. CLICK: Open the repository page in a browser.
2. CLICK: Open the branch selector above the file list.
3. TYPE THIS: The exact branch name returned locally.

### Push-rejected recovery

If Git says the remote contains work you do not have, do not use `--force`. Run `git fetch origin`, inspect `git log --oneline --graph --decorate --all -20`, then rebase or merge only after understanding the divergence. Resolve conflicts one file at a time, run tests again, and push normally. A rejection protects remote work; it is not permission to overwrite it.

6. Design choice: Explain one tradeoff of Track A and one production alternative.
7. Code reading: Why are input, accepted, rejected, and deduplicated counts recorded separately?
8. Ownership: Which status may you select only after personally performing and inspecting the verification?

---

## Mini quiz answer key and explanations

**1. B.** This phase is ordered after its prerequisites so its output has a trustworthy input. A is wrong because order is intentional; C is wrong because later phases depend on the handoff; D is wrong because screenshots follow verification.

**2. False.** Lack of an error proves only that the application accepted something; context and independent verification still matter.

**3. Grain.** Grain is the precise meaning of one row. A key identifies a row, but it does not by itself state the row’s business meaning.

**4. `Get-Location`.** It shows the shell’s current folder. `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` separately verifies the repository root when inside a clone.

**5.** Check application, folder/path, branch, server/database, catalog/schema, batch ID, parameters, source/target grain, filter context, version/tier differences, and the first meaningful error. Destructive changes are not a diagnostic step.

**6.** Track A has manual upload/download boundaries and batch latency. A production alternative is routable private connectivity with cloud object storage/managed warehouse, identities, and automated orchestration.

**7.** Separate counts make every row outcome explainable. A single final count can hide silent drops, duplicates, or records that moved to quarantine.

**8. `Verified by me` / `VERIFIED BY USER`.** `PLANNED`, `CREATED BY USER`, and `RUN BY USER` describe earlier states; only inspected evidence supports verification.

# Phase 8 — Configure Databricks, governed storage, notebooks, and compute

[Back to the master table of contents](#master-table-of-contents)

**Track:** Track A required  
**Status when first opened:** `PLANNED`  
**Completion rule:** The phase is not complete because its instructions exist. Mark it `VERIFIED BY USER` only after you perform the work, inspect the output, and save evidence.

## Why this phase happens now

**Earlier work this phase depends on:** A valid local batch, manifest, and verified Databricks environment.  
**What would go wrong if it happened earlier:** You would create objects without a verified requirement, valid upstream input, protected repository state, or known execution environment.  
**Later work that depends on it:** Phase 9 ingests that exact batch into append-only raw Delta tables.  
**Decision being made:** Choose and verify the simplest local-first method that teaches the professional concept without pretending that local services are publicly reachable.  
**Alternatives:** A company could use managed cloud databases, infrastructure as code, service principals, direct JDBC publication, deployment bundles, or streaming. Those options are discussed as tradeoffs, not substituted silently.  
**Beginner path selected:** Track A: local SQL Server and PostgreSQL, Python batch extracts, manual governed upload to Databricks, Delta Bronze/Silver/Gold, manual verified export, local SQL Server warehouse, and Power BI Import.  
**Reason for the order:** Requirements become source decisions; sources become generated data; source data becomes extraction batches; batches become Bronze; Bronze becomes Silver; Silver becomes Gold; Gold becomes warehouse and Power BI input.

## Three-level explanation of the phase

### Level 1 — Child-simple explanation

Imagine building a store from labeled boxes. This phase handles one box, checks that the label is correct, and makes sure the next box receives the right thing. You do not pour all boxes together and hope the result is understandable.

### Level 2 — Northstar Retail project explanation

Phase 8 creates the specific Northstar Retail files, database objects, transformations, tests, model objects, or evidence described in the lessons. Every output keeps a visible connection to its source and batch so you can trace an order, customer, product, campaign, return, shipment, or inventory record.

### Level 3 — Professional explanation

This phase establishes a controlled boundary in an end-to-end batch platform. It defines contracts, execution context, idempotency behavior, quality expectations, evidence, and handoff artifacts so the downstream layer can be reproduced and reviewed independently.

## Applications to open

Web browser, Databricks workspace, VS Code, and File Explorer. Open only the application needed for the immediate action. Extra windows increase the chance of typing a command into the wrong context.

## Lesson 8.2 — Perform the notebook-guided actions one at a time

## What your screen should look like before starting

## Retained phase lesson, exercises, rules, and expected results

> **Track:** Track A required  
> **Ownership status at start:** Workbook instructions exist; your execution is not yet verified.  
> **Evidence rule:** Replace placeholders only after the verification steps pass.

## 1. What you are building

An available Databricks workspace configured with a usable catalog, `landing`, `bronze`, `silver`, `gold`, and `quality` schemas, a governed volume for Track A files, Git-friendly source notebooks, and a successful `00_environment_check` run using the exact uploaded batch ID.

## 2. Why it matters

Databricks is the remote lakehouse and orchestration environment. Before transforming data, you must prove identity, object permissions, storage paths, Spark, parameters, and Delta read/write. This isolates environment failures from business-code failures.

## 3. Words to know

| Term | Plain-language definition |
| --- | --- |
| Workspace | Databricks environment containing notebooks, data, compute, SQL, and Jobs. |
| Compute | Resources that execute Spark/SQL. Free Edition commonly provides serverless managed compute subject to quotas. |
| Catalog | Top governed namespace in Unity Catalog. |
| Schema | Namespace below a catalog for tables/volumes. |
| Volume | Governed file storage for non-tabular files and batch handoff. |
| Notebook | Document with executable cells and Markdown. |
| Git folder | Databricks workspace folder linked to a Git repository; older documentation may call it Repos. |
| Cluster | User-configured Spark compute; availability varies by tier. |
| SQL warehouse | Compute endpoint for Databricks SQL and BI queries. |
| Secret | Protected credential value referenced without printing it. |
| Widget | Notebook input parameter. |
| Task value | Small output passed/recorded between Job tasks. |
| Serverless | Provider-managed compute; feature/quotas vary by workspace. |
| Catalog Explorer | UI for catalogs, schemas, tables, volumes, and permissions. |

## 4. What must already be completed

A verified SUCCESS extraction batch exists. Databricks account/workspace availability and current limitations were reviewed in Phase 2. The feature branch is pushed if using Git folder integration.

## 5. Applications to open

| Application | How to open it | Why it is open |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Web browser | Open the Databricks workspace URL. | Create/inspect workspace objects and run notebook. |
| VS Code | Open `databricks/notebooks/00_environment_check.py` and `databricks/README.md`. | Understand every cell before importing/running. |
| File Explorer | Open exact local `datasets/raw/EXT-...` batch. | Upload the correct immutable folder. |
| Windows PowerShell | Repository root. | Read manifest and verify batch ID/checksums before upload. |

## 6. Exact click-by-click steps

> **Beginner rhythm:** Read the whole step. Confirm the application and location. Perform only that step. Verify the visible result. Record an error before attempting a fix.

## 7. Exact commands, one code block at a time

## 8. Where each command runs

Never infer the execution location from the code language. The command headings above identify the application and folder/database/catalog. Before every PowerShell command, run `Get-Location`; before SQL, verify the selected database; before Spark, print the catalog/schema/batch widgets.

## TEACHING EXAMPLE

The following small example or reference pattern explains the concept before you attempt Northstar-specific work. Read it, then complete **MY TASK** without copying the answer.

### Line-by-line code explanation

| Line or action | Meaning | Why it belongs here |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $BatchId = 'EXT-YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ'; Get-Content "datasets\raw\$BatchId\batch_manifest.json" | Prints the local manifest before upload. | The remote parameter must match a complete local batch. |
| print(spark.version) | Prints Spark and resolved parameters/path. | Hidden defaults cause wrong-catalog and wrong-batch failures. |
| SHOW SCHEMAS IN northstar_retail; | Lists schemas in the chosen catalog. | Verifies namespaces independently of notebook variables. |
| dbutils.fs.ls(f"/Volumes/{catalog}/{landing_schema}/{volume}/{batch_id}") | Lists uploaded batch contents. | Proves compute can access the exact handoff. |
| SELECT * FROM northstar_retail.quality.environment_check ORDER BY checked_at_utc DESC LIMIT 10; | Reads the Delta test table written by Spark. | Proves table creation and SQL access. |

### Compute choice summary

- Use available serverless notebook/job compute for Track A when the workspace provides it.
- A SQL warehouse runs Databricks SQL and BI queries; it is not the same execution surface as a PySpark notebook task.
- Free Edition is quota-limited and, as verified on 2026-08-16, Jobs concurrency is limited; the documented graph stays below five parallel tasks. Verify current limits again when you run.

### Catalog fallback

If `CREATE CATALOG` is denied, do not request administrator rights merely for a name. Use a writable catalog, record it, and pass it consistently. The architecture is about governed namespaces, not the literal string `northstar_retail`.

## MY TASK

Create/identify the governed namespaces and volume, upload one exact SUCCESS batch, import/sync the notebooks, run `00_environment_check`, and document any tier/UI variance with a screenshot and official source.

## 13. Expected files or output

## 15. Automated tests

- No secret scanner finding in Git.

## 16. Common errors and exact fixes

| Message/symptom | Likely cause | Exact diagnostic | Safe fix | Verify |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| PERMISSION_DENIED creating catalog/schema/volume | Workspace identity lacks privilege. | Inspect object named in error; `SHOW CATALOGS`/grants if allowed. | Use permitted catalog/schema or request minimum grant; do not use admin token workaround. | Environment check writes table. |
| Batch path not found | Upload flattened/renamed/wrong parameter. | Volume browser; print batch_root; compare manifest ID. | Recreate exact folder structure and parameter. | ls returns contents. |
| Git folder authentication fails | Credential/provider/branch configuration issue. | Workspace user settings and official Git folder docs. | Use supported OAuth/PAT securely or manual import fallback. | Notebooks visible and current. |
| Compute unavailable/quota exceeded | Tier quota or temporary capacity. | Workspace banner/run error and limits page. | Use quick data, stop repeated retries, resume when quota permits; do not claim run. | Environment run completes. |
| Notebook creates wrong catalog | Default widgets not replaced. | Print widgets/current_catalog. | Set job/notebook parameters consistently; clean accidental disposable object only after review. | Objects live in recorded catalog. |

For deeper tool-specific diagnosis, use [`the troubleshooting index near the end of this workbook`](#complete-troubleshooting-index).

```markdown
# Databricks learning assets

- `notebooks/00...12`: Git-friendly Databricks source notebooks in execution order.
- `jobs/job_definition.example.yml`: version-controlled dependency map.

## Track A boundary

Your local SQL Server and PostgreSQL instances are not reachable from a cloud workspace simply because they use the name `localhost`. Track A therefore extracts locally, uploads a batch folder to a Unity Catalog volume, processes it in Databricks, and exports Gold files for local download. This manual boundary is intentional, honest, and inexpensive for learning.

## Workspace-specific placeholders

Replace catalog, schema, volume, user email, and batch ID values with resources that your workspace permits. Do not commit tokens or passwords. Read Phase 8 and Phase 14 before creating a Job.
```

### Optional reference answer for `databricks/notebooks/00_environment_check.py`

Attempt the file construction first. This reference is learning material, not evidence that you created or ran the file.

**Language:** Python  
**Exact file:** `databricks/notebooks/00_environment_check.py`  
**Purpose:** executable Python logic.  
**Inputs:** The requirements, configuration, source data, or upstream objects described in Phase 8.  
**Expected outputs:** The file's declared objects, logs, tables, checks, or documentation when the user later runs or reads it.

```python
# Databricks notebook source
# Northstar Retail End-to-End Data Platform
# This file is a Git-friendly Databricks source notebook.
# Track A reads files that you manually uploaded to a Unity Catalog volume.
# It never attempts to reach SQL Server or PostgreSQL on localhost.


# COMMAND ----------
# MAGIC %md
# MAGIC # 00 — Environment check
# MAGIC **Purpose:** verify Spark, parameters, catalog, schemas, volume access, and Delta read/write.
# MAGIC **Input:** widget values. **Output:** one disposable Delta test table and a task value.

# COMMAND ----------
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pyspark.sql import functions as F

for name, default in {
    "catalog": "northstar_retail",
    "landing_schema": "landing",
    "bronze_schema": "bronze",
    "silver_schema": "silver",
    "gold_schema": "gold",
    "quality_schema": "quality",
    "volume": "track_a_files",
    "batch_id": "MANUAL-REPLACE-ME",
}.items():
    dbutils.widgets.text(name, default)

catalog = dbutils.widgets.get("catalog")
landing_schema = dbutils.widgets.get("landing_schema")
bronze_schema = dbutils.widgets.get("bronze_schema")
silver_schema = dbutils.widgets.get("silver_schema")
gold_schema = dbutils.widgets.get("gold_schema")
quality_schema = dbutils.widgets.get("quality_schema")
volume = dbutils.widgets.get("volume")
batch_id = dbutils.widgets.get("batch_id")

if batch_id == "MANUAL-REPLACE-ME":
    raise ValueError("Set batch_id to the exact extraction folder name, such as EXT-20260815T180000Z.")

# COMMAND ----------
# Creating a catalog may require workspace permissions. If this fails, use a catalog you can access.
spark.sql(f"CREATE CATALOG IF NOT EXISTS `{catalog}`")
for schema_name in [landing_schema, bronze_schema, silver_schema, gold_schema, quality_schema]:
    spark.sql(f"CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS `{catalog}`.`{schema_name}`")
spark.sql(f"CREATE VOLUME IF NOT EXISTS `{catalog}`.`{landing_schema}`.`{volume}`")

volume_root = f"/Volumes/{catalog}/{landing_schema}/{volume}"
batch_root = f"{volume_root}/{batch_id}"
print({"catalog": catalog, "batch_root": batch_root, "spark_version": spark.version})

# COMMAND ----------
# Write and read a tiny Delta table. This proves Spark and the Gold schema work.
test_table = f"`{catalog}`.`{quality_schema}`.`environment_check`"
test_df = spark.createDataFrame([(batch_id, datetime.now(timezone.utc), "PASS")], ["batch_id", "checked_at_utc", "status"])
(test_df.write.format("delta").mode("append").saveAsTable(test_table))
assert spark.table(test_table).filter(F.col("batch_id") == batch_id).count() >= 1

# Verify the uploaded batch folder. It is normal for this to fail before you upload extracts.
try:
    uploaded = dbutils.fs.ls(batch_root)
    print(f"Found {len(uploaded)} objects in {batch_root}")
except Exception as exc:
    raise FileNotFoundError(
        f"Databricks cannot find {batch_root}. Upload the entire local extraction batch folder "
        "to the volume and keep the batch folder name unchanged."
    ) from exc

# COMMAND ----------
dbutils.jobs.taskValues.set(key="environment_status", value="PASS")
dbutils.jobs.taskValues.set(key="batch_root", value=batch_root)
print("ENVIRONMENT CHECK PASSED")
```

## Lesson 8.4 completion checklist

- [ ] Every required object was built separately — [STATUS]
- [ ] Every object has a declared responsibility/grain — [STATUS]
- [ ] Inputs and outputs were inspected — [STATUS]
- [ ] A rerun or alternate-result branch was tested where applicable — [STATUS]

## Safe stopping point

Stop only after the active command, database transaction, Databricks cell/Job, Python process, warehouse load, or Power BI refresh finishes. Save all files and the Power BI project. Record uncommitted Git changes and exact resume action. Resume at [Lesson 8.5](#phase-8-lesson-5).


<a id="phase-8-lesson-5"></a>
## Lesson 8.5 — Verify, troubleshoot, commit, teach back, and stop safely

## What your screen should look like before starting

The Phase 8 outputs are visible, all runs are finished, open files are saved, and you can state the active branch and execution context. Any error you encountered has a recorded message and has not been hidden by deleting evidence.

## Design decision — Databricks compute and storage

**Question:**  
Which UI and compute path should the learner use when tiers differ?

**Options considered:**

- Serverless when available.
- Classic compute when allowed.
- Skip execution.

**Beginner path selected:**  
Use the compute option the workspace actually offers and a governed volume or My Files fallback.

**Why this path was selected:**  
It is tier-aware and avoids claiming unavailable features.

**Tradeoff:**  
Free or trial quotas and labels vary.

**What a company might do instead:**  
Enterprises define Unity Catalog objects, external locations, policies, service principals, and job clusters.

**How to explain this in an interview:**  
I verified the workspace tier first and selected an available compute/storage path while keeping object names and validation contracts consistent.


## Design decision — Databricks storage options

**Question:**  
Where should Track A batch files be placed when workspace features and permissions vary?

**Options considered:**

- A governed Unity Catalog volume.
- Workspace or user file storage available to the account.
- An external cloud storage location.

**Beginner path selected:**  
Use a governed volume when permitted; otherwise use the workspace-supported user-file fallback and record the exact path, limitation, and cleanup procedure.

**Why this path was selected:**  
The path remains observable and tier-aware without inventing permissions. A governed volume teaches catalog/schema ownership while the fallback keeps the learning path usable.

**Tradeoff:**  
Fallback storage can have tighter quotas, weaker sharing, or different governance and should not be presented as the enterprise target.

**What a company might do instead:**  
Use external locations and cloud object storage with storage credentials, managed identities, access controls, lifecycle policies, and infrastructure as code.

**How to explain this in an interview:**  
I selected the most governed storage object my workspace actually allowed and parameterized the path so the pipeline contract survived tier differences.


## If you see Result A

A writable catalog/schema/storage path and available compute run the environment check. Record the exact result, perform the named independent verification, and continue only when the gate is satisfied.

## If you see Result B

The workspace exposes a different tier/UI, lacks permission, or offers a different compute/storage object. Treat this as information, not permission to delete or overwrite. Follow the branch-specific diagnostic in the current action, preserve evidence, and continue only after the state is understood.

## If you see an error

Read the first meaningful error line, redact secrets, and verify the application, path, branch, server/database, catalog/schema, batch ID, parameters, version/tier, and object name. Run the smallest observational check first. Do not reset Git history, drop data, disable a rule, force-push, or replace the target merely to make the error disappear.


## Phase-specific verification gate

- [ ] Required files/objects exist in the exact location.
- [ ] I personally created or configured them.
- [ ] I ran the phase commands in the documented context.
- [ ] I inspected the output rather than relying on a green icon alone.
- [ ] Counts, keys, relationships, measures, checksums, statuses, or settings meet the declared contract.
- [ ] Same-batch/rerun behavior is known where applicable.
- [ ] A controlled failure or realistic alternate-result branch was tested safely where applicable.
- [ ] No password, token, or secret appears in tracked files, screenshots, notebook output, terminal history pasted into documentation, or staged changes.
- [ ] Actual verified result: `[ENTER VERIFIED RESULT]`.

## Point-of-failure troubleshooting record

**Exact or representative error message:**  
`[PASTE THE FIRST MEANINGFUL ERROR, WITH SECRETS REDACTED]`

**What it means in plain language:**  
`[WRITE YOUR INTERPRETATION]`

**Most likely cause:**  
`[WRITE ONE TESTABLE HYPOTHESIS]`

**What not to do:**  
Do not delete data, drop databases, reset Git history, force-push, disable constraints, edit raw evidence, change a quality threshold, or expose credentials merely to make the symptom disappear.

**First diagnostic action:**  
`[ENTER THE SMALLEST OBSERVATIONAL CHECK]`

**How to read the diagnostic result:**  
`[RESULT A MEANS... / RESULT B MEANS...]`

**Safest fix:**  
`[ENTER THE NARROW FIX]`

**Alternative fix when applicable:**  
`[ENTER OR N/A]`

**How to verify the fix:**  
`[ENTER THE INDEPENDENT RECHECK]`

**How to return to the main tutorial:**  
Resume at the exact action number that failed; do not skip its verification gate.

## Screenshot checkpoint

**Application(s) that should be visible:** Web browser, Databricks workspace, VS Code, and File Explorer.  
**Window/panel:** Show workspace/catalog/schema/volume/compute plus successful environment-check output.  
**Sensitive information to hide:** Passwords, tokens, connection strings, email addresses, cloud account IDs, unnecessary Windows profile details, and any secret revealed by an error.  
**Include:** The object name, batch/run ID when relevant, result/status, and enough surrounding UI to prove which application and layer is shown.  
**Crop out:** Unrelated desktop windows, notification previews, bookmarks, chat, and empty background.  
**Recommended filename:** `docs/images/phase08_configure-databricks-governed-storage-notebooks-and-com_verified.png`.  
**Recommended repository folder:** `docs/images/`.  
**README placement:** The section describing Phase 8's verified result; do not use the image before the result is actually verified.  
**What it proves:** The visible state existed under the shown context. It does not prove hidden rows, other batches, every filter combination, or a later run.

`[ADD YOUR VERIFIED SCREENSHOT HERE]`


## Git checkpoint after the verified Phase 8 changes

Do not use `git add .` until you understand that it stages every matching change under the current directory, including files you did not intend. Prefer targeted staging after inspecting status and diffs.

### Save open work

1. PRESS: In VS Code, press Ctrl+K, then S if you use **Save All**, or press Ctrl+S in every modified editor.
2. In Power BI, press Ctrl+S and confirm the local file location.
3. Wait for database, Python, Databricks, and refresh operations to finish; Git does not capture uncommitted database/cloud state.

**Application:**

2. LOOK FOR: Confirm the current location matches `The selected Databricks workspace, catalog, schema, volume, notebook, or Job named in the action.` or the more specific location stated below.

6. LOOK FOR: Wait until the busy indicator stops and a new prompt, result grid, cell output, or status badge appears.
7. DO NOT CONTINUE UNTIL: Compare the result with the expected shape and complete the verification action.

**Command or code (PowerShell):**

```powershell
git rev-parse --show-toplevel
```

**Where to enter it:**  
VS Code integrated PowerShell terminal. Do not enter terminal commands into a source-code file and do not paste expected output back into the editor.

**Plain-English translation:**  
This instruction asks the selected application to perform exactly the operation named by its leading keyword, using the following names, paths, clauses, flags, and values as inputs.

**What each part means:**

- **Line 1:** `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` — `git` calls the Git version-control program; `rev-parse` is a name, keyword, argument, identifier, or literal whose project-specific role is described in the surrounding explanation; `--show` is a command option or flag; its exact behavior is defined beside the command; `-toplevel` is a command option or flag; its exact behavior is defined beside the command

**Does it change anything?**  
This is intended to inspect or validate state rather than change it.

**Is it safe to rerun?**  
Normally safe to rerun because it is observational, but still confirm the execution location first.

**What should happen:**  
The application should finish without an unhandled error and display a result that corresponds to the command's stated purpose.

**Expected example:**

> Your exact values may differ. The exact values may differ. Expect either a version/path/status line, a query result grid, or a clearly labeled completion message that matches the command purpose.

Your Windows username, installation version, server instance, database owner, generated identifier, batch timestamp, row count, Databricks interface label, Power BI ribbon position, and terminal theme can differ. A different object name, wrong branch, wrong database, missing target, unexpected duplicate, or failed quality status is not harmless.

**How to verify success:**  
Run or perform the smallest independent check named in the lesson. For a path, use `Get-Location` or `Test-Path`; for Git, use `git status` and `git branch --show-current`; for SQL, run a metadata or row-count query; for Databricks, inspect the target object and cell output; for Power BI, compare a filtered DAX result to SQL.

**Do not continue unless:**  
The result is visible, understandable, and recorded as `RUN BY USER` or `VERIFIED BY USER`. Displaying this workbook does not count as execution.

**Common mistake:**  
The most common mistake is running the right text in the wrong application, folder, database, catalog, schema, branch, or notebook language.

**Exact recovery:**  
Do not delete, reset, overwrite, or force-push. Read the first error line. Re-run the location check for this application. Confirm the current folder, branch, server/database, or Databricks catalog. Correct only the mismatched location or spelling, then retry this single command.

**What you just accomplished:**  
You executed and checked one controlled operation rather than treating a long script as a black box.

### Interpret `git status --short`

- `??` means untracked: Git sees a new path but it is not staged.
- ` M` means modified in the working tree but not staged.
- `M ` means the staged version differs from the last commit.
- `MM` means a staged version exists and the file has additional unstaged edits.
- `A ` means staged as a new file.
- `D` means deletion; stop and investigate unless deletion is deliberate.
- `R` means rename; inspect both old and new paths.
- A blank result means the working tree is clean. It does not prove database, Databricks, or Power BI work occurred.

Safe to rerun only after reading the idempotency note and confirming that the same batch, file, or object will not be duplicated.

**What should happen:**  
The application should finish without an unhandled error and display a result that corresponds to the command's stated purpose.

**Expected example:**

> Your exact values may differ. The exact values may differ. Expect either a version/path/status line, a query result grid, or a clearly labeled completion message that matches the command purpose.

**What may look different:**  
Your Windows username, installation version, server instance, database owner, generated identifier, batch timestamp, row count, Databricks interface label, Power BI ribbon position, and terminal theme can differ. A different object name, wrong branch, wrong database, missing target, unexpected duplicate, or failed quality status is not harmless.

**How to verify success:**  
Run or perform the smallest independent check named in the lesson. For a path, use `Get-Location` or `Test-Path`; for Git, use `git status` and `git branch --show-current`; for SQL, run a metadata or row-count query; for Databricks, inspect the target object and cell output; for Power BI, compare a filtered DAX result to SQL.

**Do not continue unless:**  
The result is visible, understandable, and recorded as `RUN BY USER` or `VERIFIED BY USER`. Displaying this workbook does not count as execution.

**Common mistake:**  
The most common mistake is running the right text in the wrong application, folder, database, catalog, schema, branch, or notebook language.

**Exact recovery:**  
Do not delete, reset, overwrite, or force-push. Read the first error line. Re-run the location check for this application. Confirm the current folder, branch, server/database, or Databricks catalog. Correct only the mismatched location or spelling, then retry this single command.

**What you just accomplished:**  
You executed and checked one controlled operation rather than treating a long script as a black box.

**How this connects to the project:**  
This verified state becomes a dependable input to the next Northstar Retail construction action.

### Push-rejected recovery

If Git says the remote contains work you do not have, do not use `--force`. Run `git fetch origin`, inspect `git log --oneline --graph --decorate --all -20`, then rebase or merge only after understanding the divergence. Resolve conflicts one file at a time, run tests again, and push normally. A rejection protects remote work; it is not permission to overwrite it.

## Mini quiz answer key and explanations

**1. B.** This phase is ordered after its prerequisites so its output has a trustworthy input. A is wrong because order is intentional; C is wrong because later phases depend on the handoff; D is wrong because screenshots follow verification.

**2. False.** Lack of an error proves only that the application accepted something; context and independent verification still matter.

**3. Grain.** Grain is the precise meaning of one row. A key identifies a row, but it does not by itself state the row’s business meaning.

**4. `Get-Location`.** It shows the shell’s current folder. `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` separately verifies the repository root when inside a clone.

**5.** Check application, folder/path, branch, server/database, catalog/schema, batch ID, parameters, source/target grain, filter context, version/tier differences, and the first meaningful error. Destructive changes are not a diagnostic step.

**6.** Track A has manual upload/download boundaries and batch latency. A production alternative is routable private connectivity with cloud object storage/managed warehouse, identities, and automated orchestration.

**7.** Separate counts make every row outcome explainable. A single final count can hide silent drops, duplicates, or records that moved to quarantine.

**8. `Verified by me` / `VERIFIED BY USER`.** `PLANNED`, `CREATED BY USER`, and `RUN BY USER` describe earlier states; only inspected evidence supports verification.

## Why this phase happens now

**Earlier work this phase depends on:** Bronze tables that preserve values and ingestion metadata.  
**What would go wrong if it happened earlier:** You would create objects without a verified requirement, valid upstream input, protected repository state, or known execution environment.  
**Later work that depends on it:** Phase 10 cleans, types, deduplicates, and quarantines Bronze records.  
**Decision being made:** Choose and verify the simplest local-first method that teaches the professional concept without pretending that local services are publicly reachable.  
**Alternatives:** A company could use managed cloud databases, infrastructure as code, service principals, direct JDBC publication, deployment bundles, or streaming. Those options are discussed as tradeoffs, not substituted silently.  
**Beginner path selected:** Track A: local SQL Server and PostgreSQL, Python batch extracts, manual governed upload to Databricks, Delta Bronze/Silver/Gold, manual verified export, local SQL Server warehouse, and Power BI Import.  
**Reason for the order:** Requirements become source decisions; sources become generated data; source data becomes extraction batches; batches become Bronze; Bronze becomes Silver; Silver becomes Gold; Gold becomes warehouse and Power BI input.

## Three-level explanation of the phase

### Level 1 — Child-simple explanation

Imagine building a store from labeled boxes. This phase handles one box, checks that the label is correct, and makes sure the next box receives the right thing. You do not pour all boxes together and hope the result is understandable.

### Level 2 — Northstar Retail project explanation

Phase 9 creates the specific Northstar Retail files, database objects, transformations, tests, model objects, or evidence described in the lessons. Every output keeps a visible connection to its source and batch so you can trace an order, customer, product, campaign, return, shipment, or inventory record.

### Level 3 — Professional explanation

This phase establishes a controlled boundary in an end-to-end batch platform. It defines contracts, execution context, idempotency behavior, quality expectations, evidence, and handoff artifacts so the downstream layer can be reproduced and reviewed independently.

## Lesson 9.2 — Perform the notebook-guided actions one at a time

## Retained phase lesson, exercises, rules, and expected results

> **Track:** Track A required  
> **Ownership status at start:** Workbook instructions exist; your execution is not yet verified.  
> **Evidence rule:** Replace placeholders only after the verification steps pass.

## 1. What you are building

Separate Bronze Delta tables for SQL Server extracts, PostgreSQL extracts, CSV feeds, and nested JSON tracking events. Raw values are preserved while source system, file path, ingestion timestamp, batch ID, record hash, unreadable-record quarantine, row counts, and manifest reconciliation are added.

## 2. Why it matters

Bronze is the replayable evidence layer. Heavy cleaning here would erase the source form and make later rule disputes difficult. The layer should answer which batch/file produced a row and support safe same-batch reruns.

## 3. Words to know

| Term | Plain-language definition |
| --- | --- |
| Raw preservation | Keep source values as received wherever readable. |
| Append-only | New batches are added rather than editing historical raw rows; same-batch replacement is a controlled exception for idempotency. |
| Record hash | Hash of the raw record used for trace/change evidence. |
| Input file name | Physical source path recorded per row. |
| PERMISSIVE mode | Reader captures malformed data where possible rather than silently dropping. |
| Quarantine | Unreadable records and error context retained outside trusted table. |
| Delta table | Transactional lakehouse table. |
| Schema inference | Reader guesses types; Bronze CSV intentionally keeps strings to defer business casting. |
| Manifest reconciliation | Expected file rows compared to read/written rows. |
| Rerun | Repeat a batch/task after failure. |
| Batch replacement | Delete only target rows with same batch ID before append. |
| Source system | Origin label such as SQLSERVER_ERP, POSTGRES_DIGITAL, FILE_FEED. |

## 4. What must already be completed

Phase 8 environment check passes and the exact batch folder is readable. Source manifest is present. Notebooks 01–03 are synced/imported.

## 5. Applications to open

| Application | How to open it | Why it is open |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Databricks workspace | Open notebooks 01, 02, 03. | Run and inspect Bronze ingestion. |
| Catalog Explorer | Open Bronze and quality schemas. | Preview tables/quarantine and properties. |
| VS Code | Open the source notebook and Bronze SQL pattern. | Read audit/idempotency functions. |
| Local manifest | Open in VS Code/browser. | Provide expected row counts/checksums. |

## 6. Exact click-by-click steps

## 7. Exact commands, one code block at a time

## 8. Where each command runs

## TEACHING EXAMPLE

The following small example or reference pattern explains the concept before you attempt Northstar-specific work. Read it, then complete **MY TASK** without copying the answer.

### Line-by-line code explanation

| Line or action | Meaning | Why it belongs here |
| --- | --- | --- |
| display(spark.table(f"{catalog}.{bronze_schema}.erp_customers").filter(F.col("_batch_id") == batch_id).limit(10)) | Shows raw customer rows and audit columns for one batch. | You must visually verify preservation and metadata before Silver. |
| SELECT _batch_id, COUNT(*) AS rows, COUNT(DISTINCT _record_hash) AS distinct_hashes | Counts Bronze orders by batch and hash. | Detects duplicate batch or duplicate raw rows. |
| manifest_text = "".join(r.value for r in spark.read.text(f"{batch_root}/batch_manifest.json").collect()) | Reads and parses local extraction manifest from volume. | Bronze must compare against source evidence, not only itself. |
| SELECT return_date, COUNT(*) AS rows | Shows raw mixed date strings. | Proves Bronze did not force one format. |
| SELECT * FROM northstar_retail.bronze.file_read_quarantine ORDER BY quarantined_at_utc DESC LIMIT 20; | Inspects unreadable file error evidence. | A failed record/file must remain diagnosable. |

### Bronze contract

Do: preserve raw values, retain nested structures, add technical metadata, identify batch/file/source, count rows, and fail visibly on unreadable inputs.

Do not: title-case names, validate emails as trusted, parse every date into one business meaning, choose duplicate winners, join sources, calculate profit, or resolve dimension keys. Those are Silver/Gold responsibilities.

### Manifest formula

For each readable file: `manifest expected rows = Bronze rows for that file and batch`. For malformed records under permissive parsing: `expected rows = accepted raw rows + row-level unreadable quarantine`, with exact reader behavior documented.

## MY TASK

Add manifest expected-row validation to each Bronze notebook, demonstrate same-batch idempotency, and document one unreadable-file quarantine test without changing the valid source batch.

## STARTER SKELETON

```python
def expected_rows(manifest: dict, source_system: str, filename: str) -> int:
    # TODO(USER): find exactly one matching manifest entry.
    matches = [
        item for item in manifest["files"]
        if item["source_system"] == ______ and item["file"].endswith(______)
    ]
    if len(matches) != 1:
        raise ValueError(______)
    return int(matches[0]["rows"])

# TODO(USER): compare expected, input DataFrame, and target batch counts.
assert ______ == ______ == ______
```

**Acceptance criteria:** Every Bronze subject has audit columns, current-batch count matches manifest, same-batch rerun is stable, controlled dirty values remain raw, and unreadable input creates evidence and failure.

## HINT 1 — CONCEPT

 Match manifest entries by source system plus terminal filename, not an unqualified substring.
## HINT 2 — PSEUDOCODE
 Compute expected/input/target once and include all values in an assertion message.
## HINT 3 — NEAR-COMPLETE PATTERN
 Follow `append_once` and add manifest lookup before the write; do not clean values.

## 15. Automated tests

## 16. Common errors and exact fixes

| Message/symptom | Likely cause | Exact diagnostic | Safe fix | Verify |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Path/file not found | Upload structure or widget mismatch. | Print batch_root; ls parent/subfolder; compare manifest. | Correct path/upload; do not hard-code random path. | Reader counts expected file. |
| Schema inference changed types | Reader options or source file evolved. | printSchema and compare previous batch. | Keep CSV Bronze strings; record additive drift; explicit Silver casts. | Schema drift test documented. |
| Target doubled on rerun | Batch deletion filter not applied or batch ID changed. | Group target by batch; print parameter. | Use exact stable batch ID and replace only that batch. | Count stable. |
| Manifest count differs | Wrong file, header count, parsing loss, or manifest method. | Compare source entry/path/input/quarantine/target. | Correct counting/parsing and document malformed behavior; do not alter expected silently. | Equation balances. |
| JSON corrupt record | Malformed nested feed. | Read with permissive/corrupt-record column and inspect source line. | Quarantine error/record and fail required gate per policy. | No silent loss. |

For deeper tool-specific diagnosis, use [`the troubleshooting index near the end of this workbook`](#complete-troubleshooting-index).

#### Folder-creation decision branches

##### If the folder is created

Run `Test-Path -LiteralPath ".\databricks" -PathType Container` and require `True`.

##### If PowerShell says the folder already exists

Do not delete or recreate it. Run `Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath ".\databricks" -Force`, inspect its existing files, and preserve them. Continue only when the existing folder is the intended path.

##### If the parent path does not exist

Return to the parent-folder tutorial. Create and verify one parent level at a time; do not create the entire future tree in one command.

#### Verify the folder

1. Run `Test-Path ".\databricks" -PathType Container`.
2. Require the output `True` before creating a child file.
3. Remember: Git does not track an empty folder by itself; the folder becomes visible in Git history when a tracked file is added.

### Optional reference answer for `databricks/notebooks/01_bronze_sqlserver.py`

Attempt the file construction first. This reference is learning material, not evidence that you created or ran the file.

**Language:** Python  
**Exact file:** `databricks/notebooks/01_bronze_sqlserver.py`  
**Purpose:** executable Python logic.  
**Inputs:** The requirements, configuration, source data, or upstream objects described in Phase 9.  
**Expected outputs:** The file's declared objects, logs, tables, checks, or documentation when the user later runs or reads it.

```python
# Databricks notebook source
# Northstar Retail End-to-End Data Platform
# This file is a Git-friendly Databricks source notebook.
# Track A reads files that you manually uploaded to a Unity Catalog volume.
# It never attempts to reach SQL Server or PostgreSQL on localhost.


# COMMAND ----------
# MAGIC %md
# MAGIC # 01 — Bronze SQL Server extracts
# MAGIC Reads Track A Parquet extracts from the uploaded volume; SQL Server itself remains local.

# COMMAND ----------

from __future__ import annotations
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from functools import reduce
from pyspark.sql import DataFrame
from pyspark.sql import functions as F

for name, default in {
    "catalog": "northstar_retail", "landing_schema": "landing", "bronze_schema": "bronze",
    "volume": "track_a_files", "batch_id": "MANUAL-REPLACE-ME"
}.items():
    dbutils.widgets.text(name, default)

catalog = dbutils.widgets.get("catalog")
landing_schema = dbutils.widgets.get("landing_schema")
bronze_schema = dbutils.widgets.get("bronze_schema")
volume = dbutils.widgets.get("volume")
batch_id = dbutils.widgets.get("batch_id")
if batch_id == "MANUAL-REPLACE-ME":
    raise ValueError("Pass the extraction batch_id from the workflow.")
batch_root = f"/Volumes/{catalog}/{landing_schema}/{volume}/{batch_id}"


def with_audit_columns(df: DataFrame, source_system: str) -> DataFrame:
    """Preserve raw columns and add repeatable ingestion metadata."""
    payload = F.to_json(F.struct(*[F.col(c).cast("string").alias(c) for c in df.columns]))
    return (
        df.withColumn("_source_system", F.lit(source_system))
          .withColumn("_source_file", F.input_file_name())
          .withColumn("_ingested_at_utc", F.current_timestamp())
          .withColumn("_batch_id", F.lit(batch_id))
          .withColumn("_record_hash", F.sha2(payload, 256))
    )


def append_once(df: DataFrame, table_name: str) -> None:
    """Append this batch once; an exact rerun replaces the same batch safely."""
    full_name = f"`{catalog}`.`{bronze_schema}`.`{table_name}`"
    if spark.catalog.tableExists(full_name.replace("`", "")):
        spark.sql(f"DELETE FROM {full_name} WHERE _batch_id = '{batch_id}'")
    (df.write.format("delta").mode("append").option("mergeSchema", "true").saveAsTable(full_name))
    loaded = spark.table(full_name).filter(F.col("_batch_id") == batch_id).count()
    if loaded != df.count():
        raise AssertionError(f"Bronze reconciliation failed for {table_name}: input={df.count()} target={loaded}")


# COMMAND ----------
tables = [
    "customers", "addresses", "products", "product_categories", "suppliers", "stores",
    "employees", "orders", "order_items", "payments", "shipments",
    "inventory_transactions", "inventory_snapshots",
]
results = []
for table in tables:
    path = f"{batch_root}/sqlserver/{table}.parquet"
    raw = spark.read.format("parquet").load(path)
    audited = with_audit_columns(raw, "SQLSERVER_ERP")
    append_once(audited, f"erp_{table}")
    results.append((table, raw.count()))
display(spark.createDataFrame(results, ["table_name", "rows_loaded"]))
dbutils.jobs.taskValues.set(key="bronze_sqlserver_status", value="PASS")
```

- **Line 2:** `# Northstar Retail End-to-End Data Platform` is a comment for a human reader; it normally does not change data or execute business logic.
- **Line 3:** `# This file is a Git-friendly Databricks source notebook.` is a comment for a human reader; it normally does not change data or execute business logic.

### Optional reference answer for `databricks/notebooks/02_bronze_postgres.py`

Attempt the file construction first. This reference is learning material, not evidence that you created or ran the file.

**Language:** Python  
**Exact file:** `databricks/notebooks/02_bronze_postgres.py`  
**Purpose:** executable Python logic.  
**Inputs:** The requirements, configuration, source data, or upstream objects described in Phase 9.  
**Expected outputs:** The file's declared objects, logs, tables, checks, or documentation when the user later runs or reads it.

```python
# Databricks notebook source
# Northstar Retail End-to-End Data Platform
# This file is a Git-friendly Databricks source notebook.
# Track A reads files that you manually uploaded to a Unity Catalog volume.
# It never attempts to reach SQL Server or PostgreSQL on localhost.


# COMMAND ----------
# MAGIC %md
# MAGIC # 02 — Bronze PostgreSQL extracts
# MAGIC Reads Track A Parquet extracts from the uploaded volume; PostgreSQL itself remains local.

# COMMAND ----------

from __future__ import annotations
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from functools import reduce
from pyspark.sql import DataFrame
from pyspark.sql import functions as F

for name, default in {
    "catalog": "northstar_retail", "landing_schema": "landing", "bronze_schema": "bronze",
    "volume": "track_a_files", "batch_id": "MANUAL-REPLACE-ME"
}.items():
    dbutils.widgets.text(name, default)

catalog = dbutils.widgets.get("catalog")
landing_schema = dbutils.widgets.get("landing_schema")
bronze_schema = dbutils.widgets.get("bronze_schema")
volume = dbutils.widgets.get("volume")
batch_id = dbutils.widgets.get("batch_id")
if batch_id == "MANUAL-REPLACE-ME":
    raise ValueError("Pass the extraction batch_id from the workflow.")
batch_root = f"/Volumes/{catalog}/{landing_schema}/{volume}/{batch_id}"


def with_audit_columns(df: DataFrame, source_system: str) -> DataFrame:
    """Preserve raw columns and add repeatable ingestion metadata."""
    payload = F.to_json(F.struct(*[F.col(c).cast("string").alias(c) for c in df.columns]))
    return (
        df.withColumn("_source_system", F.lit(source_system))
          .withColumn("_source_file", F.input_file_name())
          .withColumn("_ingested_at_utc", F.current_timestamp())
          .withColumn("_batch_id", F.lit(batch_id))
          .withColumn("_record_hash", F.sha2(payload, 256))
    )


def append_once(df: DataFrame, table_name: str) -> None:
    """Append this batch once; an exact rerun replaces the same batch safely."""
    full_name = f"`{catalog}`.`{bronze_schema}`.`{table_name}`"
    if spark.catalog.tableExists(full_name.replace("`", "")):
        spark.sql(f"DELETE FROM {full_name} WHERE _batch_id = '{batch_id}'")
    (df.write.format("delta").mode("append").option("mergeSchema", "true").saveAsTable(full_name))
    loaded = spark.table(full_name).filter(F.col("_batch_id") == batch_id).count()
    if loaded != df.count():
        raise AssertionError(f"Bronze reconciliation failed for {table_name}: input={df.count()} target={loaded}")


# COMMAND ----------
tables = ["web_users", "web_sessions", "web_events", "campaigns", "campaign_touchpoints", "marketing_spend"]
results = []
for table in tables:
    path = f"{batch_root}/postgres/{table}.parquet"
    raw = spark.read.format("parquet").load(path)
    audited = with_audit_columns(raw, "POSTGRES_DIGITAL")
    append_once(audited, f"digital_{table}")
    results.append((table, raw.count()))
display(spark.createDataFrame(results, ["table_name", "rows_loaded"]))
dbutils.jobs.taskValues.set(key="bronze_postgres_status", value="PASS")
```

### Optional reference answer for `databricks/notebooks/03_bronze_files.py`

Attempt the file construction first. This reference is learning material, not evidence that you created or ran the file.

**Language:** Python  
**Exact file:** `databricks/notebooks/03_bronze_files.py`  
**Purpose:** executable Python logic.  
**Inputs:** The requirements, configuration, source data, or upstream objects described in Phase 9.  
**Expected outputs:** The file's declared objects, logs, tables, checks, or documentation when the user later runs or reads it.

```python
# Databricks notebook source
# Northstar Retail End-to-End Data Platform
# This file is a Git-friendly Databricks source notebook.
# Track A reads files that you manually uploaded to a Unity Catalog volume.
# It never attempts to reach SQL Server or PostgreSQL on localhost.


# COMMAND ----------
# MAGIC %md
# MAGIC # 03 — Bronze file feeds
# MAGIC CSV values remain strings in Bronze. Nested tracking JSON is preserved and parsed as a struct/array.

# COMMAND ----------

from __future__ import annotations
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from functools import reduce
from pyspark.sql import DataFrame
from pyspark.sql import functions as F

for name, default in {
    "catalog": "northstar_retail", "landing_schema": "landing", "bronze_schema": "bronze",
    "volume": "track_a_files", "batch_id": "MANUAL-REPLACE-ME"
}.items():
    dbutils.widgets.text(name, default)

catalog = dbutils.widgets.get("catalog")
landing_schema = dbutils.widgets.get("landing_schema")
bronze_schema = dbutils.widgets.get("bronze_schema")
volume = dbutils.widgets.get("volume")
batch_id = dbutils.widgets.get("batch_id")
if batch_id == "MANUAL-REPLACE-ME":
    raise ValueError("Pass the extraction batch_id from the workflow.")
batch_root = f"/Volumes/{catalog}/{landing_schema}/{volume}/{batch_id}"


def with_audit_columns(df: DataFrame, source_system: str) -> DataFrame:
    """Preserve raw columns and add repeatable ingestion metadata."""
    payload = F.to_json(F.struct(*[F.col(c).cast("string").alias(c) for c in df.columns]))
    return (
        df.withColumn("_source_system", F.lit(source_system))
          .withColumn("_source_file", F.input_file_name())
          .withColumn("_ingested_at_utc", F.current_timestamp())
          .withColumn("_batch_id", F.lit(batch_id))
          .withColumn("_record_hash", F.sha2(payload, 256))
    )


def append_once(df: DataFrame, table_name: str) -> None:
    """Append this batch once; an exact rerun replaces the same batch safely."""
    full_name = f"`{catalog}`.`{bronze_schema}`.`{table_name}`"
    if spark.catalog.tableExists(full_name.replace("`", "")):
        spark.sql(f"DELETE FROM {full_name} WHERE _batch_id = '{batch_id}'")
    (df.write.format("delta").mode("append").option("mergeSchema", "true").saveAsTable(full_name))
    loaded = spark.table(full_name).filter(F.col("_batch_id") == batch_id).count()
    if loaded != df.count():
        raise AssertionError(f"Bronze reconciliation failed for {table_name}: input={df.count()} target={loaded}")


# COMMAND ----------
file_specs = {
    "file_returns": (f"{batch_root}/files/returns.csv", "csv"),
    "file_supplier_cost_updates": (f"{batch_root}/files/supplier_cost_updates.csv", "csv"),
    "file_promotion_calendar": (f"{batch_root}/files/promotion_calendar.csv", "csv"),
    "file_shipment_tracking_events": (f"{batch_root}/files/shipment_tracking_events.jsonl", "json"),
}
results = []
for table_name, (path, kind) in file_specs.items():
    try:
        if kind == "csv":
            raw = spark.read.option("header", "true").option("mode", "PERMISSIVE").csv(path)
        else:
            raw = spark.read.option("mode", "PERMISSIVE").json(path)
        audited = with_audit_columns(raw, "FILE_FEED")
        append_once(audited, table_name)
        results.append((table_name, raw.count(), "PASS"))
    except Exception as exc:
        # Create a visible quarantine record and fail the task so the quality gate cannot be bypassed.
        quarantine = spark.createDataFrame([(batch_id, path, str(exc), datetime.now(timezone.utc))], ["batch_id", "source_path", "error_message", "quarantined_at_utc"])
        quarantine.write.format("delta").mode("append").saveAsTable(f"`{catalog}`.`{bronze_schema}`.`file_read_quarantine`")
        raise

display(spark.createDataFrame(results, ["table_name", "rows_loaded", "status"]))
dbutils.jobs.taskValues.set(key="bronze_files_status", value="PASS")
```

```python
(bronze_df.write.format("delta")
    .mode("append")
    .saveAsTable(target_table))
```

```python
source_path = "/Volumes/<catalog>/landing/northstar/<batch_id>/postgres/web_users.csv"

(bronze_df.write.format("delta")
    .mode("append")
    .saveAsTable(target_table))
```

```python
source_path = "/Volumes/<catalog>/landing/northstar/<batch_id>/postgres/web_sessions.csv"

(bronze_df.write.format("delta")
    .mode("append")
    .saveAsTable(target_table))
```

```python
source_path = "/Volumes/<catalog>/landing/northstar/<batch_id>/postgres/campaign_touchpoints.csv"
```
