## Why this phase happens now

**Earlier work this phase depends on:** A successful, idempotent Databricks Job run.  
**What would go wrong if it happened earlier:** You would create objects without a verified requirement, valid upstream input, protected repository state, or known execution environment.  
**Later work that depends on it:** Phase 15 exports only verified Gold results and loads them into the local warehouse.  
**Decision being made:** Choose and verify the simplest local-first method that teaches the professional concept without pretending that local services are publicly reachable.  
**Alternatives:** A company could use managed cloud databases, infrastructure as code, service principals, direct JDBC publication, deployment bundles, or streaming. Those options are discussed as tradeoffs, not substituted silently.  
**Beginner path selected:** Track A: local SQL Server and PostgreSQL, Python batch extracts, manual governed upload to Databricks, Delta Bronze/Silver/Gold, manual verified export, local SQL Server warehouse, and Power BI Import.  
**Reason for the order:** Requirements become source decisions; sources become generated data; source data becomes extraction batches; batches become Bronze; Bronze becomes Silver; Silver becomes Gold; Gold becomes warehouse and Power BI input.

## Three-level explanation of the phase

### Level 1 — Child-simple explanation

Imagine building a store from labeled boxes. This phase handles one box, checks that the label is correct, and makes sure the next box receives the right thing. You do not pour all boxes together and hope the result is understandable.

### Level 2 — Northstar Retail project explanation

Phase 14 creates the specific Northstar Retail files, database objects, transformations, tests, model objects, or evidence described in the lessons. Every output keeps a visible connection to its source and batch so you can trace an order, customer, product, campaign, return, shipment, or inventory record.

### Level 3 — Professional explanation

This phase establishes a controlled boundary in an end-to-end batch platform. It defines contracts, execution context, idempotency behavior, quality expectations, evidence, and handoff artifacts so the downstream layer can be reproduced and reviewed independently.

## 1. What you are building

A parameterized Lakeflow Job containing environment validation, three Bronze tasks, four Silver domain tasks, Gold dimensions, Gold facts, quality gate, publication, and final reconciliation, with correct dependencies, compute, retries, timeouts, notifications, schedule decision, repair-run procedure, and a version-controlled definition.

## 2. Why it matters

A set of notebooks becomes a pipeline only when execution order, shared parameters, failure behavior, retries, and operational evidence are controlled. Orchestration prevents a user from accidentally publishing before upstream tasks or tests finish.

## 3. Words to know

| Term | Plain-language definition |
| --- | --- |
| Job | Named orchestrated workflow. |
| Task | One executable unit inside a Job. |
| Dependency | Task that must succeed before another starts. |
| Parameter | Runtime value passed to tasks, such as batch ID. |
| Retry | Automatic rerun for likely transient failure. |
| Timeout | Maximum task/job runtime before failure. |
| Notification | Message on selected run events. |
| Schedule | Time/trigger for starting a Job. |
| Repair run | Rerun failed/skipped downstream tasks within an existing run. |
| Run history | Stored status, timing, parameters, logs, task graph. |
| Concurrent run | Multiple Job instances executing at once. |
| Job cluster/serverless | Compute selected for Job tasks; availability varies. |
| Declarative Automation Bundle | Current Databricks version-controlled deployment packaging; formerly Asset Bundles in older naming. |
| Task dependency diagram | Visual execution graph. |

## 4. What must already be completed

Notebooks 00–12 exist in workspace; manual runs through quality are understood; exact parameter names are consistent; current workspace Jobs/compute limitations are reviewed.

## TEACHING EXAMPLE

The following small example or reference pattern explains the concept before you attempt Northstar-specific work. Read it, then complete **MY TASK** without copying the answer.

### Line-by-line code explanation

| Line or action | Meaning | Why it belongs here |
| --- | --- | --- |
| batch_id = EXT-YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ | Selects one uploaded extraction batch for every task. | A Job without a concrete batch can mix/default wrong input. |
| print({name: dbutils.widgets.get(name) for name in ["catalog", "batch_id"]}) | Shows key task parameters. | Detects parameter propagation failure. |
| python -c "import yaml, pathlib; p=yaml.safe_load(pathlib.Path('databricks/jobs/job_definition.example.yml').read_text()); print([t['task_key'] for t in p['resources']['jobs']['northstar_retail_daily']['tasks']])" | Parses job YAML and lists tasks. | Version-controlled definition must be valid YAML and complete. |
| python -m pytest -q tests\integration\test_repository_contract.py | Checks every YAML notebook path exists and Gold dictionary contract. | Prevents stale orchestration references. |

### Retry policy

Retry transient storage/compute/network availability failures a small number of times with delay. Do not repeatedly retry deterministic schema, permission, missing-path, or quality assertion failures; retries waste quota and hide diagnosis.

### Scheduling Track A

Because the local extraction/upload is manual, an automatic daily Job can find no new batch or rerun an old one. The beginner default is manual run after upload. An advanced readiness trigger reads a control object/manifest and selects an unprocessed batch safely.

### Version control

The example YAML captures logical resources and real repository-relative notebook paths. A deployable Databricks bundle additionally needs workspace target configuration and supported CLI authentication; keep that optional until the UI Job is verified.

## MY TASK

Build the entire Job in the UI, align it to the YAML and dependency diagram, run a valid batch, demonstrate blocked publication and repair, and document manual-versus-scheduled trigger decision.

## STARTER SKELETON

```yaml
resources:
  jobs:
    northstar_retail_daily:
      name: northstar-retail-daily
      max_concurrent_runs: 1
      parameters:
        - name: batch_id
          default: TODO(USER)-REQUIRED
      tasks:
        - task_key: TODO(USER)
          depends_on:
            - task_key: TODO(USER)
          notebook_task:
            notebook_path: ../notebooks/TODO(USER).py
            base_parameters:
              batch_id: "{{job.parameters.batch_id}}"
          max_retries: TODO(USER)
          timeout_seconds: TODO(USER)
# TODO(USER): fill only after building/validating UI graph.
```

**Acceptance criteria:** UI graph and YAML contain all real notebook tasks/dependencies; all tasks receive same parameters; valid run succeeds; failed gate skips publish; repair succeeds; concurrent/schedule/retry decisions are documented.

## 16. Common errors and exact fixes

| Message/symptom | Likely cause | Exact diagnostic | Safe fix | Verify |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Notebook path invalid | Workspace Git/import path differs from YAML. | Open task source selector and repository paths. | Point to actual synced notebook; update workspace-neutral mapping. | Task opens/runs. |
| Parameter default used accidentally | Run dialog not set or task mapping wrong. | Inspect run/task parameters/log output. | Require/validate batch placeholder and pass Job parameters. | All print exact batch. |
| Retries repeat quality failure | Retry configured for deterministic assertion. | Run attempts/error same each time. | Reduce retry or classify; fix data/code, use repair. | Quota not wasted. |
| Publish runs too early | Missing/wrong dependency. | Inspect graph edges and run timeline. | Make publish directly depend on successful quality gate. | Failure skips publish. |
| Schedule reruns old batch | Manual handoff has no readiness selection. | Inspect scheduled parameter/history. | Keep manual or implement processed-batch control/readiness gate. | Each run selects new intended batch. |

For deeper tool-specific diagnosis, use [`the troubleshooting index near the end of this workbook`](#complete-troubleshooting-index).

Run or perform the smallest independent check named in the lesson. For a path, use `Get-Location` or `Test-Path`; for Git, use `git status` and `git branch --show-current`; for SQL, run a metadata or row-count query; for Databricks, inspect the target object and cell output; for Power BI, compare a filtered DAX result to SQL.

**Do not continue unless:**  
The result is visible, understandable, and recorded as `RUN BY USER` or `VERIFIED BY USER`. Displaying this workbook does not count as execution.

**Common mistake:**  
The most common mistake is running the right text in the wrong application, folder, database, catalog, schema, branch, or notebook language.

**Exact recovery:**  
Do not delete, reset, overwrite, or force-push. Read the first error line. Re-run the location check for this application. Confirm the current folder, branch, server/database, or Databricks catalog. Correct only the mismatched location or spelling, then retry this single command.

**What you just accomplished:**  
You executed and checked one controlled operation rather than treating a long script as a black box.

**How this connects to the project:**  
This verified state becomes a dependable input to the next Northstar Retail construction action.

#### File-creation decision branches

##### If the command creates the file

Run `Test-Path -LiteralPath ".\databricks\jobs\job_definition.example.yml" -PathType Leaf`. Continue only when it returns `True` and the file is empty because you just created it.

##### If PowerShell says the file already exists

Do not add `-Force`, do not clear the file, and do not overwrite it. Open the existing file in VS Code, run `git status --short -- "databricks/jobs/job_definition.example.yml"`, inspect its contents and Git history, and decide whether this lesson should edit the preserved file rather than create a new one.

##### If PowerShell says part of the path does not exist

Stop. Create only the missing parent folder through the earlier folder tutorial, verify it with `Test-Path -PathType Container`, and rerun this one file command.

#### File-content construction

1. Start with the smallest header, comment, or first section shown in the phase lesson.
2. Read the purpose before typing the section.
3. Add one logical section at a time.
4. Save with Ctrl+S.
5. Run the syntax or content validation named in the phase.
6. Correct the first error before adding another section.
7. Use `TODO(USER)` where the workbook requires your own decision or verified value.

#### File verification

1. In the VS Code Explorer, confirm the file appears under `databricks/jobs`.
2. Right-click the editor tab and choose **Copy Path**; compare the ending with `databricks/jobs/job_definition.example.yml`.
3. In PowerShell at the repository root, run `Test-Path ".\databricks\jobs\job_definition.example.yml"` and require `True`.
4. Run `git status --short -- "databricks/jobs/job_definition.example.yml"` to see only this file's Git state.
5. Run the phase-specific validator before committing.


### Optional reference answer for `databricks/jobs/job_definition.example.yml`

Attempt the file construction first. This reference is learning material, not evidence that you created or ran the file.

**Language:** YAML  
**Exact file:** `databricks/jobs/job_definition.example.yml`  
**Purpose:** human-readable configuration.  
**Inputs:** The requirements, configuration, source data, or upstream objects described in Phase 14.  
**Expected outputs:** The file's declared objects, logs, tables, checks, or documentation when the user later runs or reads it.

```yaml
# Example version-controlled Lakeflow Job definition.
# Paths are repository-relative and point to files the learner manually creates through this workbook.
# Adapt this file to your workspace or convert it into a root databricks.yml bundle.
resources:
  jobs:
    northstar_retail_daily:
      name: northstar-retail-daily
      max_concurrent_runs: 1
      timeout_seconds: 7200
      parameters:
        - name: catalog
          default: northstar_retail
        - name: landing_schema
          default: landing
        - name: bronze_schema
          default: bronze
        - name: silver_schema
          default: silver
        - name: gold_schema
          default: gold
        - name: quality_schema
          default: quality
        - name: volume
          default: track_a_files
        - name: batch_id
          default: MANUAL-REPLACE-ME
      tasks:
        - task_key: environment_check
          notebook_task:
            notebook_path: ../notebooks/00_environment_check.py
            base_parameters: {catalog: "{{job.parameters.catalog}}", landing_schema: "{{job.parameters.landing_schema}}", bronze_schema: "{{job.parameters.bronze_schema}}", silver_schema: "{{job.parameters.silver_schema}}", gold_schema: "{{job.parameters.gold_schema}}", quality_schema: "{{job.parameters.quality_schema}}", volume: "{{job.parameters.volume}}", batch_id: "{{job.parameters.batch_id}}"}
        - task_key: bronze_sqlserver
          depends_on: [{task_key: environment_check}]
          notebook_task: {notebook_path: ../notebooks/01_bronze_sqlserver.py, base_parameters: {catalog: "{{job.parameters.catalog}}", landing_schema: "{{job.parameters.landing_schema}}", bronze_schema: "{{job.parameters.bronze_schema}}", volume: "{{job.parameters.volume}}", batch_id: "{{job.parameters.batch_id}}"}}
          max_retries: 2
          min_retry_interval_millis: 60000
        - task_key: bronze_postgres
          depends_on: [{task_key: environment_check}]
          notebook_task: {notebook_path: ../notebooks/02_bronze_postgres.py, base_parameters: {catalog: "{{job.parameters.catalog}}", landing_schema: "{{job.parameters.landing_schema}}", bronze_schema: "{{job.parameters.bronze_schema}}", volume: "{{job.parameters.volume}}", batch_id: "{{job.parameters.batch_id}}"}}
          max_retries: 2
        - task_key: bronze_files
          depends_on: [{task_key: environment_check}]
          notebook_task: {notebook_path: ../notebooks/03_bronze_files.py, base_parameters: {catalog: "{{job.parameters.catalog}}", landing_schema: "{{job.parameters.landing_schema}}", bronze_schema: "{{job.parameters.bronze_schema}}", volume: "{{job.parameters.volume}}", batch_id: "{{job.parameters.batch_id}}"}}
          max_retries: 2
        - task_key: silver_customers
          depends_on: [{task_key: bronze_sqlserver}, {task_key: bronze_files}]
          notebook_task: {notebook_path: ../notebooks/04_silver_customers.py, base_parameters: {catalog: "{{job.parameters.catalog}}", bronze_schema: "{{job.parameters.bronze_schema}}", silver_schema: "{{job.parameters.silver_schema}}", quality_schema: "{{job.parameters.quality_schema}}", batch_id: "{{job.parameters.batch_id}}"}}
        - task_key: silver_products
          depends_on: [{task_key: bronze_sqlserver}, {task_key: bronze_files}]
          notebook_task: {notebook_path: ../notebooks/05_silver_products.py, base_parameters: {catalog: "{{job.parameters.catalog}}", bronze_schema: "{{job.parameters.bronze_schema}}", silver_schema: "{{job.parameters.silver_schema}}", quality_schema: "{{job.parameters.quality_schema}}", batch_id: "{{job.parameters.batch_id}}"}}
        - task_key: silver_sales
          depends_on: [{task_key: bronze_sqlserver}, {task_key: bronze_files}, {task_key: silver_products}]
          notebook_task: {notebook_path: ../notebooks/06_silver_sales.py, base_parameters: {catalog: "{{job.parameters.catalog}}", bronze_schema: "{{job.parameters.bronze_schema}}", silver_schema: "{{job.parameters.silver_schema}}", quality_schema: "{{job.parameters.quality_schema}}", batch_id: "{{job.parameters.batch_id}}"}}
        - task_key: silver_digital
          depends_on: [{task_key: bronze_postgres}]
          notebook_task: {notebook_path: ../notebooks/07_silver_digital.py, base_parameters: {catalog: "{{job.parameters.catalog}}", bronze_schema: "{{job.parameters.bronze_schema}}", silver_schema: "{{job.parameters.silver_schema}}", quality_schema: "{{job.parameters.quality_schema}}", batch_id: "{{job.parameters.batch_id}}"}}
        - task_key: gold_dimensions
          depends_on: [{task_key: silver_customers}, {task_key: silver_products}, {task_key: silver_sales}, {task_key: silver_digital}]
          notebook_task: {notebook_path: ../notebooks/08_gold_dimensions.py, base_parameters: {catalog: "{{job.parameters.catalog}}", bronze_schema: "{{job.parameters.bronze_schema}}", silver_schema: "{{job.parameters.silver_schema}}", gold_schema: "{{job.parameters.gold_schema}}", batch_id: "{{job.parameters.batch_id}}"}}
        - task_key: gold_facts
          depends_on: [{task_key: gold_dimensions}]
          notebook_task: {notebook_path: ../notebooks/09_gold_facts.py, base_parameters: {catalog: "{{job.parameters.catalog}}", silver_schema: "{{job.parameters.silver_schema}}", gold_schema: "{{job.parameters.gold_schema}}", batch_id: "{{job.parameters.batch_id}}"}}
        - task_key: data_quality_gate
          depends_on: [{task_key: gold_facts}]
          notebook_task: {notebook_path: ../notebooks/10_data_quality.py, base_parameters: {catalog: "{{job.parameters.catalog}}", gold_schema: "{{job.parameters.gold_schema}}", quality_schema: "{{job.parameters.quality_schema}}", batch_id: "{{job.parameters.batch_id}}"}}
        - task_key: publish_gold
          depends_on: [{task_key: data_quality_gate}]
          notebook_task: {notebook_path: ../notebooks/11_publish_gold.py, base_parameters: {catalog: "{{job.parameters.catalog}}", landing_schema: "{{job.parameters.landing_schema}}", gold_schema: "{{job.parameters.gold_schema}}", quality_schema: "{{job.parameters.quality_schema}}", volume: "{{job.parameters.volume}}", batch_id: "{{job.parameters.batch_id}}"}}
        - task_key: final_reconciliation
          depends_on: [{task_key: publish_gold}]
          notebook_task: {notebook_path: ../notebooks/12_demo_queries.py, base_parameters: {catalog: "{{job.parameters.catalog}}", gold_schema: "{{job.parameters.gold_schema}}", quality_schema: "{{job.parameters.quality_schema}}", batch_id: "{{job.parameters.batch_id}}"}}
```

### Optional reference answer for `databricks/jobs/job_task_map.md`

Attempt the file construction first. This reference is learning material, not evidence that you created or ran the file.

**Language:** Markdown  
**Exact file:** `databricks/jobs/job_task_map.md`  
**Purpose:** project documentation.  
**Inputs:** The requirements, configuration, source data, or upstream objects described in Phase 14.  
**Expected outputs:** The file's declared objects, logs, tables, checks, or documentation when the user later runs or reads it.

```markdown
# Lakeflow Jobs task map

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  E[environment_check] --> B1[bronze_sqlserver]
  E --> B2[bronze_postgres]
  E --> B3[bronze_files]
  B1 --> S1[silver_customers]
  B3 --> S1
  B1 --> S2[silver_products]
  B3 --> S2
  B1 --> S3[silver_sales]
  B3 --> S3
  S2 --> S3
  B2 --> S4[silver_digital]
  S1 --> D[gold_dimensions]
  S2 --> D
  S3 --> D
  S4 --> D
  D --> F[gold_facts]
  F --> Q[data_quality_gate]
  Q --> P[publish_gold]
  P --> R[final_reconciliation]
```

The quality gate is intentionally between Gold construction and publication. A failed required check must prevent publication. In Databricks Free Edition, compute and concurrency are quota-limited; this graph uses at most three parallel Bronze tasks and four parallel prerequisites for Gold dimensions, below the documented five-task concurrent Jobs limit as accessed on 2026-08-16.
```

### Databricks Job task 13 — `demo_queries`

**Notebook:** `databricks/notebooks/12_demo_queries.py`  
**Depends on:** `publish_gold`  
**Inputs:** Job parameters, upstream verified tables/files, and task outputs named in the task map.  
**Output:** A validated table set, quality status, export, or demonstration result for the current Job run.  
**Retry policy:** Retry only transient failures; deterministic data-quality failures require diagnosis rather than repeated compute cost.  
**Timeout:** Set a finite threshold large enough for the fixture but short enough to surface a stuck task.  
**Idempotency expectation:** Repairing or rerunning the task for the same batch must not create unintended duplicates.

## Lesson 14.5 — Verify, troubleshoot, commit, teach back, and stop safely

## What your screen should look like before starting

The Phase 14 outputs are visible, all runs are finished, open files are saved, and you can state the active branch and execution context. Any error you encountered has a recorded message and has not been hidden by deleting evidence.

## Design decision — Verification before automation

**Question:**  
Should the phase prioritize a visible manual verification or jump directly to automation?

**Options considered:**

- Manual verification first, then automation.
- Automation without a known-good baseline.
- Manual operation forever.

**Beginner path selected:**  
Establish one verified manual baseline and then automate repeatable checks.

**Why this path was selected:**  
A known-good example makes failures interpretable and prevents automation from hiding a wrong assumption.

**Tradeoff:**  
The first run takes longer.

**What a company might do instead:**  
Teams often pair infrastructure as code and automated tests with controlled bootstrap and acceptance procedures.

**How to explain this in an interview:**  
I established a verified baseline, then encoded the same contract in tests and orchestration so automation preserved meaning rather than just speed.




## If you see Result A

The Job DAG completes and the run history shows successful dependent tasks. Record the exact result, perform the named independent verification, and continue only when the gate is satisfied.

## If you see Result B

A task fails or is skipped; repair targets only the failed/downstream tasks after the cause is fixed. Treat this as information, not permission to delete or overwrite. Follow the branch-specific diagnostic in the current action, preserve evidence, and continue only after the state is understood.

## If you see an error

Read the first meaningful error line, redact secrets, and verify the application, path, branch, server/database, catalog/schema, batch ID, parameters, version/tier, and object name. Run the smallest observational check first. Do not reset Git history, drop data, disable a rule, force-push, or replace the target merely to make the error disappear.


## Phase-specific verification gate

- [ ] Required files/objects exist in the exact location.
- [ ] I personally created or configured them.
- [ ] I ran the phase commands in the documented context.
- [ ] I inspected the output rather than relying on a green icon alone.
- [ ] Counts, keys, relationships, measures, checksums, statuses, or settings meet the declared contract.
- [ ] Same-batch/rerun behavior is known where applicable.
- [ ] A controlled failure or realistic alternate-result branch was tested safely where applicable.
- [ ] No password, token, or secret appears in tracked files, screenshots, notebook output, terminal history pasted into documentation, or staged changes.
- [ ] Actual verified result: `[ENTER VERIFIED RESULT]`.

### Interpret `git status --short`

- `??` means untracked: Git sees a new path but it is not staged.
- ` M` means modified in the working tree but not staged.
- `M ` means the staged version differs from the last commit.
- `MM` means a staged version exists and the file has additional unstaged edits.
- `A ` means staged as a new file.
- `D` means deletion; stop and investigate unless deletion is deliberate.
- `R` means rename; inspect both old and new paths.
- A blank result means the working tree is clean. It does not prove database, Databricks, or Power BI work occurred.

### Verify on GitHub

1. CLICK: Open the repository page in a browser.
2. CLICK: Open the branch selector above the file list.
3. TYPE THIS: The exact branch name returned locally.
4. CLICK: Select that branch.
5. LOOK FOR: The latest commit message `feat: orchestrate northstar lakehouse job` and the intended changed paths.

7. Do not merge solely because the push succeeded; CI and review must pass.

### Push-rejected recovery

If Git says the remote contains work you do not have, do not use `--force`. Run `git fetch origin`, inspect `git log --oneline --graph --decorate --all -20`, then rebase or merge only after understanding the divergence. Resolve conflicts one file at a time, run tests again, and push normally. A rejection protects remote work; it is not permission to overwrite it.

## OPTIONAL REFERENCE ANSWER — PHASE 14 TEACH-BACK MODEL

Read this only after completing **MY TASK** and using the three hints in order. The model is a learning reference, not evidence of your execution.

“Phase 14 created the verified boundary described by **Create and operate a multi-task Databricks Job**. It consumes only the outputs accepted from earlier phases, produces a named and auditable handoff, and records enough metadata and tests to detect wrong context, missing data, duplicates, failed rules, or unsafe reruns. I verified the result in its owning application and connected the evidence to Git without claiming that displayed instructions were executed.”

## Mini quiz

1. Multiple choice: Why does Phase 14 occur at this point in the source-to-consumption chain? A) Because menu order is arbitrary. B) Because its verified upstream input now exists. C) Because later phases do not depend on it. D) To create portfolio screenshots before validation.
2. True or false: A command that displays no error is automatically verified even when it ran in the wrong folder, database, catalog, schema, branch, or filter context.
3. Fill in the blank: The statement that defines what one row represents is the table or entity ________.
4. What command would you use first to confirm the PowerShell current folder before a repository command?
5. Troubleshooting: Your output differs from the example. What should you check before deleting, overwriting, resetting, force-pushing, or weakening a test?
6. Design choice: Explain one tradeoff of Track A and one production alternative.
7. Code reading: Why are input, accepted, rejected, and deduplicated counts recorded separately?
8. Ownership: Which status may you select only after personally performing and inspecting the verification?

---

## Mini quiz answer key and explanations

**1. B.** This phase is ordered after its prerequisites so its output has a trustworthy input. A is wrong because order is intentional; C is wrong because later phases depend on the handoff; D is wrong because screenshots follow verification.

**2. False.** Lack of an error proves only that the application accepted something; context and independent verification still matter.

**3. Grain.** Grain is the precise meaning of one row. A key identifies a row, but it does not by itself state the row’s business meaning.

**4. `Get-Location`.** It shows the shell’s current folder. `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` separately verifies the repository root when inside a clone.

**5.** Check application, folder/path, branch, server/database, catalog/schema, batch ID, parameters, source/target grain, filter context, version/tier differences, and the first meaningful error. Destructive changes are not a diagnostic step.

**6.** Track A has manual upload/download boundaries and batch latency. A production alternative is routable private connectivity with cloud object storage/managed warehouse, identities, and automated orchestration.

**7.** Separate counts make every row outcome explainable. A single final count can hide silent drops, duplicates, or records that moved to quarantine.

**8. `Verified by me` / `VERIFIED BY USER`.** `PLANNED`, `CREATED BY USER`, and `RUN BY USER` describe earlier states; only inspected evidence supports verification.

# Phase 15 — Publish Gold data into the SQL Server dimensional warehouse

[Back to the master table of contents](#master-table-of-contents)

**Track:** Track A required  
**Status when first opened:** `PLANNED`  
**Completion rule:** The phase is not complete because its instructions exist. Mark it `VERIFIED BY USER` only after you perform the work, inspect the output, and save evidence.

## Why this phase happens now

**Earlier work this phase depends on:** A validated SQL Server dimensional warehouse.  
**What would go wrong if it happened earlier:** You would create objects without a verified requirement, valid upstream input, protected repository state, or known execution environment.  
**Later work that depends on it:** Phase 16 imports trusted tables, builds relationships, and defines DAX measures.  
**Decision being made:** Choose and verify the simplest local-first method that teaches the professional concept without pretending that local services are publicly reachable.  
**Alternatives:** A company could use managed cloud databases, infrastructure as code, service principals, direct JDBC publication, deployment bundles, or streaming. Those options are discussed as tradeoffs, not substituted silently.  
**Beginner path selected:** Track A: local SQL Server and PostgreSQL, Python batch extracts, manual governed upload to Databricks, Delta Bronze/Silver/Gold, manual verified export, local SQL Server warehouse, and Power BI Import.  
**Reason for the order:** Requirements become source decisions; sources become generated data; source data becomes extraction batches; batches become Bronze; Bronze becomes Silver; Silver becomes Gold; Gold becomes warehouse and Power BI input.

## Three-level explanation of the phase

### Level 1 — Child-simple explanation

Imagine building a store from labeled boxes. This phase handles one box, checks that the label is correct, and makes sure the next box receives the right thing. You do not pour all boxes together and hope the result is understandable.

### Level 2 — Northstar Retail project explanation

Phase 15 creates the specific Northstar Retail files, database objects, transformations, tests, model objects, or evidence described in the lessons. Every output keeps a visible connection to its source and batch so you can trace an order, customer, product, campaign, return, shipment, or inventory record.

### Level 3 — Professional explanation

This phase establishes a controlled boundary in an end-to-end batch platform. It defines contracts, execution context, idempotency behavior, quality expectations, evidence, and handoff artifacts so the downstream layer can be reproduced and reviewed independently.

## Applications to open

Databricks, File Explorer, PowerShell, SSMS, and Python. Open only the application needed for the immediate action. Extra windows increase the chance of typing a command into the wrong context.

## 1. What you are building

A local SQL Server warehouse named `NorthstarRetail_DW` with `dw`, `stg`, `audit`, and `semantic` schemas, dimension/fact DDL, unknown rows, constraints/indexes, staging and transactional publication, load audit/reconciliation, semantic views, and exact SSMS inspection steps. Track A uses Gold export/download; Track B direct publication remains optional.

## 2. Why it matters

Gold Delta is business-ready, but a SQL Server serving mirror teaches warehouse DDL, transactional stage-and-publish, relational constraints/indexes, local Power BI connectivity, and cross-platform reconciliation. The manual download preserves the honest localhost boundary.

## 3. Words to know

| Term | Plain-language definition |
| --- | --- |
| Serving warehouse | Curated database optimized for analyst/BI consumption. |
| Staging schema | Temporary load tables before target publish. |
| Transactional publication | Stage/validate/delete-merge/insert/audit commit as one unit. |
| Full development reload | Replace target scope safely in disposable development. |
| Incremental publication | Apply new/changed rows while preserving history. |
| Audit table | Records batch process status/timing/errors. |
| Reconciliation table | Stores source/target values/differences/status. |
| Clustered/nonclustered index | SQL Server physical/access structures; design depends on workload. |
| Primary/foreign key | Relational integrity constraints in serving layer. |
| Semantic view | Stable SQL view exposing business-friendly columns. |
| Parquet export | Columnar Gold files downloaded from volume. |
| Direct publication | Track B write over reachable network/JDBC/connector, requiring security/network support. |
| Rollback | Transaction reverts target changes after failure. |

## 4. What must already be completed

Job quality gate passes; all Gold tables exist; publish notebook exports manifest/path; local SQL Server/SSMS/ODBC works; downloaded files are in one known folder; disk space available.

| --- | --- | --- |

| SSMS | Local server. | Run warehouse DDL, inspect/stage/validate. |

## 7. Exact commands, one code block at a time

## 8. Where each command runs

## TEACHING EXAMPLE

The following small example or reference pattern explains the concept before you attempt Northstar-specific work. Read it, then complete **MY TASK** without copying the answer.

### Line-by-line code explanation

| Line or action | Meaning | Why it belongs here |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SELECT @@SERVERNAME AS server_name, SUSER_SNAME() AS login_name, DB_NAME() AS database_name; | Verifies server/login/context. | ERP and DW have similar names; context mistakes are dangerous. |
| -- Execute the entire 01_create_warehouse.sql file. | Creates DW schemas/tables/constraints/indexes/unknown rows. | Loader needs target contract. |
| -- Execute 02_create_staging_tables.sql, then 03_semantic_views.sql. | Creates staging mirrors and business-friendly views. | Publication isolates incoming files and Power BI can use stable semantic access. |
| python -m scripts.loading.load_gold_to_sqlserver --input-dir "C:\Users\User\Downloads\gold_exports\EXT-YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ" --mode full-dev | Stages and transactionally publishes all Gold tables into the local DW. | This is Track A's controlled local serving handoff. |
| -- Execute sql/sqlserver/validation/02_validate_warehouse.sql | Checks duplicate fact grain, dimension RI, SCD current rows, revenue identity, audit/reconciliation. | Loader success does not prove model correctness. |
| SELECT TOP (20) * FROM semantic.vw_executive_daily_kpi ORDER BY full_date DESC; | Queries serving semantic view. | Confirms views compile and aggregate loaded warehouse. |

### Safe full-dev order

Stage every table first. Validate stage counts/schema. Delete fact tables before dimensions to satisfy foreign keys. Insert dimensions in dependency order, then facts. Recreate/retain unknown rows consistently. Record audit/reconciliation and commit once. On exception, roll back.

### Incremental tradeoff

An incremental warehouse publish must MERGE Type 1 dimensions, append/expire SCD2 versions correctly, upsert facts by immutable grain, handle deletes/corrections, and reconcile the batch. Full-dev is simpler and transparent for small learning data; it is not a production claim.

## MY TASK

Review/fix the local loader for fact-before-dimension deletion and explicit target columns, publish one validated batch, prove rollback with a safe staged failure, reconcile Gold to DW, and verify a same-batch reload.

## STARTER SKELETON

```python
# TODO(USER): safe full-dev publication outline
with engine.begin() as connection:
    stage_all_exports(connection, input_dir)
    validate_stage_counts(connection, manifest)
    for fact in reversed(FACT_TABLES):
        connection.execute(text(f"DELETE FROM dw.{fact}"))
    for dimension in reversed(DIMENSION_TABLES):
        connection.execute(text(f"DELETE FROM dw.{dimension} WHERE {dimension_key(dimension)} <> 0"))
    for dimension in DIMENSION_TABLES:
        insert_explicit_columns(connection, dimension)
    for fact in FACT_TABLES:
        insert_explicit_columns(connection, fact)
    record_reconciliation(connection, batch_id)
# TODO(USER): test a forced error rolls back target counts.
```

**Acceptance criteria:** Warehouse objects exist; publication is transactional and FK-safe; all Gold/SQL Server counts/amounts reconcile; invalid staged run rolls back; same-batch full-dev reload reproduces results; semantic views query successfully.

## HINT 1 — CONCEPT

 Delete child facts before parent dimensions; insert parents before children.
## HINT 2 — PSEUDOCODE
 Ask SQL Server `sys.columns` for insertable non-computed columns and use explicit lists.
## HINT 3 — NEAR-COMPLETE PATTERN
 Stage all tables and validate first; adapt skeleton inside one `engine.begin()` transaction.

- Semantic view values match base query.

## 15. Automated tests

- Warehouse validation SQL.
- Gold-to-DW count/amount checks.
- Transaction rollback test.
- Same-batch reproducibility.
- Constraint/index inspection.
- Semantic view query and KPI validation.

## 16. Common errors and exact fixes

| Message/symptom | Likely cause | Exact diagnostic | Safe fix | Verify |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| FK delete conflict | Dimensions deleted before facts. | Read constraint/table error; inspect deletion order. | Delete child facts first inside transaction. | Reload succeeds. |
| Computed column insert error | SELECT * includes computed/non-insertable target column. | Inspect `sys.columns.is_computed` and stage schema. | Use explicit insertable column list. | fact_inventory loads. |
| Missing Gold export | Fact TODO incomplete or download structure lost. | List input directory and Databricks manifest. | Complete Gold, rerun gated publish, preserve folders. | All 15 exports found. |
| Partial warehouse changes | Operations not in one transaction or DDL auto-commit boundary. | Compare audit/status/counts after forced failure. | Stage/validate then data DML in one transaction; avoid DDL in load transaction. | Rollback restores state. |
| Power BI later sees no tables | Wrong database/schema/permission or import selection. | SSMS context and view/table queries. | Use NorthstarRetail_DW and read-only rights on dw/semantic. | SQL query succeeds. |

For deeper tool-specific diagnosis, use [`the troubleshooting index near the end of this workbook`](#complete-troubleshooting-index).

### Optional reference answer for `sql/sqlserver/warehouse/01_create_warehouse.sql`

Attempt the file construction first. This reference is learning material, not evidence that you created or ran the file.

**Language:** SQL  
**Exact file:** `sql/sqlserver/warehouse/01_create_warehouse.sql`  
**Purpose:** database or lakehouse definitions and queries.  
**Inputs:** The requirements, configuration, source data, or upstream objects described in Phase 15.  
**Expected outputs:** The file's declared objects, logs, tables, checks, or documentation when the user later runs or reads it.

```sql
-- Dialect: SQL Server / T-SQL
-- Purpose: create the local serving warehouse NorthstarRetail_DW.
-- Run in: SSMS connected to your local SQL Server instance.
-- Safety: creates missing objects; it does not drop populated tables.

USE master;
GO
IF DB_ID(N'NorthstarRetail_DW') IS NULL CREATE DATABASE NorthstarRetail_DW;
GO
USE NorthstarRetail_DW;
GO
IF SCHEMA_ID(N'dw') IS NULL EXEC(N'CREATE SCHEMA dw AUTHORIZATION dbo;');
IF SCHEMA_ID(N'stg') IS NULL EXEC(N'CREATE SCHEMA stg AUTHORIZATION dbo;');
IF SCHEMA_ID(N'audit') IS NULL EXEC(N'CREATE SCHEMA audit AUTHORIZATION dbo;');
IF SCHEMA_ID(N'semantic') IS NULL EXEC(N'CREATE SCHEMA semantic AUTHORIZATION dbo;');
GO

IF OBJECT_ID(N'audit.etl_batch', N'U') IS NULL
CREATE TABLE audit.etl_batch
(
    batch_id VARCHAR(80) PRIMARY KEY,
    process_name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
    status VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,
    started_at_utc DATETIME2(3) NOT NULL,

    CONSTRAINT FK_fact_sales_date FOREIGN KEY (order_date_key) REFERENCES dw.dim_date(date_key),
    CONSTRAINT FK_fact_sales_customer FOREIGN KEY (customer_key) REFERENCES dw.dim_customer(customer_key),
    CONSTRAINT FK_fact_sales_product FOREIGN KEY (product_key) REFERENCES dw.dim_product(product_key),

    CONSTRAINT FK_fact_sales_promotion FOREIGN KEY (promotion_key) REFERENCES dw.dim_promotion(promotion_key),

);

### Optional reference answer for `sql/sqlserver/warehouse/02_create_staging_tables.sql`

Attempt the file construction first. This reference is learning material, not evidence that you created or ran the file.

**Language:** SQL  
**Exact file:** `sql/sqlserver/warehouse/02_create_staging_tables.sql`  
**Purpose:** database or lakehouse definitions and queries.  
**Inputs:** The requirements, configuration, source data, or upstream objects described in Phase 15.  
**Expected outputs:** The file's declared objects, logs, tables, checks, or documentation when the user later runs or reads it.

```sql
-- Dialect: SQL Server / T-SQL
-- Purpose: create empty staging tables that mirror warehouse targets.
-- Run after 01_create_warehouse.sql in NorthstarRetail_DW.
USE NorthstarRetail_DW;
GO

DECLARE @table sysname;
DECLARE table_cursor CURSOR LOCAL FAST_FORWARD FOR
SELECT name FROM sys.tables WHERE schema_id = SCHEMA_ID('dw');
OPEN table_cursor;
FETCH NEXT FROM table_cursor INTO @table;
WHILE @@FETCH_STATUS = 0
BEGIN
    DECLARE @stage sysname = N'stg_' + @table;
    IF OBJECT_ID(QUOTENAME('stg') + N'.' + QUOTENAME(@stage), N'U') IS NULL
    BEGIN
        DECLARE @sql nvarchar(max) = N'SELECT TOP (0) * INTO stg.' + QUOTENAME(@stage) + N' FROM dw.' + QUOTENAME(@table) + N';';
        EXEC sys.sp_executesql @sql;
    END;
    FETCH NEXT FROM table_cursor INTO @table;
END;
CLOSE table_cursor;
DEALLOCATE table_cursor;
GO
SELECT TABLE_SCHEMA, TABLE_NAME FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TABLES WHERE TABLE_SCHEMA='stg' ORDER BY TABLE_NAME;
```

### Optional reference answer for `scripts/loading/load_gold_to_sqlserver.py`

Attempt the file construction first. This reference is learning material, not evidence that you created or ran the file.

**Language:** Python  
**Exact file:** `scripts/loading/load_gold_to_sqlserver.py`  
**Purpose:** executable Python logic.  
**Inputs:** The requirements, configuration, source data, or upstream objects described in Phase 15.  
**Expected outputs:** The file's declared objects, logs, tables, checks, or documentation when the user later runs or reads it.

```python
"""Track A local loader: publish downloaded Gold exports to NorthstarRetail_DW safely.

The required beginner mode is ``full-dev`` for a disposable learning warehouse. It stages and
validates every table before changing targets, deletes child facts before parent dimensions,
inserts parents before children with explicit noncomputed columns, and commits once.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import logging
from datetime import UTC, datetime
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

import pandas as pd
from sqlalchemy import Connection, text

from scripts.utilities.config import load_environment
from scripts.utilities.database import sqlserver_warehouse_engine
from scripts.utilities.logging_utils import configure_logging

LOGGER = logging.getLogger("northstar.publish_gold")
DIMENSION_TABLES = [
    "dim_date", "dim_customer", "dim_product", "dim_store", "dim_employee",
    "dim_supplier", "dim_promotion", "dim_channel", "dim_campaign",
]
FACT_TABLES = [
    "fact_sales", "fact_returns", "fact_inventory_snapshot", "fact_shipments",
    "fact_web_sessions", "fact_marketing_spend",
]
TABLE_ORDER = DIMENSION_TABLES + FACT_TABLES


def read_export(path: Path) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Read one downloaded Spark Parquet directory/file or CSV file."""
    if path.suffix.lower() == ".parquet":
        return pd.read_parquet(path)
    if path.suffix.lower() == ".csv":
        return pd.read_csv(path)
    raise ValueError(f"Unsupported Gold export path: {path}")


def find_export(input_dir: Path, table: str) -> Path:
    """Find exactly one ``table.parquet`` or ``table.csv`` export."""
    candidates = [input_dir / f"{table}.parquet", input_dir / f"{table}.csv"]
    existing = [path for path in candidates if path.exists()]
    if len(existing) != 1:
        raise FileNotFoundError(
            f"Expected exactly one Gold export for {table}; found {existing} in {input_dir}"
        )
    return existing[0]


def quote_identifier(name: str) -> str:
    """Quote a trusted SQL Server identifier after a strict local allow-list check."""
    if not name.replace("_", "").isalnum():
        raise ValueError(f"Unsafe identifier: {name!r}")
    return f"[{name}]"


def insertable_columns(connection: Connection, table: str) -> list[str]:
    """Return target columns excluding identity and computed columns, in physical order."""
    rows = connection.execute(
        text(
            """
            SELECT c.name
            FROM sys.columns AS c
            WHERE c.object_id = OBJECT_ID(:object_name)
              AND c.is_identity = 0
              AND c.is_computed = 0
            ORDER BY c.column_id;
            """
        ),
        {"object_name": f"dw.{table}"},
    ).fetchall()
    columns = [str(row[0]) for row in rows]
    if not columns:
        raise RuntimeError(f"No insertable columns found for dw.{table}")
    return columns


def stage_all(connection: Connection, input_dir: Path) -> tuple[dict[str, pd.DataFrame], list[dict[str, Any]]]:
    """Read and stage every table before any target row is deleted."""
    frames: dict[str, pd.DataFrame] = {}
    results: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    for table in TABLE_ORDER:
        export_path = find_export(input_dir, table)
        frame = read_export(export_path)
        if frame.empty and table in {"dim_date", "dim_channel"}:
            raise ValueError(f"Required reference table {table} is empty")
        stage = f"stg_{table}"
        connection.execute(text(f"TRUNCATE TABLE stg.{quote_identifier(stage)};"))
        frame.to_sql(
            stage,
            connection,
            schema="stg",
            if_exists="append",
            index=False,
            chunksize=1000,
            method="multi",
        )
        staged_count = int(
            connection.execute(text(f"SELECT COUNT_BIG(*) FROM stg.{quote_identifier(stage)};")).scalar_one()
        )
        if staged_count != len(frame):
            raise AssertionError(
                f"Staging mismatch for {table}: file={len(frame)} stage={staged_count}"
            )
        frames[table] = frame
        results.append(
            {
                "table": table,
                "export_path": str(export_path),
                "file_rows": len(frame),
                "staged_rows": staged_count,
            }
        )
    return frames, results


def full_dev_publish(connection: Connection, results: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> None:
    """Replace a disposable development warehouse in foreign-key-safe order."""
    for table in FACT_TABLES:
        connection.execute(text(f"DELETE FROM dw.{quote_identifier(table)};"))
    for table in reversed(DIMENSION_TABLES):
        connection.execute(text(f"DELETE FROM dw.{quote_identifier(table)};"))

    for table in TABLE_ORDER:
        columns = insertable_columns(connection, table)
        quoted_columns = ", ".join(quote_identifier(column) for column in columns)
        stage = f"stg_{table}"
        connection.execute(
            text(
                f"INSERT INTO dw.{quote_identifier(table)} ({quoted_columns}) "
                f"SELECT {quoted_columns} FROM stg.{quote_identifier(stage)};"
            )
        )
        target_count = int(
            connection.execute(text(f"SELECT COUNT_BIG(*) FROM dw.{quote_identifier(table)};")).scalar_one()
        )
        result = next(item for item in results if item["table"] == table)
        result["target_rows"] = target_count
        if target_count != result["staged_rows"]:
            raise AssertionError(
                f"Target mismatch for {table}: stage={result['staged_rows']} target={target_count}"
            )


def write_artifact(batch_id: str, status: str, results: list[dict[str, Any]], error: str | None = None) -> Path:
    """Write a local nonsecret publication summary."""
    output_dir = Path("run_artifacts")
    output_dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    path = output_dir / f"{batch_id}.json"
    path.write_text(
        json.dumps({"batch_id": batch_id, "status": status, "error": error, "tables": results}, indent=2),
        encoding="utf-8",
    )
    return path


def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--input-dir", type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--mode", choices=["full-dev", "incremental"], default="full-dev")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    if args.mode == "incremental":
        raise NotImplementedError(
            "TODO(USER): implement and test the Phase 15 incremental strategy only after full-dev is verified."
        )
    if not args.input_dir.exists():
        raise FileNotFoundError(args.input_dir)

    configure_logging()
    load_environment()
    batch_id = f"PUB-{datetime.now(UTC):%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ}"
    engine = sqlserver_warehouse_engine()
    results: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    try:
        with engine.begin() as connection:
            connection.execute(
                text(
                    "INSERT INTO audit.etl_batch"
                    "(batch_id, process_name, status, started_at_utc) "
                    "VALUES (:batch_id, 'publish_gold', 'RUNNING', SYSUTCDATETIME())"
                ),
                {"batch_id": batch_id},
            )
            _, results = stage_all(connection, args.input_dir)
            full_dev_publish(connection, results)
            connection.execute(
                text(
                    "UPDATE audit.etl_batch SET status='SUCCESS', "
                    "finished_at_utc=SYSUTCDATETIME() WHERE batch_id=:batch_id"
                ),
                {"batch_id": batch_id},
            )
        artifact = write_artifact(batch_id, "SUCCESS", results)
        LOGGER.info("Published batch %s; artifact=%s", batch_id, artifact)
    except Exception as exc:
        # The data transaction above rolls back. Record failure in a separate transaction.
        try:
            with engine.begin() as connection:
                connection.execute(
                    text(
                        "INSERT INTO audit.etl_batch"
                        "(batch_id, process_name, status, started_at_utc, finished_at_utc, error_message) "
                        "VALUES (:batch_id, 'publish_gold', 'FAILED', SYSUTCDATETIME(), "
                        "SYSUTCDATETIME(), :error_message)"
                    ),
                    {"batch_id": batch_id, "error_message": str(exc)[:2000]},
                )
        except Exception:
            LOGGER.exception("Could not record failed publication audit row")
        write_artifact(batch_id, "FAILED", results, str(exc))
        raise


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

### Optional reference answer for `sql/sqlserver/validation/02_validate_warehouse.sql`

Attempt the file construction first. This reference is learning material, not evidence that you created or ran the file.

**Language:** SQL  
**Exact file:** `sql/sqlserver/validation/02_validate_warehouse.sql`  
**Purpose:** database or lakehouse definitions and queries.  
**Inputs:** The requirements, configuration, source data, or upstream objects described in Phase 15.  
**Expected outputs:** The file's declared objects, logs, tables, checks, or documentation when the user later runs or reads it.

```sql
-- Dialect: SQL Server / T-SQL
USE NorthstarRetail_DW;
GO

-- Duplicate fact grain should be zero.
SELECT order_item_id, COUNT_BIG(*) AS duplicate_count
FROM dw.fact_sales GROUP BY order_item_id HAVING COUNT_BIG(*) > 1;

-- Orphan dimension keys should be zero; key 0 is valid and means Unknown.
SELECT COUNT_BIG(*) AS orphan_customer_keys
FROM dw.fact_sales f LEFT JOIN dw.dim_customer d ON d.customer_key=f.customer_key
WHERE d.customer_key IS NULL;

-- SCD2 dimensions: no more than one current row per business key.
SELECT customer_number, COUNT_BIG(*) AS current_count
FROM dw.dim_customer WHERE is_current=1
GROUP BY customer_number HAVING COUNT_BIG(*) > 1;

SELECT sku, COUNT_BIG(*) AS current_count
FROM dw.dim_product WHERE is_current=1
GROUP BY sku HAVING COUNT_BIG(*) > 1;

-- Revenue identity: net sales equals gross minus discount.
SELECT COUNT_BIG(*) AS invalid_revenue_rows
FROM dw.fact_sales
WHERE ABS(net_sales_amount - (gross_sales_amount - discount_amount)) > 0.01;

-- Inspect the most recent ETL and reconciliation results.
SELECT TOP (20) * FROM audit.etl_batch ORDER BY started_at_utc DESC;
SELECT TOP (50) * FROM audit.reconciliation_result ORDER BY checked_at_utc DESC;
```

### Optional reference answer for `sql/sqlserver/warehouse/03_semantic_views.sql`

Attempt the file construction first. This reference is learning material, not evidence that you created or ran the file.

**Language:** SQL  
**Exact file:** `sql/sqlserver/warehouse/03_semantic_views.sql`  
**Purpose:** database or lakehouse definitions and queries.  
**Inputs:** The requirements, configuration, source data, or upstream objects described in Phase 15.  
**Expected outputs:** The file's declared objects, logs, tables, checks, or documentation when the user later runs or reads it.

```sql
-- Dialect: SQL Server / T-SQL
-- Purpose: thin semantic access views for analysts and Power BI.
USE NorthstarRetail_DW;
GO

CREATE OR ALTER VIEW semantic.vw_sales_detail AS
SELECT
    fs.order_number,
    dd.full_date AS order_date,
    dc.customer_number,
    CONCAT(dc.first_name, ' ', dc.last_name) AS customer_name,
    dp.sku,
    dp.product_name,
    dp.category_name,
    ds.store_name,
    ds.region,
    dch.channel_name,
    fs.quantity,
    fs.net_sales_amount,
    fs.cost_of_goods_sold,
    fs.gross_profit_amount,
    fs.discount_amount,
    fs.tax_amount
FROM dw.fact_sales AS fs
JOIN dw.dim_date AS dd ON dd.date_key = fs.order_date_key
JOIN dw.dim_customer AS dc ON dc.customer_key = fs.customer_key
JOIN dw.dim_product AS dp ON dp.product_key = fs.product_key
JOIN dw.dim_store AS ds ON ds.store_key = fs.store_key
JOIN dw.dim_channel AS dch ON dch.channel_key = fs.channel_key;
GO

CREATE OR ALTER VIEW semantic.vw_executive_daily_kpi AS
SELECT
    dd.full_date,
    SUM(fs.net_sales_amount) AS total_revenue,
    SUM(fs.gross_profit_amount) AS gross_profit,
    COUNT(DISTINCT fs.order_id) AS orders,
    SUM(fs.quantity) AS units_sold,
    CAST(SUM(fs.net_sales_amount) / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT fs.order_id), 0) AS DECIMAL(18,2)) AS average_order_value
FROM dw.fact_sales AS fs
JOIN dw.dim_date AS dd ON dd.date_key = fs.order_date_key
GROUP BY dd.full_date;
GO

CREATE OR ALTER VIEW semantic.vw_data_quality_monitor AS
SELECT batch_id, check_name, source_value, target_value, difference_value, status, checked_at_utc
FROM audit.reconciliation_result;
GO
```

<a id="warehouse-dw-dimdate"></a>
### SQL Server warehouse object 1 — `dw.dim_date`

**Object type:** dimension.  
**Responsibility:** Preserve or present exported Gold file for the verified batch in the local dimensional warehouse without inventing direct cloud-to-laptop connectivity.  
**Grain:** Match the corresponding Gold object exactly for dimensions/facts; staging retains one row per exported record; audit tables retain one row per load/check event.  
**Keys and constraints:** Dimensions use surrogate primary keys and business-key/history rules; facts use foreign keys/indexes appropriate to the declared grain; staging favors load/reconciliation metadata before final constraints.  
**Load metadata:** `load_batch_id`, source filename/checksum, loaded timestamp, row count, and load status.  
**Rerun rule:** The loader identifies the batch and target state before inserting, replacing, or rejecting a duplicate load.

GO

<a id="warehouse-dw-dimcustomer"></a>
### SQL Server warehouse object 2 — `dw.dim_customer`

**Object type:** dimension.  
**Responsibility:** Preserve or present exported Gold file for the verified batch in the local dimensional warehouse without inventing direct cloud-to-laptop connectivity.  
**Grain:** Match the corresponding Gold object exactly for dimensions/facts; staging retains one row per exported record; audit tables retain one row per load/check event.

**Load metadata:** `load_batch_id`, source filename/checksum, loaded timestamp, row count, and load status.  
**Rerun rule:** The loader identifies the batch and target state before inserting, replacing, or rejecting a duplicate load.

### SQL Server warehouse object 5 — `dw.dim_employee`

**Object type:** dimension.  
**Responsibility:** Preserve or present exported Gold file for the verified batch in the local dimensional warehouse without inventing direct cloud-to-laptop connectivity.  
**Grain:** Match the corresponding Gold object exactly for dimensions/facts; staging retains one row per exported record; audit tables retain one row per load/check event.  
**Keys and constraints:** Dimensions use surrogate primary keys and business-key/history rules; facts use foreign keys/indexes appropriate to the declared grain; staging favors load/reconciliation metadata before final constraints.  
**Load metadata:** `load_batch_id`, source filename/checksum, loaded timestamp, row count, and load status.  
**Rerun rule:** The loader identifies the batch and target state before inserting, replacing, or rejecting a duplicate load.

**Object type:** dimension.  
**Responsibility:** Preserve or present exported Gold file for the verified batch in the local dimensional warehouse without inventing direct cloud-to-laptop connectivity.  
**Grain:** Match the corresponding Gold object exactly for dimensions/facts; staging retains one row per exported record; audit tables retain one row per load/check event.  
**Keys and constraints:** Dimensions use surrogate primary keys and business-key/history rules; facts use foreign keys/indexes appropriate to the declared grain; staging favors load/reconciliation metadata before final constraints.  
**Load metadata:** `load_batch_id`, source filename/checksum, loaded timestamp, row count, and load status.  
**Rerun rule:** The loader identifies the batch and target state before inserting, replacing, or rejecting a duplicate load.

<a id="warehouse-dw-factsales"></a>
### SQL Server warehouse object 10 — `dw.fact_sales`

**Object type:** fact.  
**Responsibility:** Preserve or present exported Gold file for the verified batch in the local dimensional warehouse without inventing direct cloud-to-laptop connectivity.  
**Grain:** Match the corresponding Gold object exactly for dimensions/facts; staging retains one row per exported record; audit tables retain one row per load/check event.  
**Keys and constraints:** Dimensions use surrogate primary keys and business-key/history rules; facts use foreign keys/indexes appropriate to the declared grain; staging favors load/reconciliation metadata before final constraints.  
**Load metadata:** `load_batch_id`, source filename/checksum, loaded timestamp, row count, and load status.  
**Rerun rule:** The loader identifies the batch and target state before inserting, replacing, or rejecting a duplicate load.

<a id="warehouse-dw-factshipments"></a>
### SQL Server warehouse object 13 — `dw.fact_shipments`

**Object type:** fact.  
**Responsibility:** Preserve or present exported Gold file for the verified batch in the local dimensional warehouse without inventing direct cloud-to-laptop connectivity.  
**Grain:** Match the corresponding Gold object exactly for dimensions/facts; staging retains one row per exported record; audit tables retain one row per load/check event.  
**Keys and constraints:** Dimensions use surrogate primary keys and business-key/history rules; facts use foreign keys/indexes appropriate to the declared grain; staging favors load/reconciliation metadata before final constraints.  
**Load metadata:** `load_batch_id`, source filename/checksum, loaded timestamp, row count, and load status.  
**Rerun rule:** The loader identifies the batch and target state before inserting, replacing, or rejecting a duplicate load.

### SQL Server warehouse object 15 — `dw.fact_marketing_spend`

**Object type:** fact.  
**Responsibility:** Preserve or present exported Gold file for the verified batch in the local dimensional warehouse without inventing direct cloud-to-laptop connectivity.

**Rerun rule:** The loader identifies the batch and target state before inserting, replacing, or rejecting a duplicate load.

### SQL Server warehouse object 18 — `dw.reconciliation_result`

**Object type:** audit.  
**Responsibility:** Preserve or present warehouse metadata and loaded tables in the local dimensional warehouse without inventing direct cloud-to-laptop connectivity.  
**Grain:** Match the corresponding Gold object exactly for dimensions/facts; staging retains one row per exported record; audit tables retain one row per load/check event.  
**Keys and constraints:** Dimensions use surrogate primary keys and business-key/history rules; facts use foreign keys/indexes appropriate to the declared grain; staging favors load/reconciliation metadata before final constraints.  
**Load metadata:** `load_batch_id`, source filename/checksum, loaded timestamp, row count, and load status.  
**Rerun rule:** The loader identifies the batch and target state before inserting, replacing, or rejecting a duplicate load.

### SQL Server warehouse object 23 — `stg.dim_employee`

**Object type:** staging.  
**Responsibility:** Preserve or present exported Gold file for the verified batch in the local dimensional warehouse without inventing direct cloud-to-laptop connectivity.

**Rerun rule:** The loader identifies the batch and target state before inserting, replacing, or rejecting a duplicate load.

<a id="warehouse-stg-dimchannel"></a>
### SQL Server warehouse object 26 — `stg.dim_channel`

**Object type:** staging.  
**Responsibility:** Preserve or present exported Gold file for the verified batch in the local dimensional warehouse without inventing direct cloud-to-laptop connectivity.  
**Grain:** Match the corresponding Gold object exactly for dimensions/facts; staging retains one row per exported record; audit tables retain one row per load/check event.  
**Keys and constraints:** Dimensions use surrogate primary keys and business-key/history rules; facts use foreign keys/indexes appropriate to the declared grain; staging favors load/reconciliation metadata before final constraints.  
**Load metadata:** `load_batch_id`, source filename/checksum, loaded timestamp, row count, and load status.  
**Rerun rule:** The loader identifies the batch and target state before inserting, replacing, or rejecting a duplicate load.

### SQL Server warehouse object 28 — `stg.fact_sales`

**Object type:** staging.  
**Responsibility:** Preserve or present exported Gold file for the verified batch in the local dimensional warehouse without inventing direct cloud-to-laptop connectivity.

**Rerun rule:** The loader identifies the batch and target state before inserting, replacing, or rejecting a duplicate load.

<a id="warehouse-stg-factshipments"></a>
### SQL Server warehouse object 31 — `stg.fact_shipments`

**Object type:** staging.  
**Responsibility:** Preserve or present exported Gold file for the verified batch in the local dimensional warehouse without inventing direct cloud-to-laptop connectivity.  
**Grain:** Match the corresponding Gold object exactly for dimensions/facts; staging retains one row per exported record; audit tables retain one row per load/check event.  
**Keys and constraints:** Dimensions use surrogate primary keys and business-key/history rules; facts use foreign keys/indexes appropriate to the declared grain; staging favors load/reconciliation metadata before final constraints.  
**Load metadata:** `load_batch_id`, source filename/checksum, loaded timestamp, row count, and load status.  
**Rerun rule:** The loader identifies the batch and target state before inserting, replacing, or rejecting a duplicate load.

<a id="warehouse-reporting-vwinventory"></a>
### SQL Server warehouse object 36 — `reporting.vw_inventory`

**Object type:** semantic view.  
**Responsibility:** Preserve or present warehouse metadata and loaded tables in the local dimensional warehouse without inventing direct cloud-to-laptop connectivity.  
**Grain:** Match the corresponding Gold object exactly for dimensions/facts; staging retains one row per exported record; audit tables retain one row per load/check event.  
**Keys and constraints:** Dimensions use surrogate primary keys and business-key/history rules; facts use foreign keys/indexes appropriate to the declared grain; staging favors load/reconciliation metadata before final constraints.  
**Load metadata:** `load_batch_id`, source filename/checksum, loaded timestamp, row count, and load status.  
**Rerun rule:** The loader identifies the batch and target state before inserting, replacing, or rejecting a duplicate load.

END;
GO

## Lesson 15.5 — Verify, troubleshoot, commit, teach back, and stop safely

## What your screen should look like before starting

The Phase 15 outputs are visible, all runs are finished, open files are saved, and you can state the active branch and execution context. Any error you encountered has a recorded message and has not been hidden by deleting evidence.

## Design decision — Local export-and-load versus direct JDBC publication

**Question:**  
How should cloud Gold data reach laptop SQL Server?

**Options considered:**

- Manual verified export and local load.
- Direct Databricks JDBC to localhost.
- Cloud warehouse target.

**Beginner path selected:**  
Use manual export-and-load for Track A.

**Why this path was selected:**  
A cloud workspace cannot normally reach a laptop loopback address; the selected method is honest and reproducible.

**Tradeoff:**  
The handoff is not fully automated.

**What a company might do instead:**  
A company uses routable private connectivity or publishes to a managed cloud warehouse.

**How to explain this in an interview:**  
I avoided false localhost connectivity and used a controlled export with row-count and checksum reconciliation before local warehouse loading.




## If you see Result A

Export manifest, staging counts, warehouse counts, and control totals reconcile. Record the exact result, perform the named independent verification, and continue only when the gate is satisfied.

## If you see Result B

A file/table is missing, the local loader partially fails, or totals differ across the handoff. Treat this as information, not permission to delete or overwrite. Follow the branch-specific diagnostic in the current action, preserve evidence, and continue only after the state is understood.

## If you see an error

Read the first meaningful error line, redact secrets, and verify the application, path, branch, server/database, catalog/schema, batch ID, parameters, version/tier, and object name. Run the smallest observational check first. Do not reset Git history, drop data, disable a rule, force-push, or replace the target merely to make the error disappear.

### Interpret `git status --short`

- `??` means untracked: Git sees a new path but it is not staged.
- ` M` means modified in the working tree but not staged.
- `M ` means the staged version differs from the last commit.
- `MM` means a staged version exists and the file has additional unstaged edits.
- `A ` means staged as a new file.
- `D` means deletion; stop and investigate unless deletion is deliberate.
- `R` means rename; inspect both old and new paths.
- A blank result means the working tree is clean. It does not prove database, Databricks, or Power BI work occurred.

### Push-rejected recovery

If Git says the remote contains work you do not have, do not use `--force`. Run `git fetch origin`, inspect `git log --oneline --graph --decorate --all -20`, then rebase or merge only after understanding the divergence. Resolve conflicts one file at a time, run tests again, and push normally. A rejection protects remote work; it is not permission to overwrite it.

1. Multiple choice: Why does Phase 15 occur at this point in the source-to-consumption chain? A) Because menu order is arbitrary. B) Because its verified upstream input now exists. C) Because later phases do not depend on it. D) To create portfolio screenshots before validation.
2. True or false: A command that displays no error is automatically verified even when it ran in the wrong folder, database, catalog, schema, branch, or filter context.
3. Fill in the blank: The statement that defines what one row represents is the table or entity ________.
4. What command would you use first to confirm the PowerShell current folder before a repository command?
5. Troubleshooting: Your output differs from the example. What should you check before deleting, overwriting, resetting, force-pushing, or weakening a test?
6. Design choice: Explain one tradeoff of Track A and one production alternative.
7. Code reading: Why are input, accepted, rejected, and deduplicated counts recorded separately?
8. Ownership: Which status may you select only after personally performing and inspecting the verification?

---

## Mini quiz answer key and explanations

**1. B.** This phase is ordered after its prerequisites so its output has a trustworthy input. A is wrong because order is intentional; C is wrong because later phases depend on the handoff; D is wrong because screenshots follow verification.

**2. False.** Lack of an error proves only that the application accepted something; context and independent verification still matter.

**3. Grain.** Grain is the precise meaning of one row. A key identifies a row, but it does not by itself state the row’s business meaning.

**4. `Get-Location`.** It shows the shell’s current folder. `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` separately verifies the repository root when inside a clone.

**5.** Check application, folder/path, branch, server/database, catalog/schema, batch ID, parameters, source/target grain, filter context, version/tier differences, and the first meaningful error. Destructive changes are not a diagnostic step.

**6.** Track A has manual upload/download boundaries and batch latency. A production alternative is routable private connectivity with cloud object storage/managed warehouse, identities, and automated orchestration.

**7.** Separate counts make every row outcome explainable. A single final count can hide silent drops, duplicates, or records that moved to quarantine.

**8. `Verified by me` / `VERIFIED BY USER`.** `PLANNED`, `CREATED BY USER`, and `RUN BY USER` describe earlier states; only inspected evidence supports verification.

# Phase 16 — Build and validate the Power BI semantic model

[Back to the master table of contents](#master-table-of-contents)

**Track:** Track A required  
**Status when first opened:** `PLANNED`

## Why this phase happens now

**Earlier work this phase depends on:** A validated star-schema semantic model and measures.  
**What would go wrong if it happened earlier:** You would create objects without a verified requirement, valid upstream input, protected repository state, or known execution environment.  
**Later work that depends on it:** Phase 17 uses those governed fields to construct report pages and visual interactions.  
**Decision being made:** Choose and verify the simplest local-first method that teaches the professional concept without pretending that local services are publicly reachable.  
**Alternatives:** A company could use managed cloud databases, infrastructure as code, service principals, direct JDBC publication, deployment bundles, or streaming. Those options are discussed as tradeoffs, not substituted silently.  
**Beginner path selected:** Track A: local SQL Server and PostgreSQL, Python batch extracts, manual governed upload to Databricks, Delta Bronze/Silver/Gold, manual verified export, local SQL Server warehouse, and Power BI Import.  
**Reason for the order:** Requirements become source decisions; sources become generated data; source data becomes extraction batches; batches become Bronze; Bronze becomes Silver; Silver becomes Gold; Gold becomes warehouse and Power BI input.

## Three-level explanation of the phase

### Level 1 — Child-simple explanation

Imagine building a store from labeled boxes. This phase handles one box, checks that the label is correct, and makes sure the next box receives the right thing. You do not pour all boxes together and hope the result is understandable.

### Level 2 — Northstar Retail project explanation

Phase 16 creates the specific Northstar Retail files, database objects, transformations, tests, model objects, or evidence described in the lessons. Every output keeps a visible connection to its source and batch so you can trace an order, customer, product, campaign, return, shipment, or inventory record.

### Level 3 — Professional explanation

This phase establishes a controlled boundary in an end-to-end batch platform. It defines contracts, execution context, idempotency behavior, quality expectations, evidence, and handoff artifacts so the downstream layer can be reproduced and reviewed independently.

## Lesson 16.2 — Perform the notebook-guided actions one at a time

## What your screen should look like before starting

## Retained phase lesson, exercises, rules, and expected results

> **Track:** Track A required  
> **Ownership status at start:** Workbook instructions exist; your execution is not yet verified.  
> **Evidence rule:** Replace placeholders only after the verification steps pass.

## 1. What you are building

A Power BI semantic model over `NorthstarRetail_DW` with a proper date table, one-to-many single-direction relationships, hidden technical columns, documented business measures, useful hierarchies, display folders, and a Databricks SQL view alternative. This workbook supplies exact model documentation and optional reference DAX; you create and verify the `.pbix` yourself so the portfolio evidence is genuinely yours.

## 2. Why it matters

The semantic layer gives every report the same business definitions. Without it, two analysts can calculate revenue, returns, or conversion differently even when they read the same warehouse tables.

## 3. Words to know

| Term | Plain-language definition |
| --- | --- |
| Semantic model | Reusable tables, relationships, measures, formats, and business definitions used by reports. |
| DAX | Data Analysis Expressions, the formula language used for Power BI measures and calculated objects. |
| Measure | A calculation evaluated under the current report filters, such as Total Revenue. |
| Filter context | The active filters from slicers, rows, columns, relationships, and visual selections. |
| Import | Power BI copies data into its in-memory model during refresh. |
| DirectQuery | Power BI sends queries to the source when a visual needs data. |
| Cardinality | How many matching rows can exist on each side of a relationship. |
| Cross-filter direction | The direction in which a filter travels through a relationship. |
| Date table | A complete one-row-per-date dimension used for time intelligence. |
| Explicit measure | A named DAX calculation rather than an automatic column aggregation. |
| Display folder | A model organization label for related measures. |
| Hierarchy | An ordered drill path, such as Year > Quarter > Month > Date. |
| Default summarization | Whether a numeric column is summed automatically; keys should normally be Do not summarize. |
| Databricks SQL view | A saved SQL query that presents business-friendly columns as an alternate semantic access path. |

## 4. What must already be completed

Phase 15 is verified: `NorthstarRetail_DW` exists, semantic views query successfully, dimensions and facts reconcile to the selected Gold batch, and the account you will use can read the `dw` or `semantic` schema.

## 5. Applications to open

| Application | How to open it | Why it is open |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Power BI Desktop | Windows Start menu > search Power BI Desktop > Open. | Create the model and report file. |
| SSMS | Open from Start and connect to the verified local SQL Server. | Validate every measure against SQL. |
| VS Code | Open the repository and `powerbi/` folder. | Read the model contract and copy reviewed DAX one measure at a time. |
| Databricks SQL editor | Workspace > SQL > SQL Editor, if your tier exposes it. | Create/query the optional semantic views. |

## 6. Exact click-by-click steps
