## 7. Exact commands, one code block at a time

## 8. Where each command runs

Never infer the execution location from the code language. The command headings above identify the application and folder/database/catalog. Before every PowerShell command, run `Get-Location`; before SQL, verify the selected database; before Spark, print the catalog/schema/batch widgets.

## TEACHING EXAMPLE

The following small example or reference pattern explains the concept before you attempt Northstar-specific work. Read it, then complete **MY TASK** without copying the answer.

### Line-by-line code explanation

| Line or action | Meaning | Why it belongs here |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SELECT SUM(net_sales_amount) AS total_revenue, | Creates the unfiltered SQL baseline for three core measures. | The semantic model must reproduce warehouse truth before visual design begins. |
| Total Revenue = | Defines a reusable revenue measure that responds to report filters. | An explicit measure is documented and behaves consistently across visuals. |
| Gross Margin Percentage = | Calculates margin safely and returns blank when the denominator is zero. | DIVIDE handles zero/blank denominators more safely than `/`. |
| SELECT SUM(f.net_sales_amount) AS filtered_revenue | Builds a filter-matched validation query. | An all-data match does not prove relationships or filter context work. |
| SELECT order_date_key, | Provides a simple alternate semantic query path over Gold. | It demonstrates that the business definition is portable across serving tools. |

### Import versus DirectQuery decision

For the small local Track A portfolio, Import is the default: it is simpler, fast for interactive visuals, and does not require the local SQL Server to answer every click. DirectQuery keeps data at the source but adds source performance, concurrency, transformation, and feature considerations. Record the decision rather than calling one mode universally better.

### Relationship rule

A dimension has one row per key/version and filters a fact with many rows. Start with single-direction dimension-to-fact relationships. Bidirectional filtering can solve specific designs but can also create multiple filter paths and ambiguous totals; do not enable it as a quick fix.

### Required measures

`powerbi/measures.dax` contains Total Revenue, Gross Profit, Gross Margin Percentage, Promotion Gross Profit, Orders, Units Sold, Average Order Value, Return Rate, On-Time Delivery Percentage, Marketing Spend, Return on Ad Spend, Conversion Rate, New Customers, Returning Customers, Inventory On Hand, and Stockout Risk Count. Each measure includes a business explanation and SQL validation method.

## MY TASK

Build the Power BI model yourself, create all required relationships and measures, validate every measure under at least one nontrivial filter, and capture model/validation evidence without publishing fabricated KPI values.

## STARTER SKELETON

```dax
-- TODO(USER): type this only after defining the business rule.
Average Order Value =
DIVIDE (
    [Total Revenue],
    [Orders]
)

-- TODO(USER): validate the numerator and denominator separately in SQL.
-- TODO(USER): set format and description in Model view.
-- TODO(USER): record the filtered test in your learning journal.
```

**Acceptance criteria:** All 15 required tables load; relationships match the contract with no unexplained ambiguity; `dim_date` is marked; technical columns are hidden; every required measure has format, description, display folder, and SQL validation evidence; the saved PBIX is labeled as your own verified work.

## HINT 1 — CONCEPT

 A measure is only trustworthy when its table grain, relationship path, and denominator are understood.
## HINT 2 — PSEUDOCODE
 Create base measures first, validate them, then create ratios with DIVIDE and validate filtered cases.
## HINT 3 — NEAR-COMPLETE PATTERN
 Use `powerbi/measures.dax` and `sql/sqlserver/analytics/kpi_validation_queries.sql`; copy one measure, place it in a simple visual, match filters in SQL, and record the difference.

## 13. Expected files or output

- A local `Northstar_Retail_Portfolio.pbix` created by you.
- Model view screenshot showing the star-schema relationships.
- 15 documented DAX measures with correct formats.
- Measure validation table with SQL result, DAX result, difference, status, and filter definition.
- Optional Databricks SQL semantic-view/query evidence.

## 14. How to verify

- Every dimension key is unique on the one side.
- No relationship is many-to-many unless explicitly justified.
- Cross-filter direction is Single by default.
- Dates filter all applicable facts through the intended date key.
- Every unfiltered and filtered DAX result matches SQL within documented rounding tolerance.
- A zero-denominator case returns blank or the documented safe value.
- No technical ID is accidentally summed in a visual.

## 15. Automated tests

- SQL-to-DAX baseline tests for all measures.
- One-date, date-range, channel, store, product, and no-data filter tests.
- Relationship uniqueness query for each dimension key.
- Ambiguous-path inspection in Manage relationships.
- Refresh test after a controlled warehouse reload.

## 16. Common errors and exact fixes

| Message/symptom | Likely cause | Exact diagnostic | Safe fix | Verify |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| The relationship cannot be created because a column contains duplicate values | The supposed dimension key is not unique or an SCD2 business key was used instead of surrogate key. | Run `GROUP BY key HAVING COUNT(*) > 1` in SSMS. | Use the dimension surrogate key on the one side and fix duplicate dimension grain upstream. | The duplicate query returns zero and relationship is 1:*. |
| Power BI detected ambiguous relationships | Multiple active paths or bidirectional filters connect the same tables. | Open Manage relationships and trace every active path. | Return to single-direction star relationships; use inactive role-playing dates plus explicit DAX only when required. | No ambiguity warning and filtered totals match SQL. |
| Measure total looks wrong | Ratio/average was calculated row-by-row or an implicit aggregation was used. | Show numerator and denominator measures beside the total; run matching SQL. | Create explicit base measures and use DIVIDE at the intended grain. | Detail rows and grand total both match their SQL definitions. |
| Time intelligence is blank or inconsistent | Date table is not marked, dates are missing, or relationship uses the wrong date key. | Inspect min/max dates and missing dates in `dim_date`; check relationship. | Use a complete date dimension, mark it, and activate the intended date relationship. | Date slicer and monthly totals match SQL. |
| Refresh cannot connect | Wrong server/database, SQL service stopped, or credentials changed. | Confirm SSMS connection with the same server and database. | Start the service, correct data source settings, and re-enter credentials through Power BI UI. | Refresh completes and row counts remain reconciled. |

For deeper tool-specific diagnosis, use [`the troubleshooting index near the end of this workbook`](#complete-troubleshooting-index).

#### Folder-creation decision branches

##### If the folder is created

Run `Test-Path -LiteralPath ".\docs" -PathType Container` and require `True`.

##### If PowerShell says the folder already exists

##### If the parent path does not exist

Return to the parent-folder tutorial. Create and verify one parent level at a time; do not create the entire future tree in one command.

#### Verify the folder

1. Run `Test-Path ".\docs" -PathType Container`.
2. Require the output `True` before creating a child file.
3. Remember: Git does not track an empty folder by itself; the folder becomes visible in Git history when a tracked file is added.

### Optional reference answer for `powerbi/semantic_model.md`

Attempt the file construction first. This reference is learning material, not evidence that you created or ran the file.

**Language:** Markdown  
**Exact file:** `powerbi/semantic_model.md`  
**Purpose:** project documentation.  
**Inputs:** The requirements, configuration, source data, or upstream objects described in Phase 16.  
**Expected outputs:** The file's declared objects, logs, tables, checks, or documentation when the user later runs or reads it.

```markdown
# Power BI Semantic Model

## Model rule

Use a star schema. Every relationship normally filters from one dimension to one fact in a single direction. Avoid fact-to-fact relationships and bidirectional filtering unless you can explain and test the ambiguity it introduces.

## Relationships

| From dimension column | To fact column | Cardinality | Cross-filter | Active? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| dim_date[date_key] | fact_sales[order_date_key] | One-to-many | Single | Yes |
| dim_date[date_key] | fact_returns[return_date_key] | One-to-many | Single | Yes |
| dim_date[date_key] | fact_inventory_snapshot[snapshot_date_key] | One-to-many | Single | Yes |
| dim_date[date_key] | fact_shipments[ship_date_key] | One-to-many | Single | Yes |
| dim_date[date_key] | fact_shipments[promised_date_key] | One-to-many | Single | No |
| dim_date[date_key] | fact_shipments[delivery_date_key] | One-to-many | Single | No |
| dim_date[date_key] | fact_web_sessions[session_date_key] | One-to-many | Single | Yes |
| dim_date[date_key] | fact_marketing_spend[spend_date_key] | One-to-many | Single | Yes |
| dim_customer[customer_key] | fact_sales[customer_key] | One-to-many | Single | Yes |
| dim_customer[customer_key] | fact_shipments[customer_key] | One-to-many | Single | Yes |
| dim_customer[customer_key] | fact_web_sessions[customer_key] | One-to-many | Single | Yes |
| dim_customer[customer_key] | fact_returns[customer_key] | One-to-many | Single | Yes |
| dim_product[product_key] | fact_sales[product_key] | One-to-many | Single | Yes |
| dim_product[product_key] | fact_returns[product_key] | One-to-many | Single | Yes |
| dim_product[product_key] | fact_inventory_snapshot[product_key] | One-to-many | Single | Yes |
| dim_employee[employee_key] | fact_sales[employee_key] | One-to-many | Single | Yes |
| dim_promotion[promotion_key] | fact_sales[promotion_key] | One-to-many | Single | Yes |
| dim_store[store_key] | sales/returns/inventory/shipments store_key | One-to-many | Single | Yes |
| dim_channel[channel_key] | sales/web_sessions/marketing_spend channel_key | One-to-many | Single | Yes |
| dim_campaign[campaign_key] | web_sessions/marketing_spend campaign_key | One-to-many | Single | Yes |
| dim_supplier[supplier_code] | dim_product[supplier_code] | One-to-many | Single | Yes — documented snowflake exception |

### Supplier relationship note

`dim_supplier` is the one documented snowflake exception in the beginner model because the required facts do not carry a supplier key. Supplier filters travel through `dim_product`. Verify `dim_supplier[supplier_code]` is unique, keep the relationship single-direction, and do not add a second supplier-to-fact path. A larger production model may denormalize supplier attributes into `dim_product` or add supplier keys to appropriate procurement/inventory facts.

## Date table

In Model view, select `dim_date`, then **Table tools > Mark as date table > Mark as date table**, choose `full_date`, and confirm. Sort `month_name` by `month_number`. Create a hierarchy: `calendar_year > quarter_number > month_name > full_date`.

## Hidden technical columns

Hide surrogate keys from report view after relationships are correct: all `*_key` columns, batch ID, record hash, load timestamp, source system, SCD effective dates unless an audit page needs them. Do not delete them from the model.

## Display folders and formats

- `_Measures\Sales`: Total Revenue, Gross Profit, Gross Margin %, Promotion Gross Profit, Orders, Units Sold, Average Order Value.
- `_Measures\Returns and Shipping`: Return Rate, On-Time Delivery %.
- `_Measures\Marketing`: Marketing Spend, Attributed Revenue, Return on Ad Spend, Conversion Rate.
- `_Measures\Customer`: Purchasing Customers, New Customers, Returning Customers.
- `_Measures\Inventory`: Inventory On Hand, Stockout Risk Count.

Format money as currency with two decimals, counts as whole numbers with thousands separators, and rates as percentages with one or two decimals. Add the business definition from `docs/kpi_definitions.md` to each measure's Description property.

## Import versus DirectQuery decision

Use **Import** for Track A: the local warehouse is modest, development is faster, and you can control refresh manually. DirectQuery is an advanced choice when near-real-time access, data volume, governance, and capacity justify the latency and modeling tradeoffs. Record the choice in `docs/assumption_log.md`.

## Attribution warning

The included `Attributed Revenue` measure uses converting session order IDs, equivalent to a simplified last-converting-session link. It is not a multi-touch causal model. Test that an order ID appears once before presenting ROAS.
```

### Optional reference answer for `powerbi/measures.dax`

Attempt the file construction first. This reference is learning material, not evidence that you created or ran the file.

**Language:** DAX  
**Exact file:** `powerbi/measures.dax`  
**Purpose:** Power BI measures.  
**Inputs:** The requirements, configuration, source data, or upstream objects described in Phase 16.  
**Expected outputs:** The file's declared objects, logs, tables, checks, or documentation when the user later runs or reads it.

```dax
// Northstar Retail Power BI measures
// Put these in a dedicated empty table named _Measures.
// Replace column names only if your loaded warehouse schema differs.

Total Revenue =
SUM ( fact_sales[net_sales_amount] )

Gross Profit =
SUM ( fact_sales[gross_profit_amount] )

Gross Margin % =
DIVIDE ( [Gross Profit], [Total Revenue] )

Promotion Gross Profit =
CALCULATE (
    [Gross Profit],
    KEEPFILTERS ( dim_promotion[promotion_key] <> 0 )
)

Orders =
DISTINCTCOUNT ( fact_sales[order_id] )

Units Sold =
SUM ( fact_sales[quantity] )

Average Order Value =
DIVIDE ( [Total Revenue], [Orders] )

Returned Units =
SUM ( fact_returns[return_quantity] )

Return Rate =
DIVIDE ( [Returned Units], [Units Sold] )

Delivered Shipments =
CALCULATE (
    COUNTROWS ( fact_shipments ),
    NOT ISBLANK ( fact_shipments[delivery_date_key] )
)

On-Time Shipments =
CALCULATE (
    [Delivered Shipments],
    fact_shipments[on_time_flag] = TRUE ()
)

On-Time Delivery % =
DIVIDE ( [On-Time Shipments], [Delivered Shipments] )

Marketing Spend =
SUM ( fact_marketing_spend[spend_amount] )

Web Sessions =
SUM ( fact_web_sessions[session_count] )

Converted Sessions =
CALCULATE (
    [Web Sessions],
    fact_web_sessions[converted_flag] = TRUE ()
)

Conversion Rate =
DIVIDE ( [Converted Sessions], [Web Sessions] )

Attributed Revenue =
VAR ConvertedOrders =
    FILTER (
        VALUES ( fact_web_sessions[converted_order_id] ),
        NOT ISBLANK ( fact_web_sessions[converted_order_id] )
    )
RETURN
    CALCULATE (
        [Total Revenue],
        TREATAS ( ConvertedOrders, fact_sales[order_id] )
    )

Return on Ad Spend =
DIVIDE ( [Attributed Revenue], [Marketing Spend] )

Purchasing Customers =
CALCULATE (
    DISTINCTCOUNT ( fact_sales[customer_key] ),
    fact_sales[customer_key] <> 0
)

New Customers =
VAR PeriodStart = MIN ( dim_date[full_date] )
VAR PeriodEnd = MAX ( dim_date[full_date] )
RETURN
    COUNTROWS (
        FILTER (
            VALUES ( fact_sales[customer_key] ),
            fact_sales[customer_key] <> 0
                && VAR FirstOrderDate =
                    CALCULATE (
                        MIN ( dim_date[full_date] ),
                        REMOVEFILTERS ( dim_date )
                    )
                RETURN
                    FirstOrderDate >= PeriodStart
                        && FirstOrderDate <= PeriodEnd
        )
    )

Returning Customers =
[Purchasing Customers] - [New Customers]

Inventory On Hand =
SUM ( fact_inventory_snapshot[quantity_on_hand] )

Stockout Risk Count =
CALCULATE (
    COUNTROWS ( fact_inventory_snapshot ),
    fact_inventory_snapshot[stockout_risk_flag] = TRUE ()
)
```

### Power BI measure 1 — `Total Revenue`

**Business meaning:** Net merchandise sales after line discounts, before subtracting cost; tax is excluded.  
**Business formula:** SUM(net_sales_amount)  
**Filter context:** Slicers and relationships change the rows visible to the expression; numerator and denominator must use compatible populations.  
**Required tables/columns:** fact_sales  
**Important filters:** Exclude cancelled/invalid lines upstream; selected date/channel/product/store filters apply.  
**Recommended format:** Currency.

#### DAX definition

```dax
Total Revenue =
SUM ( fact_sales[net_sales_amount] )
```

#### Line-by-line DAX explanation

<a id="measure-promotion-gross-profit"></a>
### Power BI measure 4 — `Promotion Gross Profit`

**Business meaning:** Gross profit contributed by accepted sales that used a known promotion. Use it to compare promotion contribution, not to claim causal incremental lift.  
**Business formula:** SUM(gross_profit_amount) for promotion_key <> 0  
**Filter context:** Slicers and relationships change the rows visible to the expression; numerator and denominator must use compatible populations.  
**Required tables/columns:** fact_sales[gross_profit_amount,promotion_key]; dim_promotion[promotion_key,promotion_name,promotion_code,start_date,end_date]  
**Important filters:** Exclude unknown/no-promotion key 0; use the same accepted-sales, date, channel, and USD filters as Gross Profit.  
**Recommended format:** Currency.

#### DAX definition

```dax
Attributed Revenue =
VAR ConvertedOrders =
    FILTER (
        VALUES ( fact_web_sessions[converted_order_id] ),
        NOT ISBLANK ( fact_web_sessions[converted_order_id] )
    )
RETURN
    CALCULATE (
        [Total Revenue],
        TREATAS ( ConvertedOrders, fact_sales[order_id] )
    )
```

#### DAX definition

```dax
New Customers =
VAR PeriodStart = MIN ( dim_date[full_date] )
VAR PeriodEnd = MAX ( dim_date[full_date] )
RETURN
    COUNTROWS (
        FILTER (
            VALUES ( fact_sales[customer_key] ),
            fact_sales[customer_key] <> 0
                && VAR FirstOrderDate =
                    CALCULATE (
                        MIN ( dim_date[full_date] ),
                        REMOVEFILTERS ( dim_date )
                    )
                RETURN
                    FirstOrderDate >= PeriodStart
                        && FirstOrderDate <= PeriodEnd
        )
    )
```

<a id="measure-stockout-risk-count"></a>
### Power BI measure 23 — `Stockout Risk Count`

**Business meaning:** Count of store-product snapshot rows at or below their reorder threshold.  
**Business formula:** COUNTROWS where stockout_risk_flag = 1  
**Filter context:** Slicers and relationships change the rows visible to the expression; numerator and denominator must use compatible populations.  
**Required tables/columns:** fact_inventory_snapshot  
**Important filters:** Use latest or selected snapshot date.  
**Recommended format:** Whole number or appropriate numeric format.

#### DAX definition

```dax
Stockout Risk Count =
CALCULATE (
    COUNTROWS ( fact_inventory_snapshot ),
    fact_inventory_snapshot[stockout_risk_flag] = TRUE ()
)
```

## Design decision — Power BI Import versus DirectQuery

**Question:**  
How should Power BI access the local dimensional warehouse?

**Options considered:**

- Import.
- DirectQuery.
- Composite model.

**Beginner path selected:**  
Use Import for the required beginner model.

**Why this path was selected:**  
It is responsive, supports the full modeling experience, and suits the synthetic batch volume.

**Tradeoff:**  
Refresh is required to see new warehouse data.

**What a company might do instead:**  
Companies choose by latency, scale, governance, gateway, and semantic-model requirements.

**How to explain this in an interview:**  
I selected Import because the project is batch-oriented and small; I validated refresh totals against SQL and documented DirectQuery tradeoffs.




## If you see Result A

Relationships have the intended cardinality/direction and DAX matches filtered SQL. Record the exact result, perform the named independent verification, and continue only when the gate is satisfied.

## If you see Result B

Power BI proposes an ambiguous or many-to-many relationship, or a measure differs under the same filter. Treat this as information, not permission to delete or overwrite. Follow the branch-specific diagnostic in the current action, preserve evidence, and continue only after the state is understood.

### Interpret `git status --short`

- `??` means untracked: Git sees a new path but it is not staged.
- ` M` means modified in the working tree but not staged.
- `M ` means the staged version differs from the last commit.
- `MM` means a staged version exists and the file has additional unstaged edits.
- `A ` means staged as a new file.
- `D` means deletion; stop and investigate unless deletion is deliberate.
- `R` means rename; inspect both old and new paths.
- A blank result means the working tree is clean. It does not prove database, Databricks, or Power BI work occurred.

### Push-rejected recovery

If Git says the remote contains work you do not have, do not use `--force`. Run `git fetch origin`, inspect `git log --oneline --graph --decorate --all -20`, then rebase or merge only after understanding the divergence. Resolve conflicts one file at a time, run tests again, and push normally. A rejection protects remote work; it is not permission to overwrite it.

I verified the result in its owning application and connected the evidence to Git without claiming that displayed instructions were executed.”

## Mini quiz

1. Multiple choice: Why does Phase 16 occur at this point in the source-to-consumption chain? A) Because menu order is arbitrary. B) Because its verified upstream input now exists. C) Because later phases do not depend on it. D) To create portfolio screenshots before validation.
2. True or false: A command that displays no error is automatically verified even when it ran in the wrong folder, database, catalog, schema, branch, or filter context.
3. Fill in the blank: The statement that defines what one row represents is the table or entity ________.
4. What command would you use first to confirm the PowerShell current folder before a repository command?
5. Troubleshooting: Your output differs from the example. What should you check before deleting, overwriting, resetting, force-pushing, or weakening a test?
6. Design choice: Explain one tradeoff of Track A and one production alternative.
7. Code reading: Why are input, accepted, rejected, and deduplicated counts recorded separately?
8. Ownership: Which status may you select only after personally performing and inspecting the verification?

---

## Mini quiz answer key and explanations

**1. B.** This phase is ordered after its prerequisites so its output has a trustworthy input. A is wrong because order is intentional; C is wrong because later phases depend on the handoff; D is wrong because screenshots follow verification.

**2. False.** Lack of an error proves only that the application accepted something; context and independent verification still matter.

**3. Grain.** Grain is the precise meaning of one row. A key identifies a row, but it does not by itself state the row’s business meaning.

**4. `Get-Location`.** It shows the shell’s current folder. `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` separately verifies the repository root when inside a clone.

**5.** Check application, folder/path, branch, server/database, catalog/schema, batch ID, parameters, source/target grain, filter context, version/tier differences, and the first meaningful error. Destructive changes are not a diagnostic step.

**6.** Track A has manual upload/download boundaries and batch latency. A production alternative is routable private connectivity with cloud object storage/managed warehouse, identities, and automated orchestration.

**7.** Separate counts make every row outcome explainable. A single final count can hide silent drops, duplicates, or records that moved to quarantine.

**8. `Verified by me` / `VERIFIED BY USER`.** `PLANNED`, `CREATED BY USER`, and `RUN BY USER` describe earlier states; only inspected evidence supports verification.

# Phase 17 — Build and validate all Power BI report pages

[Back to the master table of contents](#master-table-of-contents)

**Track:** Track A required  
**Status when first opened:** `PLANNED`  
**Completion rule:** The phase is not complete because its instructions exist. Mark it `VERIFIED BY USER` only after you perform the work, inspect the output, and save evidence.

## Why this phase happens now

**Earlier work this phase depends on:** Accurate report pages and SQL-to-DAX validation evidence.  
**What would go wrong if it happened earlier:** You would create objects without a verified requirement, valid upstream input, protected repository state, or known execution environment.  
**Later work that depends on it:** Phase 18 reviews every location where secrets, compute cost, or sensitive data can appear.  
**Decision being made:** Choose and verify the simplest local-first method that teaches the professional concept without pretending that local services are publicly reachable.  
**Alternatives:** A company could use managed cloud databases, infrastructure as code, service principals, direct JDBC publication, deployment bundles, or streaming. Those options are discussed as tradeoffs, not substituted silently.  
**Beginner path selected:** Track A: local SQL Server and PostgreSQL, Python batch extracts, manual governed upload to Databricks, Delta Bronze/Silver/Gold, manual verified export, local SQL Server warehouse, and Power BI Import.  
**Reason for the order:** Requirements become source decisions; sources become generated data; source data becomes extraction batches; batches become Bronze; Bronze becomes Silver; Silver becomes Gold; Gold becomes warehouse and Power BI input.

## Lesson 17.1 — Understand the phase and starting screen

## What your screen should look like before starting

- **Application open:** Power BI Desktop Report view, Format pane, Selection pane, and SSMS validation windows.
- **Window in front:** The application named by the first action; do not keep an installer, database editor, notebook, and Power BI dialog stacked ambiguously.

- **Git branch:** A feature branch, not a detached commit. Run `git branch --show-current` and record the exact result.
- **Database/workspace connection:** The connection named in the action, not merely the most recent connection.
- **Files that should already exist:** Only files from verified earlier phases. Do not pre-create the full tree.
- **Files that should not exist yet:** New Phase 17 files remain absent until their creation lesson.
- **Terminal prompt:** It should end in the expected repository path or another explicitly named folder.
- **Previous verification:** Phase 16 must be verified when this phase has a prerequisite.

## Three-level explanation of the phase

### Level 1 — Child-simple explanation

Imagine building a store from labeled boxes. This phase handles one box, checks that the label is correct, and makes sure the next box receives the right thing. You do not pour all boxes together and hope the result is understandable.

### Level 2 — Northstar Retail project explanation

Phase 17 creates the specific Northstar Retail files, database objects, transformations, tests, model objects, or evidence described in the lessons. Every output keeps a visible connection to its source and batch so you can trace an order, customer, product, campaign, return, shipment, or inventory record.

### Level 3 — Professional explanation

This phase establishes a controlled boundary in an end-to-end batch platform. It defines contracts, execution context, idempotency behavior, quality expectations, evidence, and handoff artifacts so the downstream layer can be reproduced and reviewed independently.

## Applications to open

Power BI Desktop Report view, Format pane, Selection pane, and SSMS validation windows. Open only the application needed for the immediate action. Extra windows increase the chance of typing a command into the wrong context.

## Lesson 17.2 — Perform the notebook-guided actions one at a time

## What your screen should look like before starting

The Phase 17 start gate is checked, only the needed application is in front, and the current context has been verified. The following retained lesson material preserves the Northstar terminology and exercise framing; the action cards then turn each hands-on step into a written screen-recording sequence.

## Retained phase lesson, exercises, rules, and expected results

> **Track:** Track A required  
> **Ownership status at start:** Workbook instructions exist; your execution is not yet verified.  
> **Evidence rule:** Replace placeholders only after the verification steps pass.

## 1. What you are building

A nine-page Power BI report design, an executive KPI view, a data-quality monitoring page, a dashboard wireframe, drill-through plan, validation checklist, and at least 20 analyst SQL questions with query skeletons. You populate visuals only from your verified model and label incomplete pages honestly.

## 2. Why it matters

A technically correct platform has value only when people can answer business questions safely. Consumption design connects each audience, question, metric, filter, visual, and validation rule.

## 3. Words to know

| Term | Plain-language definition |
| --- | --- |
| Consumption layer | The reports, SQL queries, exports, or applications through which people use trusted data. |
| KPI card | A visual displaying one important measure, often with period context or target. |
| Slicer | A report control that changes filter context. |
| Drill-through | Navigation from a summary item to a detail page filtered to that item. |
| Tooltip page | A report page shown when a user hovers over a visual data point. |
| Wireframe | A layout plan showing where visuals and controls belong without claiming real results. |
| Executive view | A compact view of outcomes, changes, risks, and decisions rather than operational detail. |
| Operational view | A detailed view used to act on current process conditions. |
| Misleading chart | A visual whose scale, aggregation, category count, or encoding can cause a false interpretation. |
| Accessibility | Design that remains usable with keyboard navigation, readable text, adequate contrast, and meaningful labels. |

## 4. What must already be completed

The Phase 16 semantic model is verified and saved. Every measure used by a report page has a business definition and at least one SQL validation.

## 5. Applications to open

| Application | How to open it | Why it is open |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Power BI Desktop | Open your verified PBIX. | Build and test report pages. |
| SSMS | Connect to NorthstarRetail_DW. | Run analyst and visual-validation queries. |
| VS Code | Open `powerbi/dashboard_requirements.md` and the SQL analytics folder. | Follow the report contract and record evidence. |
| Web browser | Open the local HTML notebook/GitHub preview after screenshots are added. | Review portfolio presentation without publishing private details. |

## 6. Exact click-by-click steps

> **Beginner rhythm:** Read the whole step. Confirm the application and location. Perform only that step. Verify the visible result. Record an error before attempting a fix.

## 7. Exact commands, one code block at a time

## 8. Where each command runs

Never infer the execution location from the code language. The command headings above identify the application and folder/database/catalog. Before every PowerShell command, run `Get-Location`; before SQL, verify the selected database; before Spark, print the catalog/schema/batch widgets.

## TEACHING EXAMPLE

The following small example or reference pattern explains the concept before you attempt Northstar-specific work. Read it, then complete **MY TASK** without copying the answer.

### Line-by-line code explanation

| Line or action | Meaning | Why it belongs here |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SELECT TOP (20) | Returns the daily series used to validate a trend visual. | A chart should be checked at its displayed grain, not only as a grand total. |
| SELECT p.category_name, | Creates the category comparison baseline. | It verifies relationship filtering and category grouping. |
| Get-Content .\sql\sqlserver\analytics\20_analyst_questions.sql \| Select-String '^-- [0-9][0-9]\.' | Lists the analyst question headings included in the reference file. | You should know the scope before attempting queries. |
| python -m scripts.validation.validate_markdown_links | Checks report documentation links and screenshot placeholders resolve. | Portfolio navigation is part of the consumption experience. |

### Page contract

Each page in `powerbi/dashboard_requirements.md` states audience, business question, measures, dimensions, slicers, recommended visuals, drill-through, SQL validation, and a common misleading alternative. A visual is not selected because it looks impressive; it is selected because its encoding fits the question.

### Do not fabricate results

Wireframes may contain labels such as `[TOTAL REVENUE]` but not invented numbers. After your pipeline runs, replace placeholders only with values visible in a validated model and capture the data-through date and batch evidence.

## MY TASK

Build and validate the nine report pages, complete at least 20 analyst questions, add one useful drill-through path, and create screenshots that prove your own execution without exposing credentials or inventing performance claims.

## STARTER SKELETON

```text
PAGE: Inventory
AUDIENCE: TODO(USER)
DECISION: TODO(USER)
GRAIN SHOWN: TODO(USER)
MEASURES: Inventory On Hand; Stockout Risk Count
DIMENSIONS: TODO(USER)
SLICERS: TODO(USER)
VISUALS: TODO(USER)
DRILL-THROUGH: TODO(USER)
SQL VALIDATION: TODO(USER)
MISLEADING CHOICE TO AVOID: TODO(USER)
SCREENSHOT FILE: docs/images/TODO_USER_inventory_page.png
```

**Acceptance criteria:** All nine pages have a documented audience and question; every visible KPI uses an explicit validated measure; interactions and drill-through work; each critical visual matches a same-grain SQL query; accessibility checks are recorded; screenshots show only real verified results or clearly marked placeholders.

## HINT 1 — CONCEPT

 Start with the decision and grain, then choose the visual.
## HINT 2 — PSEUDOCODE
 For each visual: identify measure, grouping columns, filters, and SQL GROUP BY; compare the resulting rows.
## HINT 3 — NEAR-COMPLETE PATTERN
 Use the page contracts, add a table visual temporarily, match it to the provided SQL patterns, then replace it with the final visual after validation.

## 13. Expected files or output

- Nine named Power BI pages.
- One drill-through flow and useful tooltip behavior.
- Executive KPI and data-quality monitoring views.
- At least 20 attempted analyst queries with notes.
- Completed screenshot checklist and evidence files.
- A wireframe that contains no fabricated numbers.

## 14. How to verify

- Every page answers its stated business question.
- All visual grains and filters are documented.
- No implicit measures are used for published KPIs.
- Critical chart table views match SQL.
- Slicer interactions and synced slicers are intentional.
- Drill-through retains the correct context.
- Data-quality page exposes failed/quarantined checks rather than hiding them.
- Screenshots include a verified data-through context.

## 15. Automated tests

- Visual-to-SQL same-grain comparisons.
- Slicer interaction matrix.
- Drill-through context test.
- Empty/no-data state test.
- Accessibility/tab-order/alt-text review.
- Screenshot privacy and truthfulness review.

## 16. Common errors and exact fixes

| Message/symptom | Likely cause | Exact diagnostic | Safe fix | Verify |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A chart changes when an unrelated slicer is used | Synced slicer or visual interaction is broader than intended. | Use Edit interactions and inspect Sync slicers. | Disable the invalid interaction or redesign the page contract. | Only intended visuals change. |
| Grand total differs from the sum of visible percentages | The measure is recalculated in total filter context, which is often correct for ratios. | Display numerator/denominator at row and total levels. | Explain the ratio behavior; do not sum percentages unless the business rule truly requires it. | Total matches the SQL ratio definition. |
| Too many categories are unreadable | A categorical visual is overloaded. | Count distinct categories and inspect audience need. | Use Top N with an explicit Other/selection path, a table, or drill-through; disclose the filter. | All omitted categories remain accessible and no hidden bias is introduced. |
| Map or region visual is blank/wrong | Geographic category is ambiguous or unsupported. | Inspect data category, country/state fields, and null/invalid codes. | Set correct data category and use a bar/matrix if geography cannot be resolved safely. | Locations or alternative visual match source counts. |
| Screenshot shows a result that later changes | Refresh batch or filters were not recorded. | Check batch/load timestamp and active filters. | Capture a data-through date and evidence note; replace stale screenshots after a material change. | Screenshot and evidence point to the same run. |

For deeper tool-specific diagnosis, use [`the troubleshooting index near the end of this workbook`](#complete-troubleshooting-index).

1. How does the audience change the amount of detail on a page?
2. Why should a visual be validated at its displayed grain?
3. Why can a grand-total percentage correctly differ from the sum of row percentages?
4. What makes a dashboard screenshot trustworthy?

Capture each completed report page, one drill-through result, one Edit interactions view, and one SQL-to-visual validation. Use the Phase 17 in-workbook checklist; do not show fabricated numbers.

Save the image under `docs/images/` with a descriptive filename. Check that no credential, token, password, or unnecessary personal account detail is visible.

## 20. Git checkpoint and suggested commit message

Run `git status`, review the Source Control diff in VS Code, stage only the intended files, then commit:

```text

```

Push the feature branch only after tests pass.

**Command or code (Sql):**

```sql
SELECT TOP (20)
       d.full_date,
       SUM(f.net_sales_amount) AS total_revenue,
       SUM(f.gross_profit_amount) AS gross_profit
FROM dw.fact_sales AS f
JOIN dw.dim_date AS d ON d.date_key = f.order_date_key
GROUP BY d.full_date
ORDER BY d.full_date DESC;
```

SSMS query window (SQL Server / T-SQL). Do not enter terminal commands into a source-code file and do not paste expected output back into the editor.

### Optional reference answer for `powerbi/dashboard_requirements.md`

Attempt the file construction first. This reference is learning material, not evidence that you created or ran the file.

**Language:** Markdown  
**Exact file:** `powerbi/dashboard_requirements.md`  
**Purpose:** project documentation.  
**Inputs:** The requirements, configuration, source data, or upstream objects described in Phase 17.  
**Expected outputs:** The file's declared objects, logs, tables, checks, or documentation when the user later runs or reads it.

```markdown
# Power BI Report Requirements

No actual performance values are included. Replace every placeholder only after running and validating your pipeline.

| Page | Audience | Business question | Fields/KPIs | Slicers | Visuals | Drill-through | Validation | Misleading choice to avoid |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Executive Overview | Executives | Are revenue, profit, orders, delivery, and returns on track? | Revenue, gross profit, margin, orders, AOV, return rate, on-time delivery; monthly trend; channel mix | Date, region, channel | KPI cards, line chart, decomposition or bar chart | Sales Performance | Validate every KPI card to SQL; verify date slicer affects all visuals | Do not use a pie chart with many categories or a truncated trend axis. |
| Sales Performance | Sales leadership | Where are sales and profit growing or declining? | Revenue/profit by month, channel, store, region; order and AOV trends | Date, channel, region, store | Lines, clustered bars, matrix, waterfall for change | Order detail or Store and Region | Check totals and drill rows against semantic.vw_sales_detail | Do not mix revenue and margin percentages on one unlabeled axis. |
| Product and Category | Merchandising | Which products and categories drive profitable demand? | Revenue, units, gross profit, margin, discount by SKU/category | Date, category, brand, supplier | Treemap only for high-level mix, bars, scatter price vs margin, matrix | Product detail | Validate top N against analyst query 07 | Top revenue is not automatically top profit. |
| Store and Region | Retail operations | Which stores and regions outperform after accounting for volume? | Revenue, profit, orders, AOV, return rate by store/region | Date, region, store | Map only if location quality is verified; bars and matrix preferred | Store detail | Compare a selected store to SQL query 03 | Avoid maps that imply area size equals performance. |
| Customer | CRM and leadership | How many new and returning customers buy, and how do segments behave? | New/returning, purchasing customers, revenue by tier/state | Date, loyalty tier, state | Cards, cohort-style matrix, bars | Customer history | Inspect first purchase dates for sample customers | Do not label signup as acquisition unless business definition says so. |
| Marketing Funnel | Marketing | Which channels and campaigns create efficient, attributable conversion? | Spend, sessions, conversion, attributed revenue, ROAS | Date, channel, campaign, device | Funnel, scatter spend vs revenue, campaign table | Campaign detail | Verify converted order IDs are unique before ROAS | Correlation and last-touch attribution are not causation. |
| Inventory | Inventory operations | Which store-product combinations are at stockout risk? | On hand, available, inventory value, risk count | Snapshot date, region, store, category | Cards, heatmap/matrix, ranked bars | Product-store detail | Use one snapshot date; recompute risk formula | Never sum snapshot stock across dates. |
| Shipping and Returns | Operations and CX | Where are delivery delays and returns concentrated? | On-time %, delivery days, returned units, return rate, refund amount | Ship/return date, carrier, region, reason | Cards, bars, distribution, matrix | Shipment/order detail | Sample promised vs actual dates and returned lines | Do not compare shipment count directly with order count without split-shipment context. |
| Data Quality | Data engineering and owners | Can decision-makers trust the latest batch? | Pass/fail, quarantines, unknown keys, freshness, reconciliation differences | Batch, date, source, rule | Status cards, rule table, trend | Batch detail | Compare to quality.test_results and audit.reconciliation_result | A green dashboard is meaningless if failed tests were filtered out. |

## Suggested executive wireframe

```text
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Northstar Retail — Executive Overview       [Date] [Region] [Channel]           |
+-----------+-----------+-----------+-----------+-----------+--------------------+
| Revenue   | Gross     | Margin %  | Orders    | AOV       | On-time / Returns  |
| [VERIFY]  | [VERIFY]  | [VERIFY]  | [VERIFY]  | [VERIFY]  | [VERIFY]           |
+---------------------------------------------+----------------------------------+
| Monthly Revenue and Gross Profit Trend      | Revenue / Profit by Channel      |
| [YOUR VERIFIED VISUAL]                      | [YOUR VERIFIED VISUAL]           |
+---------------------------------------------+----------------------------------+
| Top/Bottom Category or Store                | Alerts: Stockout / DQ / Shipping |
| [YOUR VERIFIED VISUAL]                      | [YOUR VERIFIED VISUAL]           |
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```
```

### File introduction — `sql/sqlserver/analytics/20_analyst_questions.sql`

**Exact filename:** `20_analyst_questions.sql`  
**Filename extension:** `.sql`. In this project it identifies database or lakehouse definitions and queries and helps the correct application choose syntax highlighting or execution behavior.  
**Exact parent folder:** `sql/sqlserver/analytics` relative to the repository root.  
**Why this file belongs there:** Files with the same responsibility are grouped so a reviewer can find configuration, source SQL, transformations, tests, documentation, and report assets without guessing.  
**What the file will contain:** database or lakehouse definitions and queries for Phase 17.  
**Later dependencies:** Later phase commands, tests, GitHub Actions, Databricks tasks, warehouse loads, Power BI work, or portfolio evidence may depend on its exact path.  
**Should Git track it?** Yes, unless the lesson explicitly identifies it as generated data, a local secret, a log, or a machine-specific artifact.  
**Could it contain secrets?** It should not contain live passwords, tokens, connection strings, or account identifiers.  
**What happens if it is missing:** The corresponding phase cannot be reproduced, validated, or explained from the repository alone.

#### VS Code click path

1. CLICK: In VS Code, open **Explorer** from the left Activity Bar.
2. LOOK FOR: Confirm the top-level folder name is `SQL-Data-Warehouse-Project` and the status bar shows the intended Git branch.
3. CLICK: Expand each parent folder in `sql/sqlserver/analytics` one level at a time.
4. If a parent folder does not exist, use the folder tutorial in this phase before creating the file.

6. CLICK: Select **New File**.
7. TYPE THIS: `20_analyst_questions.sql`.

### Optional reference answer for `sql/sqlserver/analytics/20_analyst_questions.sql`

Attempt the file construction first. This reference is learning material, not evidence that you created or ran the file.

**Language:** SQL  
**Exact file:** `sql/sqlserver/analytics/20_analyst_questions.sql`  
**Purpose:** database or lakehouse definitions and queries.  
**Inputs:** The requirements, configuration, source data, or upstream objects described in Phase 17.  
**Expected outputs:** The file's declared objects, logs, tables, checks, or documentation when the user later runs or reads it.

```sql
-- Dialect: SQL Server / T-SQL
-- Teaching analyst questions. Complete each TODO(USER), compare to the reference appendix,
-- and record your validation in the learning journal.
USE NorthstarRetail_DW;
GO

-- 01. Revenue by month.
SELECT d.calendar_year, d.month_number, SUM(f.net_sales_amount) AS revenue
FROM dw.fact_sales f JOIN dw.dim_date d ON d.date_key=f.order_date_key
GROUP BY d.calendar_year,d.month_number ORDER BY d.calendar_year,d.month_number;

-- 02. Gross profit by category.
SELECT p.category_name, SUM(f.gross_profit_amount) AS gross_profit
FROM dw.fact_sales f JOIN dw.dim_product p ON p.product_key=f.product_key
GROUP BY p.category_name ORDER BY gross_profit DESC;

-- 03. Best-performing stores by revenue. TODO(USER): add order count and gross margin.
SELECT s.store_name, SUM(f.net_sales_amount) AS revenue
FROM dw.fact_sales f JOIN dw.dim_store s ON s.store_key=f.store_key
GROUP BY s.store_name ORDER BY revenue DESC;

-- 04. Online versus store average order value.
SELECT c.channel_name, SUM(f.net_sales_amount)/NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT f.order_id),0) AS average_order_value
FROM dw.fact_sales f JOIN dw.dim_channel c ON c.channel_key=f.channel_key
GROUP BY c.channel_name;

-- 05. Return rate by category. TODO(USER): define numerator and denominator at compatible grain.
-- Hint: aggregate return quantity and sold quantity separately before joining.

-- 06. On-time delivery percentage by carrier.
SELECT carrier, 100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN on_time_flag=1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/NULLIF(COUNT_BIG(*),0) AS on_time_pct
FROM dw.fact_shipments GROUP BY carrier;

-- 07. Top ten products by units sold.
SELECT TOP (10) p.sku,p.product_name,SUM(f.quantity) AS units
FROM dw.fact_sales f JOIN dw.dim_product p ON p.product_key=f.product_key
GROUP BY p.sku,p.product_name ORDER BY units DESC;

-- 08. Products with negative gross profit. TODO(USER): add a date filter.
SELECT p.sku,p.product_name,SUM(f.gross_profit_amount) AS gross_profit
FROM dw.fact_sales f JOIN dw.dim_product p ON p.product_key=f.product_key
GROUP BY p.sku,p.product_name HAVING SUM(f.gross_profit_amount)<0;

-- 09. Discount amount by promotion.
SELECT pr.promotion_name,SUM(f.discount_amount) AS discount_amount,SUM(f.net_sales_amount) AS revenue
FROM dw.fact_sales f JOIN dw.dim_promotion pr ON pr.promotion_key=f.promotion_key
GROUP BY pr.promotion_name ORDER BY discount_amount DESC;

-- 10. New customers by month. TODO(USER): use dim_customer.signup_date and avoid double-counting SCD2 versions.

-- 11. Returning customers by month. TODO(USER): define returning as a customer with an earlier order.

-- 12. Conversion rate by source channel.
SELECT c.channel_name,100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN f.converted_flag=1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/NULLIF(SUM(f.session_count),0) AS conversion_pct
FROM dw.fact_web_sessions f JOIN dw.dim_channel c ON c.channel_key=f.channel_key
GROUP BY c.channel_name;

-- 13. Marketing spend and clicks by campaign.
SELECT c.campaign_name,SUM(f.spend_amount) AS spend,SUM(f.clicks) AS clicks
FROM dw.fact_marketing_spend f JOIN dw.dim_campaign c ON c.campaign_key=f.campaign_key
GROUP BY c.campaign_name ORDER BY spend DESC;

-- 14. Return on ad spend. TODO(USER): decide and document an attribution rule before joining sales and spend.

-- 15. Stockout-risk products by store.
SELECT s.store_name,p.product_name,COUNT_BIG(*) AS risk_snapshot_count
FROM dw.fact_inventory_snapshot f
JOIN dw.dim_store s ON s.store_key=f.store_key
JOIN dw.dim_product p ON p.product_key=f.product_key
WHERE f.stockout_risk_flag=1 GROUP BY s.store_name,p.product_name;

-- 16. Inventory value by category.
SELECT p.category_name,SUM(f.inventory_value_amount) AS inventory_value
FROM dw.fact_inventory_snapshot f JOIN dw.dim_product p ON p.product_key=f.product_key
GROUP BY p.category_name;

-- 17. Average delivery days by region.
SELECT s.region,AVG(1.0*f.delivery_days) AS average_delivery_days
FROM dw.fact_shipments f JOIN dw.dim_store s ON s.store_key=f.store_key
GROUP BY s.region;

-- 18. Customers whose attributes changed under SCD2.
SELECT customer_number,COUNT_BIG(*) AS version_count
FROM dw.dim_customer GROUP BY customer_number HAVING COUNT_BIG(*)>1;

-- 19. Sales using unknown dimension members.
SELECT
 SUM(CASE WHEN customer_key=0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS unknown_customer_rows,
 SUM(CASE WHEN product_key=0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS unknown_product_rows,
 SUM(CASE WHEN store_key=0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS unknown_store_rows
FROM dw.fact_sales;

-- 20. Daily data-quality failures.
SELECT CAST(checked_at_utc AS date) AS check_date,COUNT_BIG(*) AS failed_checks
FROM audit.reconciliation_result WHERE status='FAIL'
GROUP BY CAST(checked_at_utc AS date) ORDER BY check_date;
```

### Optional reference answer for `sql/sqlserver/analytics/kpi_validation_queries.sql`

Attempt the file construction first. This reference is learning material, not evidence that you created or ran the file.

**Language:** SQL  
**Exact file:** `sql/sqlserver/analytics/kpi_validation_queries.sql`  
**Purpose:** database or lakehouse definitions and queries.  
**Inputs:** The requirements, configuration, source data, or upstream objects described in Phase 17.  
**Expected outputs:** The file's declared objects, logs, tables, checks, or documentation when the user later runs or reads it.

```sql
-- Dialect: SQL Server / T-SQL
-- Independent SQL checks used to validate Power BI measures.
USE NorthstarRetail_DW;
GO
SELECT SUM(net_sales_amount) AS Total_Revenue FROM dw.fact_sales;
SELECT SUM(gross_profit_amount) AS Gross_Profit FROM dw.fact_sales;
SELECT SUM(gross_profit_amount)/NULLIF(SUM(net_sales_amount),0) AS Gross_Margin_Ratio FROM dw.fact_sales;
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) AS Orders FROM dw.fact_sales;
SELECT SUM(quantity) AS Units_Sold FROM dw.fact_sales;
SELECT SUM(net_sales_amount)/NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT order_id),0) AS Average_Order_Value FROM dw.fact_sales;
SELECT 1.0*SUM(return_quantity)/NULLIF((SELECT SUM(quantity) FROM dw.fact_sales),0) AS Return_Rate FROM dw.fact_returns;
SELECT 1.0*SUM(CASE WHEN on_time_flag=1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/NULLIF(COUNT_BIG(*),0) AS On_Time_Delivery_Rate FROM dw.fact_shipments;
SELECT SUM(spend_amount) AS Marketing_Spend FROM dw.fact_marketing_spend;
SELECT 1.0*SUM(CASE WHEN converted_flag=1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/NULLIF(SUM(session_count),0) AS Conversion_Rate FROM dw.fact_web_sessions;
SELECT SUM(quantity_on_hand) AS Inventory_On_Hand, SUM(CASE WHEN stockout_risk_flag=1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS Stockout_Risk_Count FROM dw.fact_inventory_snapshot;
-- Promotion Gross Profit by promotion. This is contribution, not causal incremental lift.
SELECT
    p.promotion_code,
    p.promotion_name,
    SUM(s.gross_profit_amount) AS Promotion_Gross_Profit
FROM dw.fact_sales AS s
INNER JOIN dw.dim_promotion AS p
    ON p.promotion_key = s.promotion_key
WHERE s.promotion_key <> 0
GROUP BY p.promotion_code, p.promotion_name
ORDER BY Promotion_Gross_Profit DESC;
```

<a id="report-page-executive-overview"></a>
### Report page 1 — `Executive Overview`

**Audience and decision:** This page groups the measures and dimensions needed for a reader to answer the page's named business question without mixing incompatible grains.  
**Required fields/measures:**

- `Total Revenue`
- `Gross Profit`
- `Gross Margin %`
- `Orders`
- `Average Order Value`
- `On-Time Delivery %`

**Page-size rule:** Use the documented canvas and keep consistent margins, alignment, reading order, and title placement.  
**Slicer rule:** Date plus only the relevant dimensions. A slicer must not imply that it filters a measure when no valid relationship exists.  
**Validation rule:** Every KPI and chart total is compared to a table visual and an independently filtered SQL query.  
**Misleading alternatives to avoid:** Truncated axes without a reason, pie charts with too many categories, averaging row-level percentages, dual axes that suggest false correlation, totals across snapshot dates, and colors used as the only status signal.

**Validation rule:** Every KPI and chart total is compared to a table visual and an independently filtered SQL query.  
**Misleading alternatives to avoid:** Truncated axes without a reason, pie charts with too many categories, averaging row-level percentages, dual axes that suggest false correlation, totals across snapshot dates, and colors used as the only status signal.

## Lesson 17.5 — Verify, troubleshoot, commit, teach back, and stop safely

## What your screen should look like before starting

The Phase 17 outputs are visible, all runs are finished, open files are saved, and you can state the active branch and execution context. Any error you encountered has a recorded message and has not been hidden by deleting evidence.

## Design decision — Verification before automation

**Question:**  
Should the phase prioritize a visible manual verification or jump directly to automation?

**Options considered:**

- Manual verification first, then automation.
- Automation without a known-good baseline.
- Manual operation forever.

**Beginner path selected:**  
Establish one verified manual baseline and then automate repeatable checks.

**Why this path was selected:**  
A known-good example makes failures interpretable and prevents automation from hiding a wrong assumption.

**Tradeoff:**  
The first run takes longer.

**What a company might do instead:**  
Teams often pair infrastructure as code and automated tests with controlled bootstrap and acceptance procedures.

**How to explain this in an interview:**  
I established a verified baseline, then encoded the same contract in tests and orchestration so automation preserved meaning rather than just speed.




## If you see Result A

Each page answers its audience question and visible values match the validated semantic model. Record the exact result, perform the named independent verification, and continue only when the gate is satisfied.

## If you see Result B

A visual is blank, misleading, differently filtered, over-aggregated, or inconsistent with SQL/DAX validation. Treat this as information, not permission to delete or overwrite. Follow the branch-specific diagnostic in the current action, preserve evidence, and continue only after the state is understood.

## If you see an error

Read the first meaningful error line, redact secrets, and verify the application, path, branch, server/database, catalog/schema, batch ID, parameters, version/tier, and object name. Run the smallest observational check first. Do not reset Git history, drop data, disable a rule, force-push, or replace the target merely to make the error disappear.


## Phase-specific verification gate

- [ ] Required files/objects exist in the exact location.
- [ ] I personally created or configured them.
- [ ] I ran the phase commands in the documented context.
- [ ] I inspected the output rather than relying on a green icon alone.
- [ ] Counts, keys, relationships, measures, checksums, statuses, or settings meet the declared contract.
- [ ] Same-batch/rerun behavior is known where applicable.
- [ ] A controlled failure or realistic alternate-result branch was tested safely where applicable.
- [ ] No password, token, or secret appears in tracked files, screenshots, notebook output, terminal history pasted into documentation, or staged changes.
- [ ] Actual verified result: `[ENTER VERIFIED RESULT]`.

## Screenshot checkpoint

**Window/panel:** Show each verified report page under a documented slicer state.  
**Sensitive information to hide:** Passwords, tokens, connection strings, email addresses, cloud account IDs, unnecessary Windows profile details, and any secret revealed by an error.

Do not use `git add .` until you understand that it stages every matching change under the current directory, including files you did not intend. Prefer targeted staging after inspecting status and diffs.

### Interpret `git status --short`

- `??` means untracked: Git sees a new path but it is not staged.
- ` M` means modified in the working tree but not staged.
- `M ` means the staged version differs from the last commit.
- `MM` means a staged version exists and the file has additional unstaged edits.
- `A ` means staged as a new file.
- `D` means deletion; stop and investigate unless deletion is deliberate.
- `R` means rename; inspect both old and new paths.
- A blank result means the working tree is clean. It does not prove database, Databricks, or Power BI work occurred.

### Verify on GitHub

1. CLICK: Open the repository page in a browser.
2. CLICK: Open the branch selector above the file list.

### Push-rejected recovery

If Git says the remote contains work you do not have, do not use `--force`. Run `git fetch origin`, inspect `git log --oneline --graph --decorate --all -20`, then rebase or merge only after understanding the divergence. Resolve conflicts one file at a time, run tests again, and push normally. A rejection protects remote work; it is not permission to overwrite it.

## Mini quiz

1. Multiple choice: Why does Phase 17 occur at this point in the source-to-consumption chain? A) Because menu order is arbitrary. B) Because its verified upstream input now exists. C) Because later phases do not depend on it. D) To create portfolio screenshots before validation.
2. True or false: A command that displays no error is automatically verified even when it ran in the wrong folder, database, catalog, schema, branch, or filter context.
3. Fill in the blank: The statement that defines what one row represents is the table or entity ________.
4. What command would you use first to confirm the PowerShell current folder before a repository command?
5. Troubleshooting: Your output differs from the example. What should you check before deleting, overwriting, resetting, force-pushing, or weakening a test?
6. Design choice: Explain one tradeoff of Track A and one production alternative.
7. Code reading: Why are input, accepted, rejected, and deduplicated counts recorded separately?
8. Ownership: Which status may you select only after personally performing and inspecting the verification?

---

## Mini quiz answer key and explanations

**1. B.** This phase is ordered after its prerequisites so its output has a trustworthy input. A is wrong because order is intentional; C is wrong because later phases depend on the handoff; D is wrong because screenshots follow verification.

**2. False.** Lack of an error proves only that the application accepted something; context and independent verification still matter.

**3. Grain.** Grain is the precise meaning of one row. A key identifies a row, but it does not by itself state the row’s business meaning.

**4. `Get-Location`.** It shows the shell’s current folder. `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` separately verifies the repository root when inside a clone.

**5.** Check application, folder/path, branch, server/database, catalog/schema, batch ID, parameters, source/target grain, filter context, version/tier differences, and the first meaningful error. Destructive changes are not a diagnostic step.

**6.** Track A has manual upload/download boundaries and batch latency. A production alternative is routable private connectivity with cloud object storage/managed warehouse, identities, and automated orchestration.

**7.** Separate counts make every row outcome explainable. A single final count can hide silent drops, duplicates, or records that moved to quarantine.

**8. `Verified by me` / `VERIFIED BY USER`.** `PLANNED`, `CREATED BY USER`, and `RUN BY USER` describe earlier states; only inspected evidence supports verification.

# Phase 18 — Secure secrets, control cost, and review operational settings

[Back to the master table of contents](#master-table-of-contents)

**Track:** Track A required  
**Status when first opened:** `PLANNED`  
**Completion rule:** The phase is not complete because its instructions exist. Mark it `VERIFIED BY USER` only after you perform the work, inspect the output, and save evidence.

## Why this phase happens now

**Earlier work this phase depends on:** A repository with secrets excluded and cost-sensitive settings recorded.  
**What would go wrong if it happened earlier:** You would create objects without a verified requirement, valid upstream input, protected repository state, or known execution environment.  
**Later work that depends on it:** Phase 19 automates local, infrastructure-free quality checks on every change.  
**Decision being made:** Choose and verify the simplest local-first method that teaches the professional concept without pretending that local services are publicly reachable.  
**Alternatives:** A company could use managed cloud databases, infrastructure as code, service principals, direct JDBC publication, deployment bundles, or streaming. Those options are discussed as tradeoffs, not substituted silently.  
**Beginner path selected:** Track A: local SQL Server and PostgreSQL, Python batch extracts, manual governed upload to Databricks, Delta Bronze/Silver/Gold, manual verified export, local SQL Server warehouse, and Power BI Import.  
**Reason for the order:** Requirements become source decisions; sources become generated data; source data becomes extraction batches; batches become Bronze; Bronze becomes Silver; Silver becomes Gold; Gold becomes warehouse and Power BI input.

- **Terminal prompt:** It should end in the expected repository path or another explicitly named folder.
- **Previous verification:** Phase 17 must be verified when this phase has a prerequisite.

## Three-level explanation of the phase

### Level 1 — Child-simple explanation

Imagine building a store from labeled boxes. This phase handles one box, checks that the label is correct, and makes sure the next box receives the right thing. You do not pour all boxes together and hope the result is understandable.

### Level 2 — Northstar Retail project explanation

Phase 18 creates the specific Northstar Retail files, database objects, transformations, tests, model objects, or evidence described in the lessons. Every output keeps a visible connection to its source and batch so you can trace an order, customer, product, campaign, return, shipment, or inventory record.

### Level 3 — Professional explanation

This phase establishes a controlled boundary in an end-to-end batch platform. It defines contracts, execution context, idempotency behavior, quality expectations, evidence, and handoff artifacts so the downstream layer can be reproduced and reviewed independently.

## What your screen should look like before starting

## Retained phase lesson, exercises, rules, and expected results

> **Track:** Track A required  
> **Ownership status at start:** Workbook instructions exist; your execution is not yet verified.  
> **Evidence rule:** Replace placeholders only after the verification steps pass.

## 1. What you are building

A no-secrets configuration pattern, `.gitignore`, `.env.example`, Databricks secret guidance, least-privilege SQL roles, read-only analyst access, development/production separation, log-redaction rules, synthetic-data classification, secret-scanning checklist, and cost shutdown checklist.

## 2. Why it matters

A portfolio project can still leak real passwords, tokens, machine details, or cloud spend. Security and cost controls are design requirements, not cleanup after the pipeline works.

## 3. Words to know

| Term | Plain-language definition |
| --- | --- |
| Secret | A password, token, private key, connection string, or credential that grants access. |
| Environment variable | A process-level name/value used to supply configuration without writing a secret into code. |
| `.env` file | A local text file commonly used for environment variables; it must be ignored by Git. |
| Least privilege | Grant only the minimum access needed for a task. |
| Read-only role | A database permission group that can query approved objects but cannot change them. |
| Secret scope | A Databricks-managed namespace for secret values, subject to workspace capabilities and permissions. |
| PII | Personally identifiable information; synthetic names/emails should still be handled as if their shape were sensitive. |
| Redaction | Removing or masking sensitive content from logs, screenshots, and error messages. |
| Configuration environment | A named set of settings such as development or production. |
| Compute auto-termination | Stopping idle cloud compute automatically to reduce cost. |
| Secret scanning | Searching repository content for credential-like patterns before commit/push. |

## 4. What must already be completed

Local source/warehouse connections work through environment variables, the repository has no real credentials, and you can identify every service/database account used by the project.

## 5. Applications to open

| Application | How to open it | Why it is open |
| --- | --- | --- |
| VS Code | Open `.gitignore`, `.env.example`, config files, and security guide. | Review what is safe to publish. |
| Windows PowerShell | Open in repository root. | Create local `.env`, inspect tracked files, and run scans. |
| SSMS and pgAdmin | Connect with an administrative learning account only while creating read roles. | Grant and test minimum database permissions. |
| Databricks workspace settings/secret interface | Open only if available on your workspace tier. | Store cloud-connected credentials without notebooks or Git. |
| GitHub repository Settings/Security | Open the repository in a browser. | Review visibility, Actions, and secret alerts if available. |

## 6. Exact click-by-click steps

> **Beginner rhythm:** Read the whole step. Confirm the application and location. Perform only that step. Verify the visible result. Record an error before attempting a fix.

## 7. Exact commands, one code block at a time

## 8. Where each command runs

Never infer the execution location from the code language. The command headings above identify the application and folder/database/catalog. Before every PowerShell command, run `Get-Location`; before SQL, verify the selected database; before Spark, print the catalog/schema/batch widgets.

## TEACHING EXAMPLE

The following small example or reference pattern explains the concept before you attempt Northstar-specific work. Read it, then complete **MY TASK** without copying the answer.

### Line-by-line code explanation

| Line or action | Meaning | Why it belongs here |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Copy-Item .env.example .env | Creates a local ignored configuration file and opens it for editing. | Scripts need connection settings, but real values must not be placed in tracked templates. |
| git check-ignore -v .env | Shows why `.env` is ignored and whether any sensitive file is staged/untracked. | Assuming an ignore rule works is not sufficient. |
| python -m scripts.validation.scan_secrets | Scans text files for several common credential patterns. | It catches obvious mistakes before GitHub receives them. |
| IF DATABASE_PRINCIPAL_ID(N'northstar_analyst_reader') IS NULL | Creates a reusable read-only semantic-schema role without embedding credentials. | Power BI/analysts should not need table-write or database-owner permission. |
| -- TODO(USER): create/login names and passwords outside Git. | Creates a group role with read access to current and future digital tables. | The extraction account does not require object ownership or write privileges. |

### Local-first security boundary

Databricks does not receive local SQL Server/PostgreSQL passwords in Track A. Python runs on your Windows machine, extracts to files, and you manually upload a batch. This is less automated but avoids pretending a cloud workspace can safely reach `localhost`.

### Cost truthfulness

Free or trial labels, quotas, and availability can change. Use `the official source register near the beginning of this workbook`, read the current account page before starting compute, record what you actually used, enable auto-stop where available, and never claim “zero cost” unless your own billing confirms it.

## MY TASK

Prove that secrets are excluded from Git, create/test read-only database roles in a safe local environment, document the Track A credential boundary, review logs/screenshots, and complete the security and cost checklists.

## STARTER SKELETON

```text
SECRET/RESOURCE: TODO(USER)
OWNER: TODO(USER)
USED BY: TODO(USER)
STORAGE LOCATION: environment variable / secret manager / identity
MINIMUM PERMISSIONS: TODO(USER)
ROTATION/REVOCATION METHOD: TODO(USER)
LOG REDACTION TEST: TODO(USER)
COST CONTROL: TODO(USER)
EVIDENCE: TODO(USER)
```

**Acceptance criteria:** No real credential or private key is tracked; `.env` ignore behavior is proven; source extraction and analyst access use least privilege; log/screenshots are reviewed; cloud/local cost shutdown steps are recorded; an accidental-secret response procedure is understood.

## HINT 1 — CONCEPT

 Treat every value that grants access as a secret even when the data is synthetic.
## HINT 2 — PSEUDOCODE
 For each component list identity, minimum actions, storage method, test for denied write, and shutdown/rotation path.
## HINT 3 — NEAR-COMPLETE PATTERN
 Use `.env.example` for variable names only, local `.env` for values, database group roles for permissions, and a pre-push scan plus manual staged-diff review.

## 13. Expected files or output

- Verified ignored `.env` file.
- Passing secret-pattern scan and reviewed staged diff.
- Read-only SQL Server and PostgreSQL role test evidence.
- Completed secret inventory and classification notes.
- Cost/shutdown checklist with actual services used.
- Sanitized logs and screenshot review.

## 14. How to verify

- `git ls-files` contains no `.env` or credential file.
- Read-only users can SELECT required objects and cannot modify them.
- Track A Databricks notebooks contain no local database connection string.
- Logs do not print complete connection URLs/passwords/tokens.
- Generated sample data is explicitly labeled synthetic.
- Cloud compute/warehouse auto-stop or manual shutdown is recorded.
- Secret rotation steps are known before any public push.

## 15. Automated tests

- Ignore-rule test with `git check-ignore`.
- Secret scanner plus manual staged-diff review.
- Positive SELECT and negative INSERT permission tests.
- Log redaction inspection.
- Repository history spot check before publication.
- Cloud billing/resource inventory check.

## 16. Common errors and exact fixes

| Message/symptom | Likely cause | Exact diagnostic | Safe fix | Verify |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| .env appears in git status | Ignore rule is missing, malformed, or the file was already tracked. | `git check-ignore -v .env` and `git ls-files .env`. | Add rule; if already tracked, use `git rm --cached .env`, rotate any exposed credential, then commit the removal. | .env is ignored/untracked and credential is rotated if needed. |
| Permission denied for SELECT | Role/user mapping, schema USAGE, or object SELECT grant is missing. | Inspect current user and database role membership. | Grant only the missing read permission; do not make the user owner/db_owner. | SELECT succeeds; write still fails. |
| Read-only account can modify data | It inherited a broader role or direct grant. | Inspect role memberships and effective grants. | Revoke broad membership/grants, reconnect, retest. | INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE are denied. |
| Secret scanner reports a template | Example resembles a real token/password pattern. | Open the exact file/line and determine whether it is a real secret. | Rotate if real; replace with unmistakable placeholder if fake; document false positive only when justified. | Scan passes and no usable credential exists. |
| Unexpected cloud charge/quota failure | Compute/storage remained active or free-tier quota was exceeded. | Open provider billing/quota and resource/run history. | Stop/delete unused resources, reduce scale/schedule, and document cost guardrails before retry. | No unintended active resource and next run fits budget/quota. |

For deeper tool-specific diagnosis, use [`the troubleshooting index near the end of this workbook`](#complete-troubleshooting-index).

## 17. Explain it in your own words

1. Why is `.env.example` safe while `.env` is not?
2. Why does a Power BI reader not need warehouse write access?
3. Why are synthetic names still classified as PII-like?
4. What must happen after a real secret is committed?

Write your answers in [`the learning-journal fields in this phase`](the learning-journal fields in this phase). Do not copy the wording above.

## 18. Mini quiz

1. Which command proves the ignore rule that applies to `.env`?
2. Does deleting a committed secret from the latest file make it safe again?
3. Why does Track A not place local database credentials in Databricks?

Record your answers before opening the answer key.

## 19. Screenshot checkpoint

Capture passing scans, ignore proof, role membership and denied-write tests, plus compute auto-stop/resource shutdown settings. Redact usernames, server endpoints, tokens, and billing identifiers.

Save the image under `docs/images/` with a descriptive filename. Check that no credential, token, password, or unnecessary personal account detail is visible.

## 20. Git checkpoint and suggested commit message

Run `git status`, review the Source Control diff in VS Code, stage only the intended files, then commit:

```text
security: add least privilege secret and cost controls
```

Push the feature branch only after tests pass.

#### Folder-creation decision branches

##### If the folder is created

Run `Test-Path -LiteralPath ".\docs" -PathType Container` and require `True`.

##### If PowerShell says the folder already exists

Do not delete or recreate it. Run `Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath ".\docs" -Force`, inspect its existing files, and preserve them. Continue only when the existing folder is the intended path.

##### If the parent path does not exist

Return to the parent-folder tutorial. Create and verify one parent level at a time; do not create the entire future tree in one command.

#### Verify the folder

1. Run `Test-Path ".\docs" -PathType Container`.
2. Require the output `True` before creating a child file.
3. Remember: Git does not track an empty folder by itself; the folder becomes visible in Git history when a tracked file is added.
